findings.title: Shannon c. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My husband and I celebrated our 20-year anniversary at Paradisus Cancun in April 2026, and we had a wonderful experience.

The resort had recently reopened after renovations, and everything felt fresh, modern, and very clean. The beach was beautiful, the pools were relaxing, and the grounds were well maintained.

The highlight of our stay was the staff. Everyone was friendly, helpful, and genuinely seemed to care about making our vacation special. A special thank you to Chris, our Reserve Concierge, who went above and beyond throughout our stay.

If you're considering upgrading to The Reserve Adults Only section, I highly recommend it. The concierge service, exclusive lounge, premium drinks, coffee bar, adults-only dining, and Bali beds were well worth it.

The resort offers several dining options, including steak, seafood, Japanese cuisine, and a buffet. While the food wasn't our favorite part of the trip, breakfast was excellent and there was plenty of variety.

We especially enjoyed the live saxophone music during breakfast, the beautiful beach, and the peaceful gym each morning.

Overall, we had an amazing anniversary trip and would gladly return to Paradisus Cancun in the future.

findings.title: Maream S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: We just came back home yesterday, April 11, 2026 from Paradis in Cancun. We have been chasing that feel from our first time but unfortunately I can't say that we ever got that same experience. The location of the hotel is perfect. The beach is beautiful. The service is excellent. The rooms are OK but there's some bumps in the road. Our first day with our check-in was a little bit complicated and the restaurant that we went to that evening was terrible. It's called Vibre. We went to the Italian restaurant, Capella, and because we had the reserve option. We also tried. Both of these restaurants were excellent. The bartenders outside were excellent Raymundo by aqua was wonderful. The bartenders at the adult side pool were also great. The service by the pools is lackluster in the general areas. In the past, we used to be able to order snacks and they would be delivered to us in the general area but now that option is only available at the reserve. If you do not have children, I highly recommend paying extra and staying on the adults only side. I don't know if we will visit Paradis again. It's not what it used to be many years ago.

findings.title: Dimitri S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: It's Friday April 10th 2026, 12:30 am and me and my family are trying to have some rest on our vacation and  the crowd using all the advantages of all inclusive bars screaming its lungs out to the abnormally loud dancing music . This is not Paradisus's  hotel only disadvantage , there are more than in the past . And it's our third and last time. Good bye once a great place!

findings.title: Teal K. (3/5)
findings.snippet: There are a few reasons I would not come back here. Some of the staff (poolside bartender and housekeeper) were extremely rude, with housekeeping there was no consistency so we never knew when to be out of the room. One day they came at 2:30, the next day they came at 5pm and the last day they came at 11am. It was all over the place and when I asked her to please clean the floors she was very rude to me. The second thing is that unless you are in your room or one of the restaurants there is no ac. It's VERY warm going to and from your room to anywhere else. The water pressure was terrible and the rooms need updating very badly. The vibe is nice and the vines are a nice touch. We also had a huge issue with room service. My grand daughter doesn't eat cheese so we ordered a burger NO CHEESE. The burger happened to be extra charge and when they brought it, it had cheese on it and the fries. We called and at first they said they can bring another burger but not charge us. Well we checked out today and yes, they did charge us! No one touched the burger so we shouldn't have to pay for it. We had a nice time and most of the staff was very nice and helpful. The pools are gorgeous and the beach was beautiful! The food was good, the buffet had lots of options and different stuff every day. We ate at the steak house that wasn't covered in the stay and Roger our waiter was awesome and the food was amazing!

findings.title: Warren T. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall Great experiences 
Very clean resorts & beach
Good service 
Just not enough different type of restaurants like other resorts.
Malva buffet restaurant can offer more different countries' foods.

findings.title: Art Y. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Don't ruin your vacation .. stay away from this hotel or should i say Motel.. upon entrance seems like a legit nice place, but when you check in things changed.. food buffet is horrible always cold and recycled food.. they even use plastic reused cups that guest thow away in the trash, everything is horrible cracked walls old paint Mickey Mouse repairs the service is super slow... anyway you get the point. Nothing to eat for toddlers!

findings.title: Edmondo F. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We made reservations in August 2024 for December 2024 . Upon arrival they only had rooms with 2 double beds ,we explicitly reserved queen bed. Next : refrigerator did not work in the room , small rodent animal on the floor I killed 2, bags of potatoes chip half open in the room ,outlet in the bathroom didn't work . The corridor just outside of the rooms had leftover food on the floor.
They are short of staff all over the resort. We where there last yr and the place was functional really well and the manager would come by every day to see if we need anything but this time I was told that there was a new manager which we never saw. We asked to see the manager but no where to be found. Stay way from this place it is a real rip-off.

findings.title: Hitesh R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: This is our 2nd stay at Paradisus, Cancún. It has gone down hill since Covid. Substandard food at restaurants, out-of-stock menu/towels/pool chairs, concierge scam, poor rooms with even basic electrical not working, and unbearable golf course. They just care about your dollars and not experience. Extremely dissatisfied and would recommend future travelers to explore other resorts.

findings.snippet:

cuando tomen en el   bar de las albercas !! a mi y mi esposo nos echaron algo a la bebida y quedamos inconscientes total mente  después de que mi esposo les dio propina  cargando ese costo al  cuarto  y les dio el numero de cuarto como es posible que mi esposo tomo mas de una bebida pero yo solo me tome una   un mojito  y ya no supe como salimos de la alberca no nos acordamos de NADA  no se cuales eran las intenciones de ellos porque te llevan al cuarto en sillas de ruedas  lo bueno es que no estábamos  solos en el cuarto estaban mis dos hijas cosa que ellos no esperaban

findings.title: Greg J. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Worst luxury hotel I've ever stayed at. First off they say they have golf and it costs almost the same as the real course across the street ibostar. The golf here is like wild fields with flags here and there. What a joke. Second, now this is the main problem. Their DINNER! Eat at the buffet with an hour line and get nasty food handled by kids dropping tongs and putting them back on counter. A Parmesan cheese wheel where you put your hand in with a spoon and scoop out your own Parmesan. And then they leave the spoon in it. Terrible buffet. But here's the worst part. All the other places are reservations only no exceptions. So if your out on an excursion or not in cell range. Well you get the buffet. I hate this place will never stay here again. I'm excited to go home in 2 days. 0 stars don't recommend

findings.title: Beatriz D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I'm staying at this hotel! And all those who come here to read, they have to know that they have to COME!! It's AMAZING, it's my second time here! My favorite restaurant is Sante, the super fresh food and the attention of Diego and all the guys was first class!

findings.title: Wayne H. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We've been members of Club Meliá for over a decade and this is our home property. We usually end up going to other resorts in other countries but recently decided to take a long weekend trip to the Cancun property. The staff are still very friendly, but the property is in serious need of a refresh, or at least some basic repairs.

Walking through the property, there are cones and towels on the floor where there is water leaking. We're not talking about one or two, but a few in each pyramid. Many of the public restrooms in the resort are of questionable cleanliness and many have no air conditioning.

Our room was also very tired and in need of a refresh. Cabinet doors and drawers were misaligned and would not shut all the way. There was evidence of a massive water leak above the bed that looked like an amateur repaired and patched it (see photos). The bathroom mirror had black spots on it where the glass had chipped away and a lot of the grout was chipped or missing or repaired with a totally different color.

When we first stayed here, the rooms were pristine and modern. I would venture to guess that other than minimal maintenance, these rooms haven't seen a single overhaul or renovation since we bought the timeshare a decade ago.

We had very good meals at Agua Marina and Santé for dinner, but food elsewhere on the property was pretty disappointing. Cocktails were also very inconsistent with one bartender using a 1/2 oz of vermouth in an extra dry martini while another was using barely a splash. One bartender asked us what was in a Negroni lol...

Overall, the property is being milked for every dollar with no visible signs of any improvements. Once our timeshare is up, we definitely will not be renewing it.

findings.title: Doris K. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I just got back. Stayed four nights. 

I do highly recommend this resort. 

Everything is in one place. They offer Yoga, silent disco, painting classes, water aerobics, which I completely enjoyed, coffee bar, pool, games, different spots to chill so you aren't in your room, buffet, and a few different restaurants. The pool area is massive, and the swim up bars are beautiful.

Downfalls, there's no air conditioning in the main part of the hotel. The spa...  absolutely one of the worst pedicures I've ever received in my life however, the girl that did it was very nice. The front desk girl wasn't. 

The restaurants are not worth it at all. They try to up charge you on certain things but it's an all inclusive resort so I didn't feel like that was necessary, the food... you wait for an hour and a half and we weren't impressed by anything provided at the restaurants from the Service to the food.... when realistically the buffet is much better.

The buffet, the maid service, the pools, huts, areas to lay out, access to the beach, service at the pool, not to mention hospitality of the workers, and the people...absolutely outstanding, and that's why I do recommend this resort, family friendly. 

Everything was clean even tho parts were completely under maintenance like leaks in the roof buckets on the floor collecting water. Some areas did smell like mold and if I was staying in those areas, I would've asked to move.

I did have a wonderful time and was impressed by all the resort offered. You do get what you paid for here and I felt like it was worth it. I did ask for two beds as I was staying with family. I was given a king bed. I had to go down and ask for two beds... twice and then I was accommodated.

Also, if you book outside the hotel, they don't offer pick up from the airport or take you to the airport on their service. 

Please use Uber. We made the mistake and paid $100 to get to the hotel. When really the Uber was $20 as we did that on the way back to the airport. Felt like an idiot, but you live and learn.

Very clean. Food was fresh. Drinks were good. Pool was clean. Hotel was clean.

findings.title: Ashley S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: A long over due review but my husband and I spent a week here for our honeymoon. We were so pleased with the services and every single encounter we had during our stay. We are excited to return anytime! Special thanks to Luis and Sofonia at the pool bar for always whipping up something special for our occasion, they went above and beyond for us!  We also are so pleased with our concierge Irán who planned a special surprise for us on our final night!

findings.title: Minh N. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing resort with a very green decoration. Fantastic food and drink. I had an amazing time.

findings.title: Niño B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
This was our first all-inclusive experience, and we had an amazing time!

I spent a week in Cancun celebrating my birthday with my family, staying at this beautiful all-inclusive hotel. The hotel's design is stunning, both inside and out, with a theme that highlights Mexico's natural elements. The use of natural light and lush indoor plants really stood out and created a memorable ambiance that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Our room was fairly standard, but it included a beachfront view that we paid a bit extra to upgrade. We mostly appreciated the room service included in our package--the staff cleaned the room daily, restocked the fridge with water, and made sure we had fresh towels.

The activities were the highlight of this trip and made it feel like a true vacation. I loved soaking up the sun and spending time in the pool. The hotel offers a variety of activities, with daily events that were a nice touch and gave us something to look forward to each day.

Dining at the different restaurants was another aspect I enjoyed, even though not all of them hit the mark. Experiencing the variety of flavors they offered was fun, and my favorite spots were Blue Agave and Cielo.

Overall, this was a fantastic first all-inclusive experience with my family. The beauty of the space, the wonderful service, and the engaging activities truly made the experience special. Paradisus really did feel like a paradise!

findings.title: Savi D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Hey Yelp Fam!

I'm back with another review, and this time we've gone international! A few weeks ago, I ventured to Cancun, Mexico, and stayed at the All-Inclusive Paradisus Cancun Resort. I'll try to give you as much info as I can about my 4-day, 3-night stay, but if you decide to stop reading at any time, just know this: **I HAD AN AMAZING TIME** and I can't wait to go back!

As we left the airport with our private driver and drove through the city, I was filled with excitement. The beautiful palm trees, the water, the people, and the vibrant culture all made me eager to start my vacation. Arriving at the resort was just as thrilling. Everyone who enters the resort must be checked in by security, and once you arrive at the front, resort staff members greet you, collect your bags, and walk you to check-in. We landed around 10:30 AM, got to the resort a little after 11 AM, and our room was ready by 12 PM. While waiting, we checked in and received our wristbands. FYI, we stayed on "The Reserve Side," which is adults-only. With about 40 minutes to kill before our room was ready, we decided to check out one of the all-you-can-eat buffets for a quick bite. This was the first and only time we ate on that side of the resort because we took full advantage of the restaurants available to us on the adults-only side.

Now, let me tell you about the room. We were on the second floor, which made it easy to access snacks, food, the beach, and other amenities. The rooms are very spacious; I went with two other family members, and we opted for the master suite, which came with two bedrooms and two bathrooms. The bathrooms have nice glass walk-in showers, with a private toilet area behind a door, and the room includes a minibar fully stocked with drinks and snacks. Our room didn't overlook the ocean, but that was fine--it was an easy walk around the corner and down the stairs.

Navigating the hotel was like a maze, but I finally got the hang of it the day before we left. The beautiful blue water, the Bali beds, the food, the staff, the views, the activities, the spa--**EVERYTHING WAS AMAZING.** I won't go into too much detail because I don't want to bore you, but I do want to share the places we ate at: 

Malva** (buffet on day one)
Lemon Fish** (must have a reservation)
Sal** (must have a reservation)
Sante** (my favorite)
Aquafish** (I didn't eat anything here; but you can try it out)

One of my favorite things was going to the snack bar in "The Reserve," which is the adults-only section that had snacks every day. I went there regularly for the cute and tasty desserts that weren't too sweet (I loved it!).

As for activities, we did the "Sound Healing" session--OMG, it was worth it. Lying by the beach with my eyes closed while the instructor using crystal singing bowls that made different frequency noises as she recited mantras was a freeing experience. I'm not one to opt for things like this, but I'm glad I tried something different. One day, my family did a morning strength session, but I couldn't make that... lol, I was sleeping. We also did hydrotherapy, which I highly recommend. You start by sitting in the sauna, then move to the steam room (which was intense, lol). Then, you walk on warm rocks that spray water on your ankles, plunge into ice-cold water, and finish in a warm jet pool with waterfalls. You're there for about 45 minutes--just enjoy it!

The staff was amazing--very friendly and attentive. Our concierge was Violette--she is OUTSTANDING! I'm sure I didn't cover everything, but I'll make it up with photos. Please enjoy the pictures!

findings.title: Jorge P. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Including this Hotel " Paradisus Cancun" I've been to other 3 paradisus properties and this one has been the worst yet. ill give this hotel 3 stars because its lacking a lot of what an all inclusive resort should be. 
the Property its over 30 years old and you can see all over how its just falling apart. while they seem to be slowly sort of fixing some things the major places like the main pool needs some major renovation as well as the rooms. Never got to use the Balcony Jacuzzi because it did not look enticing at all, old and dirty seems to be the norm throughout. The food was ok at best. just like many places as soon as you walk in they start selling you extremely overpriced things left and right. and if you have resort credit just disregard it cuz it's worthless. Over all unfortunately I cannot recommend this hotel because with a few hundred more for the week im sure you can stay at a much much better and newer hotel. This place its just falling apart.

findings.title: Aadi G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This resort is completely sh** I would not recommend this to anybody visiting this area,  I would for sure recommend staying at Hilton mar caribe the experience is much better there. From the checking in process to the service, it just absolutely sucks. the service is really bad and the checking in process took almost 2 hours for just a simple check in. The property may be nice from the images and the reviews on google but do not trust it the room and very old and basically falling apart if I got paid to stay at this resort again I would decline the offer, 0/10 do not recommend

findings.title: C T. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Horrible resort! This is my first time staying here. First day checked in, no power for the whole night. No air conditioning and no water, can't shower. We were suffering in the room. The front desk people were not very helpful at all. Do not do anything trying to help. Horrible service, and food is really bad too! We came to Cancun few times and stayed at Hyatt Ziva. It's so so much better there. Food and service were a lot better at Hyatt for sure! Don't stay here even if it's cheaper. Not worth it at all! Your vacation will become nightmare

findings.title: Joe K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The hotel and the facilities were very clean, modern, and easy to navigate. Only issue was that the entire hotel was not cooled down. 
The service was excellent with room service, restaurants, bars, and the spa. 
Pleasantly surprised with all the restaurants. Food was very good and the individual restaurants were all distinctly different from other restaurants. 
The Malva restaurant has the buffet had the combination of all restaurants frim the resort. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner was great at the buffet. 
The beach area had good amount of lounge chairs and cabanas and a picture perfect scene with that warm Caribbean water. Only disappointment was the sargassum. 
First time at an all inclusive resort and was a great value. 
The excursions is a must:
Xcaret, Chichén Itzá, and Isla Mujeres.

findings.title: Felix A. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
stay away from this HOTEL! a horrible experience that ended with our baby in the ER due to poor food control. When you step into the room you will be wowed by the type of room and the horrible conditions of a so called 5 star hotel !
do your review and make sure if you want to stay within the amount spend for x amount of nights you find another as you will be terribly disappointed by it all .

findings.title: Alan B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
From check in to check out, the staff and experience were wonderful. The facilities are in great shape and the choice of restaurants is very good. The only thing I would have liked is for the A/C in my room to get colder.

We had a conference there, as well, and the room and A/V were top notch. 

I was very impressed that at every restaurant they asked about food allergies and restrictions when you check in or ask to be seated. At the buffet, someone walked it with me, showing me which items had no gluten. There are symbols on many of the items (although I didn't see a legend to know which is which - some were more obvious that others).

They made me gluten free pancakes the first morning, which was nice, but they were small and had that gummy texture which is common. There was a section of the buffet with gluten free bread (which was a little crusty) and a muffin (I couldn't really tell what kind, but it was fine for breakfast).

At the fish restaurant, they brought me gluten free soy sauce for my sushi and there were gluten free dessert options. The staff is very attentive to our GF needs, better than most restaurants in the US.

findings.title: Tim L. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Spent a week at the Paradisus Cancún - booked the all inclusive stay, flight, and shuttle transfers through the Melia website. 

THE GOOD:
 The beach is beautiful.  Soft, white sand, clear water, not too crowded. 
The common areas are pretty well maintained - the lobby area is sun drenched and covered in plants which gives a welcoming and tropical feel. 
The service is mostly good - hit or miss depending on which department/restaurant, but overall they're friendly. 
The food was above average for an all inclusive. We had a couple of stellar days at Malva the buffet. We had an excellent dinner at Agua Marina the seafood place. We had several great experiences at the taqueria Blue Agave, and we really enjoyed Cielo, the more traditional Mexican spot. 

THE BAD:
Check in took nearly an hour. Any time I had a question for guest services it took a minimum of 30 minutes. This place still after 30+ years really has not figured out how to streamline this process and it's very frustrating. 
The hotel is old and it shows - so they're constantly trying to upcharge you for something. Our first room was AWFUL. The door to the balcony was literally falling off. Our shower flooded the entire bathroom. None of the light switches worked. The closet doors were broken and wouldn't close. I've honestly stayed in nicer Holiday Inns or Days Inn... no joke. We ended up upgrading to Nitke, which was worth it because the rooms have recently been renovated and are much nicer. 
There are not enough chairs at the pools or the beach. No joke people start getting up at 6am to reserve chairs. If you're not down there by 8am you won't be finding a chair. 
They also run out of towels by 4 or 5pm. I've never stayed at a hotel that runs out of towels literally every day and can't figure out a way to replenish them... it's mind boggling. 
The steakhouse Sal was terrible. I mean terrible. Just don't go (and if you're not in a Nitke room you have to pay anyway). The ceviche restaurant Lemon Fish was bad too. 
The spa is just ok... a bit expensive... the facilities are showing their age a bit. 

OVERALL we had a decent experience - we could ignore most of the bad stuff and just relax on the beach most days. If you get a really good deal I'd recommend it, but there are much nicer properties in Cancun at the same price point or just a bit more expensive that are superior.

findings.title: Ben W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall, a good value but noticeable weaknesses.

Positives:  Wonderful location, amazing pools (plural) that allowed for kids but also lap swimming for adults.  Nice rooms.  Very attentive, motivated staff in every area.  Great access to warm ocean swimming.  Good to decompress.  The main buffet was very good with fresh choices and a good fresh salad bar.

Negatives:  

Checking in was slow and backed up.  When you are arriving tired this is dissapointing.  We checked the box for adjacent rooms (though it was not guaranteed) but they put us in different buildings.

The restaurants were not up to par and would never survive in the private sector.  Portions were small and limited options and desserts were average, but better in the main buffet.  Very difficult for vegans in the restaurants (though okay at the buffet).  The Japanese restaurant was in a beautiful setting but service was slow and poor.  It seemed to be way understaffed.  The food was okay but if you wanted vegan sushi it was only a cucumber roll.  The health oriented restaurant, Flora, had one vegan "entree" but it was just broccoli.  It would have been a good side dish.  The restaurants all were nice to be in with good service (except the Japanese, which was terrible) but the dishes were consistently disappointing.

Finally, the brewed coffee in the buffet was pretty good, but other options were poor.  They have a nespresso bar outside the restaurant but the wait is long and if you don't like Nespresso there were no other options.  Get a real barista and espresso bar.

findings.title: amanda c. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The room was outdated and musty. Strong smell of sewage/ poo/something bad, on the third floor. Party music all night long on most nights so bring a sound machine. Restaurants had just ok food, nothing authentic or anything to write home about except for the short rib at the capella restaurant. No hot tubs. 3 stars bc most of the staff was awesome, room service food awful but staff again awesome. The place looks beautiful but needs serious updates. Pools close at 7?!?!? So early, we like a night swim opportunity! Bed was firm but comfortable. Definitely not worth the money. Will take my travel agents advice and stay elsewhere next time.

findings.title: Nikki T. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I loved Paradisus and recommend it to anyone who asks. The staff is friendly, the food is good, and the resort itself is beautiful. I've been twice and each time it's always been a great experience!

findings.title: Alex P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Horrible this hotel is marketed as family friendly, but almost half the restaurants are adults only and so are many of the pools. I am beyond disappointed of this. Plus me and my friends who are 16 tried to watch our parents sing karaoke and being completely respectful watching them and we got kicked out since we weren't allowed and it was 18+ but we were just doing nothing wrong and trying to watch our parents. Also if you're looking for a nice cool resort, this one isn't the option it is very hot and humid all throughout and the air-conditioning barely works in the rooms. Another factor is the room was flooded when we first got here and had a  2 hour wait to get a new room even though this  place is huge and I'm sure we could've gotten a hotel in no time if they were on their game. We also asked for two full beds in the received a king, if you're looking for comfort, this hotel is definitely not the option. The beds are rock solid and the pillows give me no comfort. The blankets are thin and crusty. The bathroom has barely any lighting, and it is very dark in there in the balcony door has gotten stuck more than half the time. There are also nightlights that don't turn off very important if you're looking for a dark space. I'm beyond disappointed please don't stay here!!!!!

findings.title: Dylan P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: 0 stars. Not family friendly at all. Bad service and food. Can't have dinners as a group with kids under 18 and can't do family activities such as karaoke at night got kicked out for " Being under 18" DO NOT COME HERE. leaving kids outside cause we are not allowed to do the karaoke.

findings.title: Viky S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
PLEASE READ BEFORE BOOKING 
First I want to start off by saying ITS A SCAM! NOT EVERYTHING IS INCLUSIVE!!! Biggest waist of money. I went there for my honeymoon, check in was supposed to be at 3:00pm only got into the room at 7:00pm. They gave us the wrong room. We paid extra for a beach view and got a bush view. As soon as we walk in it smells like throw up. The shower was absolutely disgusting there were bugs all over the bed. We went to the front desk they said they can't do anything about it. We stood there arguing for 2 hours and finally agreed on giving us our room that we actually booked but made us pay an extra $900 because it's in adults only section.
Food is absolutely disgusting they don't change their menus so it gets annoying eating the same thing everyday also on the menu you have to pay for most of the food it's not inclusive. They have parties all night long blasting music and you can't do anything about it. The front desk people are extremely rude! There is absolutely nothing to do in this hotel I recommend getting a better hotel. I regret going there so bad! DON'T WAIST YOUR MONEY TRUST ME!!!!!!!!!

findings.title: Donna W. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Kick's Sport Bar is the BEST!!! We loved Jesus Gorociea (sp?) - he was running the entire bar, mainly by himself. No matter how busy it got and how long the line was, he waited on us (we were sitting at the bar). My husband & I were there from March 6-9. He ws always very friendly and patient. He did have a couple of other helpers from time to time; Luis & Emmanuel - they were good too.
My brother & his wife will be staying at the resort in April - I told them they must go see Jesus!

findings.title: Sylvia C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We just returned from this wonderful resort after spending five days there! It was absolutely fabulous! We stayed in the reserve area, which is for adults only and it's more upscale than the rest of the resort. We had a personal concierge, and his name was Roberto! Roberto deserves a raise because he was freaking awesome! We returned to our room only to find a freshly drawn bubble bath with rose petals waiting for us!  Our bed was decorated with rose petals too! He said after a day on the ocean yacht that we had chartered with some friends, a bubble bath seemed like the logical thing to do! We loved it! The food was pretty good, but you know food at an all-inclusive is not going to be spectacular! We did eat at Fuego and we decided to upgrade for the lobster and steak dinner. It was $75 and it was sooo worth it! We are so glad that we did because the lobster was 9 ounces, and it was fabulous! But let me tell you about that filet mignon because it was outstanding! Perfectly seasoned, and just melted in your mouth! We were there for my girlfriends 50th birthday party and about 42 of us met up down there and had a great time! I can't say one bad thing about it! The grounds were meticulously obtained! Can't wait to return!

findings.title: Maddii B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Absolutely loved loved loved staying at this resort! The dining options were amazing and even better ambiance's. I had the whole fried snapper and Mussles almost everyday. They had such fun events every night and all of the staff were always extremely helpful!

findings.title: Stephanie C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Our family Loves  this hotel!  We have been going for years and bought the Circle timeshare. One of the reasons we love this place is because of Elliott Gonzalez. He was the Pool Conceirge  for the guests and he was AWESOME!! He IS one of the reasons we keep coming back because he always took care of our family. I heard that he was let go because they didn't need him. Are you kidding me? You NEED him. He was friendly, always available, ran circles around the others. Our family is very, very disappointed with this decision. I hope management rehires him because they will be missing one of the best workers they had.

findings.title: Larry E. (1/5)
findings.snippet: The food is substandard.  I got sick the first night from food poisoning.    Can't leave rare beef under a heat lamp that is not warm enough.    Never enough chairs.   Racism is subtle from room selection to where they try to sit you if you are african american.  I've seen people who came in after me be served first.  A lot of times my food arrived cold while the waiter was standing around talking.   My girlfriend ordered fish and it was undercooked.  They need to change the oil in their deep fryers more often and have the temperature increased on some of the fryers.   Some fried food tasted like other food and because the oil was not hot enough it was soggy and greasy

findings.title: Yuwa A. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Summer time last year my family and I decided to go to Mexico with friends and family and we picked Paradisus de la Carmen. The suite we stayed in was big and I really like it. My kids and I slept separately as the sofa turns into a bed. The one thing I did notice was the old sofa and I wish they would get rid of that. 

Food was 24/7 but my kids loved the fact the each morning a stag came to replenish all their Candy and cookies I mean the kids were in candy heaven. It's a big resort so you really have to walk around a lot. At some point we left the kids with the child care at the resort and they did a wonderful job.

The resort also has a private section for adults which I thought was cool. Also some of the hotel rooms had private pools attached to them which was also very nice. I'm going to have to say that the water park for kids was definitely my highlight. I mean this place was just amazing. 

I would definitely come back!!!

findings.title: Matthew W. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Just got back from a 6 day stay.  Please be patient as I have a lot to share.

Check in for us was not smooth.  We made a few requests when we booked that were completely ignored.  We were told they could not accommodate what was asked for at this time.  After an hour and a half of going around and around, amazingly they were able to meet our requests.  Whole check in thing is kind of a joke.

That being said the room was nice.  Big enough for myself, my wife, and two teenagers.  The weather was beautiful so we weren't in it much but had a great ocean front view.  Maid service was great.  Room was well cleaned daily.  Fridge and snack bar always refilled.

We were in building three, which was very well maintained.  Almost all the restaurants are in this building, and it has a 24 hour coffee/snack bar.  The main pool and a smaller pool are also located at building three.  

The grounds are well groomed, and the beach is huge and beautiful.  The pools were not my favorite.  They were not heated.  The water was also below the skimmer line so water was not circulating in the main pool.  Also, pool chair saving starts very early, and unfortunately, many "reserved" chairs sat empty all day.  I just started moving people's things after a couple of hours.  Service at the pools was pretty good.

Food was hit or miss.  The taqueria and Mexican restaurant were great.  The buffet and Italian restaurant were ok.  The seafood restaurant was below average.  The service and food at the Asian restaurant were bad.

We booked through Costco, and arranged our transfers through their provider: BD Experience.  I do not recommend them.  They wanted to pick us up 3.5 hours before our return flight when were were 20 minutes from the airport.

Overall, it's not a 5 star resort, but it was a good escape in the winter.

findings.title: Mackenzie C. (4/5)
findings.snippet: My girlies & I just spent the weekend here & it was lovely. Richer, Rafael, & Arturo served us on the buffet patio all weekend & were especially welcoming, but all of the staff was incredibly accommodating!! The food wasn't the best honestly but Lemon Fish was soooo good that it made up for it lol, very nice resort!!

findings.title: Jeffery C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Uriel and Bryan were super friendly during the paint and sip, they provided awesome service!!

findings.title: Nancy A. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I went to this all inclusive resort back in 2014 when it was first built and it was a great experience. I went there for a week with my ex boyfriend and our itinerary was set out for the whole week by the staff. 

This resort has many restaurants such as the international buffet and a Japanese restaurant. There is also an open bar and we got unlimited drinks at no charge. All we did was tip the bartender. The staff was amazing and cleaned up after me all the time. Always gave me piña coladas everywhere I went and took them away or refill them immediately when I finished.

Beach shore was kind of rocky but it was still nice. Got to do parasailing to see the views of playa del Carmen! Staff was very nice and attentive. Everything looked very clean and brand new too. My room was very beautiful and had two sinks and two showers to use including a tub. Very nice

findings.title: XX Y. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
This may be a great resort but my husband and I booked transport from the airport to the property and nobody is here to pick us up and the hotel phone keeps ringing. It's been ringing for about seven minutes now on my second go of trying to contact someone. Now I'm surrounded by taxi hounds. What a terrible first impression.

After a few days the "little things" started to add up. This morning I wanted to order room service but the phone in the room does not work and I can't order it through the app either. 

Yesterday my husband and I had a Bali bed and we tried to order drinks from the app and they never came and the staff didn't know we ordered at all.

findings.title: Vianca M. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Did not like it! It's a dated hotel, in much need of a remodel. We paid extra to be on the reserve side of hotel and was expecting a nice room boy was I wrong. If you're someone who likes a  clean nice aesthetic hotel this is not it. smell in the hotel was too much coming from someone who's not sensitive to smells. The Food wasn't great either. The one pro is it does have a beautiful beach and the massage was great.

findings.title: Nichole C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
PLEASE READ- This is the worst hotel I've ever stayed out in Mexico. First of all the heat inside of the hotel is terrible. It is hotter than it is outside inside the hotel. Second of all the food is absolutely horrendous. I went with my mom and dad and both of my parents were throwing up, three out of the seven days that we were there. 

When we went to the Buffet, I cut into my pancakes, and the pancake was completely oozing batter and it was completely RAW. We went into the sushi restaurant, it was called a Fishhouse or something, that's where my mom got food poisoning . I got ramen at that place, and it literally tasted like DISH water mixed with noodles. also, the sushi tastes like it's from Walmart (if Walmart had sushi) . Lol. 

My dad got food poisoning from the tacos at the Buffet but all of the meat the same throughout the hotel so good luck people .... We literally tried all of the restaurants and they were so disgusting either overcooked or undercooked. Everyone was complaining about the food. Ugh how could they not do anything when EVERYTHING WAS DISGUSTING AND MAKING PEOPLE VOMIT

We talked to FOUR COUPLES there- they threw up from different restaurants. We talked to a guy who worked there, and even he knew about all of the food poisoning that was going on in the hotel . So at this point we were like fuck it let's eat at this fancy expensive restaurant - we'll when we went into the steakhouse we THOUGHT that it would be better since it's super expensive, but when I ordered my steak it  was completely raw. So the next night we thought we would try that Italian restaurant. I got the most simplest thing on the menu fettuccine Alfredo and I thought to myself how can they mess this up? Well, they certainly did. It had a NO TASTE AND was completely bland and I took two bites . my parents and I lost a total of 5 pounds during this vacation and we were so ready to go home! So sad and I will never be coming back to this Resort.

I have one positive thing to say. The waiters were amazing. They were always happy and accommodating.

But yea.. all in all if you want to be miserable and scared of food, puke your guts out, then this is the place for you !

findings.title: Claudine L. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I came here with my family around May for a few days and we really enjoyed our stay. The service was not too bad and they were attentive, it does get a bit slow at times (which is odd as I don't think it was too busy during our stay) but that's understandable. 

The resort comes with multiple restaurants and we enjoyed trying all of them. 

I think the service could be improved especially with the amount of money we spent.

findings.title: Morgan R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I had an amazing time at Paradisus Cancun. I stayed there recently for my boyfriends birthday. The staff went above and beyond at every turn. We stayed in the Reserve section which was adults only and it was amazing. The room was very large and clean. The food was ok over all but the Sal steakhouse was very good. Our server Juan was a delight. I would definitely recommend and would love to come back again!

findings.title: Patty P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Booked hotel through Expedia and my husband got us a suit with two double bed s when we arrived they told us we they did not have double beds only king size bed. We booked the room for my husband, myself and our 13 year old. I told them there's no way we could all sleep in the same bed. They said that the room you book is upon what's available. And could not get us anything else. The rooms are nothing like the pictures online. They are outdated and not worth what we paid for. Also we found that you don't make reservations to the restaurants it's first come first serve. I have not yet ate at the restaurant but I will be coming back to review

findings.title: eva s. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I normally love all inclusives
but this one has a lot to be desired. First and foremost they should warn you that most of the menu items at the restaurants have an up charge. The reserve section is tranquil, you have an adults only pool and a snack area. That's it!!! Too much money for too little value. Very disappointed.
Lastly the rooms are very warm
Probably due to the age of the property.

findings.title: Ana R. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The worst Customer Service in all of Cancun. The "manager" walks around looking down on all the guest and staff and does absolutely nothing else. The are no perks at all in this hotel. 

Upon arrival, we booked an outing to Isla Minerva and then a taxi that would take us back to the airport upon departure. The person we paid didn't tell us that after our outing, we would have to find our way back to the hotel on our own. He also never booked the Taxi, although we paid for it and we ended up missing our flight. They never returned my money or cared. Will never go back.

findings.title: S D. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Horrible experience
Butler incompetent
Staff blamed us for things instead of admitting to
Obvious mistakes 
Uleses "manager" did nothing when complaints made
General lack of concern regarding terrible experience
Many great hotels on hotel zone
Recommend Marriott !! So much better

findings.title: Michelle V. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The experience this trip for me was decent. The three star was for the view. Customer service is a bit slow, food wasn't the greatest as I've tried other resorts. The room 
a/c wasn't working properly. But room service was great! Overall, it's decent for a quick trip but not a long stay.

findings.title: Raylynn N. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The all inclusive stay was 100% worth it. 

- The resort is super safe (plenty of staff available 27/7, only authorized vehicles and guests can enter past the front gate, resort is located on a hill so it's difficult for randos to come in, national guard makes regular rounds on the beach via foot and helicopter).  

- The resort is gorgeous with plenty of restaurants, bars, lounge areas, and pools. 

- Tours and taxis are extremely easy to book

- Live entertainment practically every night 

- All of the facilities are clean and cleaned often! Our room was replenished and visited by housekeeping every day of our stay. 

- Lastly the staff is amazing! Everyone is genuinely so kind, accommodating, helpful, and available. They really go the extra mile to make your stay a positive experience.

findings.title: Leonardo B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: If you want a great time in Cancun, this is the place. Customer service was excellent.

findings.title: Imran S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I was traveling to Cancun to celebrate a friend's birthday so we were looking for an all-inclusive hotel that would have good service, good access to the beach and the pool, and overall provide a nice time during our short stay.  I booked the room through the Melia app as through the app there was a discount in addition to the discounted rates given to MeliaRewards members. 

The lack of service continued during the check-in process.  The Paradisus is a large property comprised of many pyramids across a wide land size.  You enter the property through the main pyramid which has a small check-in and check-out section to the left-hand side.  We went in there to check-in and were instructed that because we were reserve, we would check-in at a different pyramid and thus were walked to the Reserve pyramid.  The attendant who walked us through was nice but could not answer any questions and kept repeating "your Reserve agent will answer all the questions".  The pyramids are designed in a similar fashion with an open layout in the middle, stores, restaurants, or hotel facilities on the ground floor in the middle and guest rooms on the top floors surrounding the open atrium.  The Reserve pyramid is also designed this way with the check-in desks as well as a lounge on the ground floor and guest rooms on the top floor.  The check-in attendant was busy helping someone else when we arrived so they asked us to wait in lounge.  On the ground floor in the open atrium, the Reserve has a lounge which serves complimentary drinks, coffee, tea, as well as heavy snacks.  The lounge was open in morning until mid-evening so you could stop here for breakfast, a late snack, a lite lunch, drinks and snacks or a lite dinner.  There were many tables surrounding the lounge and sitting in the open atrium was very nice and peaceful.  After a little while, the hotel attendant came in and said they were ready to check us in.  

The room itself was also a decent size and contained the following - along the left side was a bench to either site or to store luggage and next to this was a long desk on top and below were drawers as well as a cabinet which contained water, soft drinks, water, and some food items.  Since this is an all-inclusive, most of the contents in the mini-bar were complimentary and should be refilled each day and refilled based on the preference of the client - ours were refilled only upon request and even though it took a couple of calls.  Above the desk was a TV mounted on the wall and finally along the left side was a table with two chairs.  On the right side of the room were the two double beds with a nightstand in the middle - the beds were comfortable and provided a decent night sleep.  

Paradisus is also a large property so there were plenty of spaces, chairs, and beds available next to the pool and beach.  The Reserve pool is a separate area where it is adults-only and it is supposed to be more exclusive - it was quieter than the regular pool but towards the end of our stay which coincided with the weekend, there were plenty of kids who joined the pool as the staff did not regulate who would come in.  For the Reserve pool, there are beds surrounding the pool which need to be reserved a day in advance and once reserved it is yours for the entire day until you give it up - so you can wander away but if you leave something of yours there or let the staff know that you will be coming back, then they will not give it to anyone.  While this is nice on one side, it does limit the amount of guests who have access to the limited beds.  Also, we were not informed upon arrival that the beds needed to be reserved a day in advance, we only found this out on our second day - again, information that would've been helpful in advance.  The large property provided plenty of opportunity and space to enjoy both the pool and beach, as well as walk along the beach and stay within the property boundaries.  

Other amenities on the property include complimentary wi-fi, which was a decent speed and allowed for email and Whatsapp but was slower for YouTube and streaming.   There is also a gym on property but it is a bit further away so we did not access it.  Overall, the Paradisus was a mixed bag.  The positives are the large resort space, the plethora of choices for restaurants, the Reserve lounge, and since the resort was so large it provided quiet areas so the noise wasn't concentrated into one area.  The negatives are the lack of customer service, the somewhat outdated rooms, lack of a map or clear instructions/details as to what is available and when, as well as communication with the hotel regarding airport access.  Final note, I went for a couple of days and it was at the beginning of the week and left right as the weekend was getting started - there was definitely a different crowd, different vibe, and increase in noise level from when we arrived to when we departed.

findings.title: Benjamin E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: was the best resort that I have ever been to must recommend. Food was sooo Goooood. The pool was hot and had activities in the middle of the day. Also there is a cat that is around and is so nice. Rooms were emacellet.

findings.title: Catherine G. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We were here for 10 days and there is a lot I wanted to say but not enough space. For a full breakdown of each day, go to my review on Tripadvisor. 

Check in: do not expect the room you booked. Make sure you get what you paid for
Food: Only places we didn't get sick at were Sal, Cielo, Blue Agave and Sante. Or the reserve bar near the spa. 
Avoid: the buffet. Any dairy products if possible, especially the cheese. Building 3 if you want to sleep (loud music every night and the doors don't black it)

Service: lacking, no apologies for mistakes made by the hotel. The honest employees will tell you about it. 
 Double check: the AC. Ours did not work and they asked us to check out at 11 and check back in at 3 for a room with working ac? Extremely inconvenient. That your discounts are applied at every dining experience. Otherwise they will NOT reverse the charges at checkout. 

Saving graces: the view, any experience outside the hotel. Building 4, Yamil (Sante Cabanas) was an amazing server, Mervin (Cielo) was an amazing server and great dining experience, dinner at Sal, lunch at Blue Agave. 

Good food options: tacos at Blue agave, the food at the reserve buffet, breakfast at Sante, aguachile in the cabanas, anything but the elote at Cielo. 

Check out: they will be rude, they will not budge even if it's their fault. Double check everything. They will hate you for it, but it will save you spending a couple extra hundred dollars. 

Safe Travels!

findings.title: Maika P. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Absolutely loved our stay at the Paradisus Cancun resort! We booked this trip for our an anniversary trip. Once we arrived, we were greeted immediately and our luggage was taken to our room for us. We were assigned a concierge person and they helped us throughout our stay. Thank you Alexis! You were amazing. We booked dining reservations through her for our entire stay and she helped us book excursions as well. She provided many options and we chose the one that worked for us. 

The room was very nice! We booked a luxury suite ocean view and the view was indeed amazing. We spent a lot of time on the balcony admiring the views. 

The food was great! I would say that the buffet was a hit or miss depending on when you get there for the freshness of the food. My favorite buffet time was breakfast! The food was coming out constantly fresh. 

If you're pool side, the chairs can fill up quickly. But many people were leaving their towels on their chairs even if they were leaving. Just ask around if folks are using their chairs or not. There are servers that you can order food and drinks from. 

Overall, I think enjoyed my stay at a Paradisus Cancun and would come back!

findings.title: Grizwald G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Came to visit received terrible service. Security escorted me out. The food and room service too was horrible too.

findings.title: Dione M. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Terrible place to stay unless you have an ocean view. The rooms otherwise, are small , dated and the lights in the bathroom are orange so women, forget about doing your hair or makeup in there. Also, the common space of The hotel Is extremely humid due to the hundred of hanging plants. The staff is nice but the service is terribly slow, the food is mediocre at best and not always warm. I would recommend staying somewhere else in the hotel zone if you are considering Cancún. The Hard Rock is a great all inclusive option.

findings.title: Shanique W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I came here to celebrate Christmas with my family. First and foremost, this hotel is absolutely gorgeous. Just beautiful. The lobby made you feel like you're in a jungle. I will say this resort is probably better for adults and not so much kids. There's not much kids activities. They did have a kids club but unfortunately, no parents were allowed to stay and watch. I personally do not feel comfortable leaving my young child alone and she wasn't comfortable with that either. 

Anywho 

I had a luxury ocean view suite in their 3rd pyramid on the 5th floor. The views were lovely but the screen door was very hard to open. Like you had to use a lot of strength to pry it open. Not fun 

I recommend making reservations at one of their many restaurants over the buffet. Everything we ate at the restaurant was delicious. The buffet was only good during breakfast time. Went once for dinner and didn't really enjoy it. 

Overall i would definitely go back but maybe not with my child.

findings.title: Chris C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I am sitting in an airport 4 hours before my flight because I was forced to leave early by the transportation company which Meliá uses so they were not inconvenienced. They, not us. This just caps an awful experience at the Meliá Paradisus. 
Last year we went to Meliá Punta Cana and regretted not joining their circle group. This year. We are glad we did not. We planned this trip in January of 2022 and requested connecting rooms for us and our children. We emailed and called about our 2 rooms and upon arrival they only had one room and of course, once they figured out we had 2 rooms, they did not have connecting rooms Anywhere in the property. We asked to speak to the general manager as checkin already took 1.5 hours and we're sent to a front desk manager who told us they could give us connecting rooms but they would be a lesser room than we have and they would still charge us for the higher room price. We asked that is they could guarantee their safety and were told no. We were then told there was nothing that can be done.  We asked to speak the general manager again and of course we're given Diana Cosmo who was not the GM but the front desk manager. After speaking with her all we could do was upgrade another $140 a night to have Kooning rooms which they told us couldn't be done before and we spiel have more perks of the report but not our children. We felt we had no choice from a safety aspect so we did. The hotel service was not very good. We ordered food at pool and it was cold and soggy. Dining experience was inconsistent to say the least. We were told more of what cannot be done than can be done. We felt as though we inconvenience the staff on a daily basis. The only time I have heard the word no more was from a 2 year old.  Housekeeping was horrible. They cleaned our room at 5pm. Well. They made the bed and swept floor, sort of. When I walked into bathroom there were no towels. I had to chase them down and found out there weee none on cart so we had to call the service express to have them sent up. We also ran out of soap in the pumps in the shower. Called 5 times to have it refilled. Our concierge only assisted when called. He was not proactive at all. 
This is it about being spoiled or privilege. When you spend &13,000.00 for a stay you do expect a level of service. This hotel disappointed from check into checkout. Oh. Apparently there is no GM of the hotel or they do not want to be bothered. We asked for their card and all we received was an email for Diana  who did nothing to help us from the start. 
Please search elsewhere for your stay in Cancun. The extra work will be worth it.

findings.title: Clara C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Paradisus is so pretty. There are greens everywhere! They're literally hanging in front of your room. Ask for room 301. It's got the perfect view of the pool.

I was here in 2021 and 2022 for Illenium's Ember Shores. It was his 3-day music festival. It was glorious. Despite the rain and government trying to enforce rules, I had a blast. This year they really screwed up reservations for a lot of people. Rooms weren't ready when promised. I personally arrived before 11 AM but didn't get into my room until 6 PM. I had to nap on the beach.

I felt like Paradisus set up different dining options for these 3 festival days (Fri, Sat, Sun) compared to their regular dining options. They only served burgers at the pool. Instead of ice cream, they had nachos. They had set menus at the restaurants. On Monday morning, it was like a 180 change because other non-festival guests started coming in. I got to eat ice cream at the ice cream cart instead of nachos. Alcohol was still unlimited, which was the best part.

findings.title: Dindayal L. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Resort is decent but bathroom areas look old. Resort reception messed up my booking and had to change my rooms. The room we finally settled into had very loud air conditioning. We complained about it and I was told they will find me a new room but we will have to check out at noon and will be allotted a new room at 3. All under the garb of process. I was also told that someone would come and verify the air conditioner. 

Food seems decent and the beach is beautiful. All in all mixed response, I would advice  to look else where. Not satisfied.

findings.title: Shells Y. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Went here for my baby moon in August. Honestly, we were extremely disappointed. We were first placed in the older building & ended up having issues with the room. The light in the bathroom kept flickering & we couldn't adjust it. The tub was very high that made it super dangerous for me as I was 7 months pregnant. This room was extremely sad looking. Felt like a run down hostile. (I've stayed for cheaper at nicer places in Cancun). The hotel accommodated us with a room that they originally tried to get us to upgrade to for an additional $900. The room was waaaay better. No view but more comfortable to stay in. I've stayed at the Paradisus in Cabo & it was top notch. GO THERE INSTEAD. 
The pool....sucks. Guests go as early as 6AM to place towels or a sandal on a chair to claim it. The hotel should not allow this. I ended up tossing towels from chairs. You aren't there, it's not your spot. I actually needed a chair to sit in. The bar at the pool was a bit hard to get any type of drink. No food really at the pool which was a bummer. Hellloo Prego needs food. 
The beach....heckled immediately by random people trying to hustle on the beach. We weren't even comfortable to stay down there & enjoy the view or the beach. Also, the adult pool is only for timeshare members. 
The food...very bland. Not much flavor. I'm from LA. A street taco guy has better food. Sucks that you have to have a reservation at the restaurants. The Buffett wasn't too bad though & hit up the taco place!!!! Sooooo good. The coffee stand was amazing. Get the almond flavor syrup. 
The gym...needs a bit of updating. Kinda sucked that it's location doesn't have a view of anything. Otherwise it was a basic gym & got the job done. 
Beware of the sales people trying to get you to buy into a timeshare. It's not worth it. We did the sales pitch, calculated it, read the fine print. Don't do it. You can get trapped into spending money & not get out of the contract. 
This hotel was a bit confusing. All based off of what type of stay you purchased. Which made 0 sense. No one was helpful about things. 
Wouldn't recommend this place at all.

findings.title: Ruben C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I had the pleasure of visiting Paradisus for a family trip for 4 nights back in early August of this year. It was our first time in Cancun so we didn't know what to expect, but wow the hotel lives up to its name was it was utter Paradise. Every employee was extremely nice and we were always greeted with a smile, we literally felt like the employees were our family members as they took care of us and showed amazing hospitality. I wish I got to remember everyone's name but a stand out and our favorite bartender at the swim up bar was Orlando. Orlando made the best drinks and joked around like he was our cousin, I advise everyone to make sure to try the Orlando Special. The drinks overall were top shelf and the food in the restaurants exceeded our expectations as every restaurant we tried had great food items, Blue Agave had amazing tacos. Our favorite moment was when they had an obstacle course race in the pool with summer music under the hot sun. Can't wait to come back to Paradisus!

findings.title: Alice S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Pyramid 5. Adult only area . Bar and food . Amazing. They treat us like family . You can have a butler take care of you. Top shelf drinks are part of the package . It's amazing . Good amazing. Butler will book your reservations for dinner each night . Best food !!

findings.title: Yvette 'Divie' E. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Great for a work trip plus; wouldn't come for a holiday. 

I stayed here to attend a 1000-person conference. There was only one class of room s available when I booked (junior suite) but they reached out and I upgraded to the Reserve for $75 more per night. I was on the first floor, right next to the family pool; loved the ocean view but didn't get the "adults only" experience I paid for. Over the 7-day period, I tried multiple restaurants and services. The verdict? 

Food: Highly recommend Cielo (lunch), Sal's Steakhouse (dinner), Malva (breakfast), and Reserve lounge (fruit and salad). Luke warm on the main buffet restaurant and wouldn't do Agua Marina again. Room service was okay and helpful in a bind. All worked with my gluten free, dairy free diet, with best service from Malva. 

Service: Variable, and this is why I wouldn't come back. I upgraded to Reserve but my concierge, Freddy, ghosted me! Meaning: I didn't know the free services and activities offered, that I needed to  book restaurants and reserve beach beds in advance, etc. I don't know if he was off but poor concierge service = giant waste of money. Other staff around hotel were generally nice and sometimes helpful. 

Ambiance: Its pretty and well constructed. Hotel was at capacity and aside from long food waits, they did a great job. Common spaces were humid but added to ambiance. 

Other: Gift shop was expensive for some items, like sunscreen ($37 US!!). Spa was amazing; Leonor worked her magic. Definitely go an hour before for the full experience. 

Could've been great but got the job done.

findings.title: Wayne G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: AC in room does not work woke up soaked in sweat told them twice and they never fixed it or moved me to new room!  Spa services total rip off over 200 USD for 75 min massage!  Restaurants are boring and lack entertainment in fact the entire hotel is boring and lacks entertainment.  It's very dated and showing its age.  Poor design where you have to walk too far to get to your room and back.  Lacks water park type amenities at pool and entertainment at pool basically this place is old and boring with awful AC and food is ok at best.  Not a good deal for 400 a night.

findings.title: Bethany W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My husband and I really enjoyed our babymoon here! We stayed three nights and loved getting to try a new restaurant each night. The whole resort is nice and clean (except a few of the lobby bathrooms that got pretty gross at night) and the staff was very friendly and welcoming. 

If you're looking for a quality resort to relax at for a few days, this is a great choice!

findings.title: Janet G. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We were originally scheduled to go to Paradisus Cancun in March of 2020. And then the world shit down. Fast forward to August 2022. 
We've been to many all inclusive resorts (including reserve paradisus punta Cana)

We stayed for a full week in the reserve section. We had a deluxe ocean view room. Before arriving, we received an email stating we were in a jr suite. When I called CS to make sure they had us in the correct room, the man on the phone was unbelievably rude. Told me to "stop talking" so he could read my reservation info to me. Huh. 

Upon arriving at the resort, we noticed how beautiful the lobby is. Humid but gorgeous. 

Our room was lovely. Housekeeping is exceptional. Eva, I think, did a great job. 

A few mornings a week, yoga is offered at the outside gazebo overlooking the ocean. The waves were so soothing. I wanted to try the stretch class but the instructor never arrived so I used the well appointed gym. 

We used the Bali beds which is a really nice perk. We loved the ocean view ones. Joel at the Bali beds was a great server.  Valeria also AMAZING!
Caesar in tower 5 reserve area was great about clearing our glasses and plates during a cocktail hour. 
Lunch box service by Teresa and Antonio and richer was perfect. They checked on us constantly refilling our drinks. 
At Capella, we also had great service. (Maybe Josue. I can't recall)
Pedro and sofino at sports bar so so good. Seriously Pedro is the best bartender. The. Best. 
Roberto great server also at sports bar. Polite and friendly. 
Sofonia  and giovani were friendly and professional. 
Ernesto at Lemon Fish was amazing server. And that food was really good and fresh!
I hate buffets. Hate. But the buffet here was good. Each day had different choices. 
Our favorite restaurant was Cielo. That food was unbelievable. 
We've been to many all inclusive and some have cost a lot more money (sandals). The service and food here was very very good. 
Our concierges were Violeta and Mauricio. They were extremely responsive every time we made any request. They were professional and friendly. Ask for them. You won't be disappointed. 

Would we stay here again ? No. We would not. 

Why? Because the temperature of the room was too warm. Goodness knows they tried several times to make our room cooler. Even with their efforts the rooms temp never got below 77* (it was btw 77*-82* the entire stay) and that is uncomfortable for us. We are from Houston so heat is not foreign for us. But the room was way, way too hot. 

***Don't spend extra money on ocean view bc we had to keep the blinds drawn or would have been unbearable. That was a rip off for us. Wasted money***

Sadly, that is a deal breaker for us. I understand it's been a warm summer. We live in Houston, so we are used to the heat. We've traveled many places in summertime (Guatemala, Jamaica, DR, PR).  My husband has MS and it's triggered by the heat. And the entire stay, he dealt with issues bc of the warmth of our room. Usually we can go to the room and cool off. Not here. We've never dealt with a hot room before. We visited many tropical locations and the heat in the room has never been a problem. 

So sadly, in spite of the good food, great cocktails, and amazing service, we won't be returning to Paradisus Cancun.

findings.title: Jennifer D. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I brought my husband here for his birthday . The resort looked nice but we were told that we cannot eat at any restaurant without reservations, when we tried to book reservations everything we wanted was booked so we ended up not eating anything we wanted . The alcohol was watered down , the food was mediocre at best and there are WAY TOO MANY raccoons running around freely . Nice hotel but they need to work on a lot of things .

findings.title: Alexis O. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Tequila and water is what my girl Anna wanted me to name this review as. Anna and Isabelle at the Yhi spa are a necessity. The spa was antiquated not even on my top ten of amenities however the massage we got from Anna and Isabelle was top tier and by far the best massage I've gotten on vacation and way better than what I've gotten in the states. 

Let's start from the top! In booking this resort I became a Meliá member which was the best choice. I instantly got a discount on each night so I was able to upgrade to the reserve. The reserve comes with an adults only pool, adults only beach, premium bar and FREE Bali beds with your Reserve stay. When we arrived, we had a small hiccup, they didn't honor our request for a king bed in our suite for the first night so on the first night we had full size beds and we hated it. First thing in the morning I switched over to a king bed. The reserve also comes with a concierge, our concierge Jorge was not responsive at all so we asked to change our concierge. We were assigned an amazing woman her name was Violeta, Violeta was nothing short of amazing!!!! She was super attentive, assisted us in every way and was truly a a gem. She made our stay at the Paradissus such a breeze, I would definitely request her in the future and would recommend that you do the same. 
One major thing to note: it's super hot in this place! It is legitimately a greenhouse there are plants everywhere and obviously plants won't thrive in colder temperatures so expect to sweat... a lot. It's poorly ventilated, it's hotter inside the resort than it is outside in the sun. 
Reservations are also a headache, it's tough to make a reservation and if you don't have a reservation all
You can do is eat at the buffet or off of the resort or order room service which is one of the more limited room service menus that I've ever experienced. 
If you are traveling with children, there isn't much to do for kids you'll either be with them at the pool or in the hotel. Most resorts have a super cool and sun kids area but there's nothing like that at the Paradissus. 
There is plenty to do for adults, they have water aerobics, Zumba, painting, crafts, hiit classes, spa, plenty of beach/swim up bars and off resort activities. 
Yhi spa was really basic. I was surprised that it was so basic when the resort is just so upscale. I typically spend time in the steam room, sauna and hydrotherapy but it was lackluster so we just had the beach massage. The beach massage was AMAZING! Ana and Isabelle did not disappoint at all. Ana made sure we got a bottle of wine with our package which was greatly appreciated. 
The service was half and half but overall great I have no complaints. 
Alexisyvette

findings.title: William L. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I enjoyed my time at Paradisus overall, the hotel interior is very beautiful adorned with real overhanging vegetation throughout. We stayed in a standard luxury ocean view room priced around $420 a night all inclusive. Had the restaurant and service been better, this could have been a 4 star review. 

CONS
- HORRIBLE HORRIBLE restaurant reservation process. We knew it would be bad so we tried calling days in advance, were put on hold for 5+ hours and no one picked up after being transferred. We then tried to make reservations in-person when we got to the hotel and was met with a line and limited hours in which you had to make them in-person.

We attempted to do a walk-in some restaurants that were clearly at 10% capacity and were told we needed a reservation. Some folks in my party complained to varying employees and they got agitated, which was not expected

I suspect they are trying to push people into eating the non-reservation offerings like the buffet and the taco bar which is much cheaper to maintain. 

PROS
- Beautiful interior, nice selection of restaurants IF you can get a reservation
- Once you can actually get into a restaurant, service is pretty good 
- Nicely stocked room beverages and snacks, did not skimp out on the alcohol for mix drinks

findings.title: Blu M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This was my first time in Cancun and this hotel was booked through a jiu jitsu retreat, so I didn't have any choice in hotel, however from the looks of this hotel it was beautiful. Despite its beautiful appearance, we had several problems during our stay. The first problem was with the check in process. I had a roommate but they booked us in a room with one king bed in it, and we had to wait an extra night to get the room we were suppose to get which was the two bedroom with beach view. The second issue was with the customer service. Pretty mediocre to be honest. Some of the staff were incompetent and not very friendly. Seemed like they didn't like us because we are Americans. The third issue was the food. Unfortunately I ended up getting ill from this trip but I sort of expected it to happen. Some of the food there were pretty good. The gift shop here is expensive as hell and they sell essentials here for a ridiculous price. Someone tried to buy sunscreen here and they were charging 40 plus dollars. If you are going to stay here just be prepared to pay alot, and make sure to bring all your essentials because it is so expensive to buy those here. I probably would not stay here again.

findings.title: Tifany E. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I just got back on 6/26/2022. We stayed for 5 days. Here's my review-
The staff is great. I enjoyed the decor. Our room was cleaned very well every day. We stayed in reserve & the extra perks were nice and worth the upgrade. The bad- it took a long time anytime we went to eat. It took while to get our food at every restaurant in the resort. The food was NOT good, i barely ate while i was there. The only thing i enjoyed was the hamburgers they serve by the pool and then when we paid extra to eat at Sal-Steakhouse. The website said there was plenty of entertainment/activities and shows to keep you entertained. We were bored most of the time, especially at night. There was never any shows. They had a couple of DJ's playing music if you wanted to dance and one night in the bar they had a 2 man band. The list of entertainment they sent me was bare and not pleasing. The only time we had any real fun on our trip was when we went and did excursions. While I did enjoy the staff i associated with, unfortunately I would NOT stay at that resort again.

Also- (and i know this may be a stupid complaint, with it being the beach/island) but 90% of the resort is hot. I spent most of my time all sweaty and couldn't sleep well at night because the room would only cool off so much.  I dont enjoy sweating while im at dinner-inside.

findings.title: Amanda S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall we truly enjoyed our stay and had an incredible vacation and experience. This is the best resort in Cancun! I was highly impressed and would not only love to return but would love to stay at another Melia property.

We upgraded to Reserve level and it was well worth it! They assign you your own concierge and Frida took such good care of us, making everything so easy and smooth- from booking our dinner reservations and any other request we had. We had access to an adults-only pool and amazing restaurant Sante that's exclusive for Reserve only. We also had the ability to book Bali beds at the pool, which was our favorite part, plus room service was included.

I am a huge foodie and that's probably the most important thing for me. In this area Paradisus Cancun is much better than any other all inclusive I have been to. Room service was pretty good, which is rare. They do a great job with authentic Mexican food- blue agave is sooo good for tacos. But our favorite was Cielo- we had an absolutely amazing experience not once but twice! This restaurant and its incredible food made our vacation unforgettable. The first time our server Jose was just wonderful in every way and so sweet. We loved the food so much we came back again and our server this time, Noe, was beyond incredible. He went above and beyond to give us a memorable experience. Everything from the guacamole, margaritas, the amazing appetizers to entrees and desserts. The tlayuda is an authentic dish from Oaxaca and it's a fusion of flavor that's mind blowing! I'll remember it for the rest of my life. Be sure to ask for the habanero sauce for a yummy kick! Chef David is a genius!

Some other highlights:
The staff is by far the best part. They really take care of you and are ALL so genuinely sweet, especially at restaurants. I will never forget them. Especially Cesar who serves the Bali beds and Sante restaurant, and took such good care of us. Every single person throughout the property greets you and checks in on you. This is top notch service!!!!
Beautiful design and aesthetic everywhere, loved the boho look and the plants everywhere in the lobby. It also smells soooo amazing and fresh everywhere!
Impeccably clean in rooms and throughout the property.
Our room was beautiful and had everything we needed. No issues whatsoever.
The beach is gorgeous! Stunning views of the Caribbean Sea .
Spa is A1. We had amazing massages and wonderful experience.
They do a great job with covid protocols. All staff wear masks religiously, which is very reassuring. They sanitize luggage and have bleach pads for your shoes. They make you wear masks at the buffet which is definitely necessary. And all paperless menus everywhere with bar codes. 
Drinks are stronger than most all inclusive resorts, which is nice!
Guest services was great anytime we needed something sent to the room and even call to follow up and ensure you received what you need.
