Loved their bracelets that are used for room keys and to display your level. Much better than the ugly wrist bands most resorts make you wear.
Covid tests are required for travel back to US and they offer covid tests in house in the resort for $25 USD which is very convenient and also cheaper than external to the hotel.
I also appreciated that the resort wasn't catered to only Americans, which is refreshing compared to most places. I loved that guests were from all over the world and that you're able to experience some culture.

The only complaint I have is that it's extremely hot throughout the inside of the lobby and main areas, which makes it uncomfortable at times.

I highly recommend the Paradisus Cancun for an upscale experience that delivers in very way. This place is highly impressive and they do a wonderful job in every way. Out of all the many resorts in Cancun, I did a ton of research and am so happy I chose this one for an unforgettable experience.

findings.title: Dianie C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Worst experience ever! What a rude environment! We spent almost 2 hours to check in. During that time we asked 3 different customer service reps to help us check in perhaps at a different counter, and they all said that we needed to wait for assistance at the counter we were at, because that was the only one available at that time. After it was finally our turn the girl at the counter told us we needed to go to a different counter because we were part of a group that were there for a convention and the other counter had all of our information and she didn't (but all counters have the same system, so how come she wouldn't be able to see our info?). I refused to go to another counter to start another line after waiting almost 2 hrs for them to tell me that, and after 3 people from their staff had assured us that's where we needed to check in at. After I firmly told her a few times I was not going anywhere else, she decided to check us in.
Also, when I was making the reservation online their system refused my card 3 times telling it declined. I checked with my bank and they confirmed the hotel never ran it through, therefore the bank never declined the transaction, so their system was acting up. I then decided to use the PayPal option they had available at their site. The transaction went finally through. Going back to the day we checked in, the girl at the counter decided to tell me that she was going to have to reverse the transaction because I used PayPal and it was under my business name and not my personal name (so why take the payment in the first place?) What the heck is wrong with this people??? After arguing for a while we were finally able to get our room keys... THE ROOM: Hot as hell! The entire hotel is hot. There is no way to get the AC pumping in your room, they control it. There is not enough lighting either. The phone didn't work. And the wall outlets have all been closed so you can hardly find where to plug your phone or even your flat iron!!! Some of our friends had problems also from lights not working AT ALL to even being getting someone else's room! Imagine being changed from room to room 3X and going into one and finding someone else already there. SHM!
We went into one of their restaurants and when one of my friends went to go serve herself she was told in a very rude way to put the serving spoon back, wait 5 min and come back, because they weren't ready and they were doing us a favor by opening a few minutes earlier. Ahh! And be ready for only bottom-shelf spirits. I mean, we supposedly are at a 5 Star Hotel (not cheap at all!!!), so you would expect some sort of better customer service and come on! Better maintenance too! I DO NOT recommend this place to nooo one! Cancún is beautiful and their people are nice, except for that inhospitable place!!! Very disappointed.

findings.title: Kim B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Everything about this place screams old. Now knowing that the property is 30+ years old i guess it's in a decent condition but wish i knew that before hand. The people at the front desk attitude was just as horrible as the food. 

When i arrived that evening at 10pm the lady at front desk said my room was cancelled. She said i needed to go back to the website and rebook. Well hold on what's the reason why my room was cancelled?? Never got a real solid answer. Everyone was pointing fingers but no one knew. 2 hours later after speaking with managers our room was finally reinstated. At that time no restaurants were opened. So we ordered room service. The food looked and tasted like cruise ship food :-/ . It's suppose to be All Inclusive but we were charged by the man that delivered  the food that it was $6 cash for delivery, we asked him if that went towards hotel or his tip so we would know how to tip him. he states $6 goes to front desk ... so we gave him $3 in tip plus the $6. When i asked the front desk the next day the gentleman at the front desk stated everything was all inclusive and no other charge. (interesting) .... the next day we went to eat at  Malva and that Buffet food sucks too. The only thing i ate was Omelet that the ladies made fresh. The Bus Burgers near the pool was the best food they had however 1st Day they gave a bag of chips with ur burger and the rest of the days they gave u about 5chips on the tray.  The Mexican restaurant didn't hv the greatest of foods either... shrimp was salty & the lamb barbqua had a funny smell & after taste.... however the churros  dessert came out nice and hot. Their Lemon drops was delicious. 

There were no coffee pots in the room. however u can grab  hot water or coffee from Nepresso near the restaurants on Floor Zero ... we found out on the last day that they served croissant sandwiches & muffins.

on the beach You can pay $250 usd for cabana on the beach. Mr Cuiche was great and attentive. the $250 came with 1 lobster and 3 shrimp skewers, 3 different kinds of civiche and a bottle of moët. 

This particular property will not get my money again even if it was comped. 

When i checked out i saw my husband and my sons copy of their passports sitting on the desk open for anyone to walk up and see. When my husband asked why was it sitting there she didn't have a reason and tore it up . 

This place is a whole bunch of horrible. 

i couldn't be so happy to Check out and leave there

findings.title: Courtney C. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed at this resort for Paradise Blue and I loved every minute of it. The rooms don't get as cool as I would have liked them to but the pool was a perfect place to cool off! All the restaurants were super yummy and the buffet was a great place to grab a bite to eat before hitting the next set. HUGE SHOUT OUT TO HENRY, who worked at the restaurant near the beach! We made sure my friends and I had shots and kept the party going! He also had wonderful customer service and told us what items on the menu were delicious! My boyfriend and I ate at Sal, and it was SO DELICIOUS! The guacamole with grasshoppers was an interesting combo but with the crunchiness/ salty of the grasshopper really tied it together. I'll definitely be back next year to try the rest of the restaurant. Thank You Paradisus for allowing us to have Paradise Blue at your resort!

findings.title: Amber G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This resort should have 10 stars. For starters, the ambience set throughout the entire resort is beautiful. The food and drinks from both the various restaurants and room service are exquisite. Everything is flawlessly clean and the little details provided in the rooms bring all of the comforts of home. The beach is exactly what you'd imagine when you think about going on a tropical vacation.  

All of these things are true and wonderful, but... 
THE SERVICE IS INCOMPARABLE! Every single member of the staff is incredibly kind and personable. They will go out of their way to make your stay as pleasant as they possibly can.  

During my stay, I became very ill and the measures that the staff went to to help me brought me to tears multiple times. From making special meals (off-menu) to accommodate my illness, to the hotel manager, Rosanna, calling the room multiple times to check on me and ask if I needed anything. They went to the extent to decorate the room with balloons and bring champagne and gifts on my last day when I'd finally started to feel better. These people treated me like I was a close, beloved family member and I am forever grateful to everyone there, truly.  If you had any reservations about staying here, don't. It is everything you could ask for and so much more. BOOK NOW! I promise you'll be so glad that you did.

findings.title: Breanne B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Not a good experience. No one knows anything. There's no clear directions about the hotel or the amenities. Reservations required at every restaurant other than the buffet. Room service doesn't want to take your order bc they are busy and will try to talk you out of ordering. AC goes out a lot, I got upgraded to a premium room because of this and the ac in that room ran out of Freon. They never fixed it. The presentation was a complete scam. Service is terrible. I will never go back.

findings.title: Charlie O. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
What an incredible resort! 
This was our second time at an all-inclusive resort, and Paradisius Cancun did NOT disappoint! We visited the week before Easter from Monday to Thursday. 
The views and beach are absolutely stunning. Plenty of beach and pool chairs to relax and enjoy the hot Mexican sun and sea air. Do be mindful of the sargassum (seaweed) that accumulates on the beach in the warmer seasons. The resort did try to clear it but there's only so much you can do. We also found the waves to be too big to swim. 
Onto the food... pretty good! There are a variety of restaurants to choose from. We found ourselves eating at the buffet pretty frequently and that was more than sufficient for us. They had a great fajita bar and the guacamole... well let's just say we got our money's worth. 
The rooms were extremely clean, comfortable, and quiet. Full-stocked mini bar. No complaints there. 
Finally, and most importantly, the service. We were FLOORED at just how friendly and pleasant EVERY STAFF MEMBER was! We were greeted with smiles and the staff truly made us feel as though we were family. 
On our last breakfast at the buffet, one of the wait staff, Julio, took our picture and made sure to tell us how much he appreciated our business. 
We appreciate the effort that Paradisus made to ensure we had a wonderful vacation, and we cannot wait to come back!

findings.title: Marlene A. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Property is beautiful. Don't expect much. The temperature in the hotel is always uncomfortably warm. There is no air conditioning  in common areas and in most restaurants. We literally left dinner at night dripping wet. No one wants to help with anything. No one knows anything. Everyone says "I don't know". Upgraded to Reserve and our concierge was a disgrace...useless Ruth. Couldn't get us a restaurant reservation and the restaurants were always at 25% capacity.  We were traveling with an 11 year old in our group and they gladly took our money for an upgrade EXCEPT no kids allowed in any of the Reserve areas. So many other great hotels in Cancun I would go to next. Also stay in the main building (building 3) we were in building 5 and it's 3/4 mile round trip the main pool from building 5.  The only reservation you will get for dinner will be the buffet your first few nights I promise you that...every restaurant is "full" yet it's empty. the Mediterranean restaurant we walked out, we couldn't even eat our food it was so bad.....grounds are well kept and clean and beautiful. They don't turn pool heater on until the weekend. Such an odd run place. The people that were amazing were Alejandro, Victoria Rodriguez at the pool and Wendy at Ginger (the only place on the hotel that has air conditioning).  Servers worth mentioning were victor rodriguez at pool, Alejandro and Wendy at Ginger (the only place that has air conditioning and can cool down).

findings.title: Emily M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: An amazing hotel with amazing staff, and good. Definitely recommend Timoteo C., he is a pool bar employee & made us feel comfortable and welcomed. Don't hesitate to book here!

findings.title: Elgin M. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Loved my stay here. 

I heard a lot about how bad the food and service was at an all inclusive resort but I saw none of that. 

Every meal I ate there had something served that made you say "wow"

Staff was friendly and attentive and the view from the pool made for plenty of great photos. 

I would come beach and plan on doing so in the near future.

findings.title: Stefan R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This is a horrible place. Fifty five times we told them we needed a quiet room as our daughter is only 2.5yrs old and needed her sleep. Twice, once in Dec and once in March, we got put essentially right above the DJ in Building 3 where nobody can sleep until 1.30am until music stops. Our concierge ensured us they building 5 had weddings, even though we have seen nothing of the likes while we were there. Bunch of liars and trying to get more of your money as they talk. A disgrace. Stefan.

findings.title: Jay S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Warning: read the 1 star reviews elsewhere before booking. We didn't and wasted a lot of money and more importantly had a terrible vacation. Let me preface this review by saying this isn't our first time in Cancun nor is it our first time staying at an all inclusive. It's never a good sign when you want to leave within 24 hours of arriving. Below, I'll break down the good and bad from our trip:

Good
Check in was easy
Bell boy was prompt and courteous
Majority of the staff around the resort were friendly.
Resort is fairly easy to navigate 
Multiple large pools 

Bad

Room type - I had reserved a Room type w/king bed since we were traveling with a toddler. Of course they gave us a room with two small double beds. No effort was made to rectify this even after we told our 'personal concierge'. Literally the resort is half empty and we are told it's at capacity and they can't do anything. Futher we were in the main tower. Great, right? Sure if you don't mind music blaring till 11pm while you try to out a toddler to sleep. 

Food reservations - you have to make reservations to each restaurant in order to go otherwise you are stuck with the subpar buffet for each meal. We tried to make reservations the night we arrived for each day of our stay. We are told restaurants are either unavailable or the best they can do is a 9pm reservation for each restaurant even if it's 3 days out. Meanwhile I see night after night the restaurants are ~30% capacity. I'm traveling with a toddler and 9pm isn't going to work. I literally had to argue to finally get accommodated. Imagine you spent all this money and have to beg for a reservation. Hardly a 5* experience.

Food quality - this is probably the worst food I've had on all my vacations. Its somewhere between the hospital food and the worst cruise ship food. Bland and lacking in every way imaginable. If you have a vegetarian in your party, they will need to Uber eats something. The running joke was this is the first all inclusive that we will lose weight. To be fair there are items on the room service menu that vegetarians can have but you shouldn't have to eat in your room constantly. Their main restaurant blue agave can't make something simple as a bean and cheese burrito or a veggie taco. C'mon... 

Mini bar in your room - what a joke. 4 beers and a pack of Oreos, you filthy animal. Laughable really. 

Upselling - oh my god the upselling. From the moment you check in your so called personal concierge will get your phone # and text you non stop to try to sell you excursions, time share sessions, photo sessions, etc. Yiu try to escape and try to relax by the pool, nice try bucko. You will be sold a photo package while you try to lounge. Oh you want towels? How about we send you on a parasail. Oh you want a veggie burger? How about a hot dog that was meant for someone else instead? Murphy's law in full effect here.

When you finally get out of the resort to do something fun you realize quickly there are charges for almost everything. You want to sit on the beach, that's $220. You want to sit under an umbrella by the pool, it's X charge. You want a coconut water, that's an extra charge. There is absolutely no personalization to your stay and they make limited to no accommodations to your dietary needs. 

Water bottles - good luck getting someone to give you one. Only a cup of water which we didn't want to give our toddler for obvious reasons. 

To go food - non existent. They tell you when to eat and where. No to go containers at the buffet if you want to take something for your kid or maybe eat by the pool or whatever. after I explained my kid was hungry and profusely crying (hence didn't want to sit inside and disturb others) they did me a solid and gave me a few napkins to take away a slice of pizza. This one really upset me. It's not that big of request. And they treat you like no one has asked something like this before?!

Liquor - the top of the line stuff is Bacardi, Jim beam, jack daniels, hornitos, etc. but you'll only get it if you ask for it otherwise it's the house stuff which is typical practice at all inclusives. 

Service - hit or miss. I'll explain;
Requested milk for my daughter to go. Got a cup of chocolate milk when I opened it to feed her. Requested water bottle. Got mineral water Requested water bottle and explicitly specified and got a cup of water. Room service repeatedly forgot ordered items, condiments, etc. 

Needless to say, I would never stay at this resort nor a Melia property again. Disappointing in every regard. You spend thousands of dollars to try and unwind and they ruin your vacation trying to upswell you. Read the other reviews and know what you are getting into. This resort was a major bust for us. Disappointed that Costco even has this resort on Costco travel. It is no where near a 5* star. The only way you think this place is a resort is if you've literally never been anywhere.

findings.title: Agnes W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing resort!!! Spent 1 week here in February for my bday. Great vacation!!! Location is amazing, resort is beautiful & clean. Beach is lovely, pools refreshing. Food limitless- sooo many options & choices. Drinks fantastic!!! All of the staff helpful, polite & kind - they all work very hard. Will return. Thank you Paradisus for an unforgettable experience

findings.title: Mike W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Have spent a week here and wow what an amazing place with amazing staff.Orlando bello at malva are absolutely amazing taking care of guests from refilling drinks to getting items for you. Axel was awesome with the pool activities especially playing water polo with guests, there are so many more staff that are very attentive at lemon fish, lunch box, the swim up bar,And Enso that I could not possibly name them all.. thank you for a fantastic experience

findings.title: Amy S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is hands-down the greatest resort I have ever been to. The staff is so friendly and welcoming. I felt so safe here with all the COVID-19 protocols and sanitizing. The resort is beautiful and the food is amazing as well. This is my first trip to Mexico and everyone made it amazing. The staff at the ginger bar were fun and exciting. I will be back!!! Pedro @ ginger bar was the best.

findings.title: Christine C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Yikes, run for the hills!  It feels like you're walking through an abandoned strip mall with half the restaurants open and half staffed. Everything is an up charge, so if you've come to take advantage of this "all inclusive" hotel, you'll be disappointed. In order to have dinner, they've requested you make a reservation via the phone in your room. Unfortunately, no one answers the line. You also are not permitted to make a reservation until the day  of. The only way we were able to make any reservations was to go down to guest services to ask why no one was answering their reservation line.  This is also for families, so you'll likely see more children than adults. Just a warning!  You also are not allowed to request alcohol to your room as room service. The only way you can get a beverage is by running down to a restaurant and bringing it back up. It's kind of laughable, you get two beers in the fridge when you arrive, but it's all on you to figure out the rest!  The cabanas are extra, certain restaurants are for higher paying guests, the room service food is something an elementary school child would be served in their school cafeteria. I should have taken a photo of the pizza for this purpose, it's laughable.  Good luck all! There are better options!

findings.title: Kristy G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Please do not even consider staying here. Everything is an up charge. Pool bed, room with a view, restaurants, beach beds, etc. I paid for a room upgrade and was not told about a live karaoke band that would echo every night booming loud into our room. Room service is inedible. We cut our trip short and weren't offered any type of reimbursement. I also had a spa treatment gifted to me by a friend and they never told me about it and have yet to reimburse her.

findings.title: Nicole G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This was my first all-inclusive resort experience and I had the literal best time of my life. We came for a weekend festival that bought out the resort for patrons so i'm not sure if this changed anything or not, but I really don't have any big complaints. The rooms were clean, service was great, and they're not stingy at all about the alcohol. The only thing I would say is that the food I had all weekend was just alright.

The resort itself was insanely beautiful... it sat right in front of the blue ocean with incredible sunrises and sunsets. There were plentiful cabanas, pools, and bars scattered throughout the resort. I loved the actual paradise feel of this resort... the soft white colors, the lush plants and beautiful little koi ponds on some of the floors were just amazing and unlike anything i've ever seen back home in California. Every single room had a great view (some more than others!! If you're lucky enough to get a room that overlooks the ocean.) Paradisus is pretty confusing to navigate though because there's 5 different pyramids and the floors don't necessarily align with the room numbers. The employees are nice enough to try to help direct you though even though some of them may have a hard time understanding you, so if you can't speak Spanish, i'd advise using a translator to help foster communication!

Anyways, I would come back here without a doubt. I'm so sad my trip was a short one because my stay here was amazing. Highly recommend.

findings.title: Veronica W. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Most of the staff at restaurants were amazing and went above and beyond. Bar staff also was fantastic. What made this bad was the reservation system. They stated that the non buffet restaurants needed reservations but there were staff saying it wasn't necessary. Then when we tried to walk in staff said it was reservation only. So we get a reservation for the next day only to see that they accepted walk-ins ONLY if they spoke Spanish. So they make exceptions for people who spoke their language. Fine. But don't come here if you don't speak Spanish.

findings.title: Luke D. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Staff is hit or miss, servers will offer to get you a drink and then just not come back. Got up early to snag a bed/seat on the pool deck since all the guests here Claim spots with their items early on. But when I returned to the spot I claimed the employees told me it was FOR STAFF. I don't understand why a cozy beach cabana is being reserved for staff with ABSOLUTELY NO SIGNAGE OR INDICATION.
Bad arrangement of areas, there's like a million dead ends and you basically have to walk through everything to get to anything.

findings.title: Nancy C. (4/5)
findings.snippet: As far as all inclusive hotels go, Paradisus was one of my favorite experiences. The service was generally awesome, the food and drinks were above expectations, and the grounds were substantial. My friends and I opted for The Reserve and were so glad we did - the extra drinks lounge, adult pool, and restaurant Sante were so worth it.

findings.title: Ilona K. (3/5)
findings.snippet: PLEASE READ When we checked in the first thing we noticed was loud construction noise and the harsh smell of paint everywhere . Not to mention as you walk around the resort inside there is no AC so it was very hot and humid , in the room the ac was fine . Always waited on the elevator which took 5 minutes minimum . A lot of flaws in the resort I would not come back . We came for our 1 year anniversary and honestly I wish we went to excellence of somewhere more nice . Keep in mind that you get what you pay for here . We had the reserve which I thought meant we would escape from kids but apparently kids can stay at the side too . The room was outdated and small and the shower didn't have good pressure . Only thing was we had our own pool. To reserve a cabana was soooo hard and they were always booked . The beach had terrible seaweed and me and my husband both got seaweed stings on our bodies , I got bit by a crab which was not fun !! And getting into the ocean was a struggle because of all the broken shells and rocks . Only 1 good day of swimming in 7 days . On the plus side the drinks were very good and the food was impressive . All the restaurants surprised us with the food so that was nice . They had a coffee cart open like 4 hours out of the day and that was not good either . Gelato bar was always out of gelato !! Entertainment was bleh not enough energy . So overall not a great experience. Would not recommend especially with all the construction and being bothered by the receptionists every day . Not romantic at all

findings.title: Michelle N. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
9/23/2021-9/27/2021
WORST HOTEL I'VE EVER BEEN AT.
I don't know why there aren't more reviews talking abt the truth of this hotel but I agree with the other reviewer, Lisa W. We also bought the all-inclusive package: purple wristbands

The honest truth abt this hotel is that management completely sucks. We had a large group of 20 people booked for a Bachelor/Bachelorette and the the front desk + management screwed everything up. They lost our reservations, made us wait hours to get our rooms ready bc they lost our reservations, booked half of the reservations wrong with the wrong number of beds and our rooms were HOT and HUMID. Then they tried to bribe us with discounted spa bookings but then said they had no reservations available.... Wth, ok??? Then they discounted our rooms from $928 to $600  for all of their mistakes which was fine with us but then they flip-flopped and switched & baited us 3 times to get us to fall for their lies so we would drop the subject. We had to go to the receptionist desk every single day to to get them to fix their mistakes and they still couldn't do anything right. Upon checkout, Alexis the manager said "Oops, my mistake, it's still $928." Horrible management, completely untrained and ignorant. Why should we, the guests, be paying for your mistakes??? We were absolutely furious and they honestly didn't give a shit about us. This is hands-down the worst hotel I've ever been at. I'd 100% rather stay at a Motel 6. Totally ruined our experience 

Hotel: I totally agree with Lisa W., that the inside of the hotel is crazy muggy and humid. The center of the hotel is pretty with vine plants everywhere but bc of that, they've made the hotel like a GREENHOUSE. Once you walk in, you immediately start sweating coming out of the shuttle from the airport. No point in trying to wear any makeup or anything particularly nice bc you start dripping sweat right away. Honestly the temperature automatically made you slightly miserable unless you go right out to the beach, sit deep inside the Malva buffet or just hang out at the receptionist desk for the AC

Waiter, waitresses, pool guys/girls: Amazing! They remembered our names, they checked in with us to make sure we had everything we needed, they interacted with us and made us feel totally welcomed. They are the only people that knows how to run this place. Give them all a raise and bump them up to management!

Food: Lots of variety but it was all ok. Not saying it was bad but nothing was mind-blowing either. To me, the fruits were the best thing there! Honeydew and papayas were amazing!

Beach/Pool Area: Very pretty, nicely kept and the only facility note-worthy of this hotel

CoVid: The hotel provides an included CoVid test with your stay. On the bottom floor, they've set up a meeting area for guests to go to at their appointed time for their CoVid test 1 day before your check-out day and email your results within 12 hours. I got mines in like 2 hours

Overall, the hotel was just ok but for a supposed 5-Star hotel on Trip Advisor and the price, this did not meet our expectations. This place really did not make the cut. Save your money and book somewhere that has nicer rooms, working AC, better food, and a front desk + management team than actually knows something.

findings.title: Emily H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
What can I say about the last 8 days to sum up our experience??! 
It was awesome!   The service is wonderful, the food was amazing! Views spectacular! 

We stayed in the reserve side.  A definite if you can swing the extra $$.    We loved that there weren't kids on that side so all you hear from your Bali bed were conversations and the ocean.  I'm glad the party and daily DJ were on the other side, we could join that when we wanted to.  We had 2 concierges that split our week.    They accommodated every request.  Dinner reservations, room change requests etc. Big thank you to Ceci (Ce-CHI!) and Violeta! 

Sante restaurant was our favorite for breakfast and lunch.  It's in the reserve, so quiet and wonderful. Amazing food on the patio under shade with an amazing view.  (see photos) The menus are at this resort are creative and wonderful.  We noted at the pool that those complaining about the food didn't even try anything!  They didn't recognize anything on the menu and would leave!  What a shame.  If you are looking to eat American food all week and hotdogs, go somewhere else. We were NOT disappointed with anything we ordered the entire week.  (And we are foodies and travelers) Everything was cooked perfectly from lamb to steak to fish.  They are extremely accommodating- anything you want, they will do it so just ask.  We would combine favorite menu items together etc.  Hats off the chefs here.  It was great!
Pool service on the reserve side was unbeatable.  Thank you to Lucas, the pool concierge,  for getting our bali bed everyday with a smile!  Because we were there for 8 days we had different wait staff at Sante for breakfast and for the pool.  A huge shout out to Valeria, Ruben, Moises, Joel, Julio, Josue, Yamil, and Maria!  And to Oscar for sharing your love of Tequila, the amazing history lesson and taste testing!   We appreciate Tequila now!  They were ALL fabulous.   Seriously, thank you everyone. 

The absolute only thing I can complain about is it is definitely hot in the lobby.  It's structured like a botanical garden so beautiful and unique, but humid like a greenhouse.  I don't know if this is on purpose or something needs to be fixed.  It did make dining at the buffet during the day uncomfortable (its fine at night) and the Italian restaurant, which is located in a side part of the main lobby, is very warm in there.  Some restaurants have outdoor seating only so make reservations about 8pm when the sun is down.  It's pleasant and they have fans.   Sals and Blue Agave have great air conditioning as well as the sports bar in Ginger lounge.
We did have to call for a fan in our room which helped tremendously.  If you like it cold when you sleep, the rooms do not get colder than 70/71, a common theme among those we met also.  The Asian restaurant is under construction in the middle of the lobby.  
No place is perfect and this would not keep us from coming back!  We miss it already.  Melia has not disappointed us thus far.  We enjoyed this as much as Spain and Orlando.

findings.title: Madiha K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We did the all inclusive with the reserve upgrade which I highly recommend. Pros:
-concierge was awesome, reserved dinner spots for us every night, available via WhatsApp and checked in on us in person every day 
-upgrade was adults only with a much better pool, less crowded and very enjoyable. Good system to reserve cabanas 
- food is fantastic, big variety of restaurants (this was most important to me)
-GREAT mask enforcement, covid testing on site 

Cons (not all related to paradisus)
- seaweed situation is unbearable. Nothing for the hotel to do here but it really is an eyesore for the beach 
- extremely long check in process, best to arrive in the late afternoon to avoid this 
- AC is not amazing, but bearable. Most areas on the premises are not AC'd up but the place is HUGE (5 buildings) so I imagine it would be hard.

findings.title: Fernanda C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed here to celebrate my 2 year anniversary and we couldn't have picked a better place! The resort is beautiful with super comfortable pillows and beds! The view is amazing and the service was exceptional!! Can't wait to come back!!

findings.title: Lisa W. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Ok, here is an honest review.  My stay was from 8/05-8/10.  The  ocean:  Calm water all week.  Terrible seaweed, so bad no one was walking on the beach let alone get in the water.  My second to last day it did not seem too bad so I was able to get in the water a bit. I hear the tractors every day to clean up the seaweed, but it never looked cleaner.
Food: I ate at the buffet and it was ok, nothing wow about it, but a lot of variety.   I did not eat at the other restaurants because it was just too hot.  I stayed in the Reserve, Tower 5, the food they offered there was very limited, meant more for snacking. Food by the pool was ok, again, I was in the reserve pool, limited menu.  I enjoyed eating breakfast every morning at La Palapa. The food was good, not great.  I have read other people say they will make anything for you, but, that is not entirely true.
Service from staff:  They were really incredible and went out of their way to make everyone happy.  A special shout out to Janick, he was my butler.  Everything I asked he did with a smile!  He made dinner reservations, I mentioned my birthday was on a certain day and he made sure everyone made a big deal of it, including a nice bottle of champagne!  He gave me his cell number and checked in on me every morning to say Hola!  And to see what I needed.  Can't say enough about him.  He did everything for me.  He even would visit me at the pool to be sure I was happy or to confirm something we had talked about.
Pool guys:  FABULOUS! Max and Lucas. Max is so great and so patient to deal with everyone wanting a bali bed.  He is very organized, and I cant get over how any of these guys do what they do in the heat.  TIP: If you take care of them, ($$$) they will take care of you!  I had a bali bed everyday, no problem.  I  was impressed how they all remembered my name.  ALSO, Bring a floaty with you, they have a pump right there to blow them up for you.
Hotel: FREAKING HOT!  That's all there is to that. The only place that was somewhat cool was the Reserve lounge and the check in area near the front of Tower 3.  I know some on hear say its not that hot, bull!  I know of some people that checked out of the hotel and went some where else. It's sweltering Period.  So, the problem is that you get so hot from walking around the hotel there is no place to cool off.  Especially in your room.  I had a technician in my room 3 times!  It didn't help.  My trip was pre-paid so that is why I stayed and dealt with it best I could.  The only cool place was at the pool.
Room:  The room as well as the rest of the hotel was very clean and had house keeping everyday. One thing though, I left $5 every day for the maid.  When I needed my mini bar re-stocked I left money for that person too.  So, on my last morning when I was leaving my room, I saw the maid's cart next door.  I knocked but no answer. I wanted to give her the money personally plus a small gift I got her.   A male employee saw me leaving, he asked if I was checking out.  I said yes and he went into the room.  Before my elevator arrived , he came out of my room and ran down the stairs!  I had a feeling and yep, he went in the room and took the money, not the gift.  And yes, I wrote a note saying who it was for. So, I am wondering if that happened everyday......really pissed me off!  I don't  know what the solution is for that.
Additional info about the views of the ocean.  Unless you are standing on your balcony, that is the only way to see the ocean from your room.  Laying by the pool reserve area, no ocean views, however; there are ocean views from the main. pools.
I am sorry this is so long, but I hope it helps!

findings.title: Jessica O. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Room:
-Beds were comfortable
-Shower was nice with a rainfall showerhead and a detachable head as well.
-Great view of the ocean with a large enough space that two people could lay out in the sun on pool lounge chairs on the balcony.
-Fridge stocked with beverages.. They did not refill these when the came to clean the room each day.
-If it rains at an angle your room will get flooded with water because the doors and windows are not sealed properly. This can be very dangerous since the floors are all slick stone. I almost slipped so many times! This can also happen in the bathroom so make sure you dry off well and put the bath mat down.

Service:
-Nice employees.
-We had our room cleaned everyday.
-Costs $5 to order room service, this is the first time I have ever seen a charge for this at an all inclusive.

Food and Drinks:
-One of my favorite spots was the Nespresso coffee stand. 
-I do wish there was a bit more options for breakfast restaurants besides just the buffet.
-Currently you have to make dinner reservations each night or eat at the buffet or blue agave. I believe this is only going on because of COVID. 
-The food served outside during lunch is very good. Nothing fancy but they make great burgers at the van stand at the smaller pool and good fish tacos at sunset grill. 
-The swim up bar is always a hit. 

Amenities:
-Gym - nice for a hotel, there was 3 different rooms with various equipment.
-Pool - water was too low in the main pool causing it to be dirty at the surface as well as the water was very warm.
-Parking- If you rent a car it is not a problem to park your car here. There is a side entrance you can take between towers 1 and 2 if you do not want to walk up to the main lobby each time. 
-Spa - did not check this out due to the prices being all way too expensive.

Planned Activities: 
Needed some work. For it being all inclusive I actually really look forward to the activities throughout the day that the hotel has planned (such as morning yoga, dance lessons, competitions, and night time entertainment). The last all-inclusive that we stayed at did a great job of making sure everyone knew about these activities. I felt like the majority of the guests at Paradisus did not know what was going on besides the nighttime shows. I showed up to play water polo one day and no one ever came, as well the majority of the events the staff showed up late to them.

Other:
-Beautiful inside with all the hanging plants. 
-Lots of kids at this resort.
-One thing I did not like is there is levels depending on the color of your bracelet, which I found out later. If you have the red bracelet you are not doing all inclusive, the purple is standard all inclusive, and the gold is adults only. You have to pay more for the adults only and you have to pay more for the cabanas ($200). It makes it feel like it is not really an all inclusive when I cannot go over to the other half of the resort without a gold bracelet. When first looking over a menu at the restaurants here at the resort there was pricing for each food item. This was confusing since I thought it is all inclusive, then realized that it was for people with the red bracelets which was not defined on the menu.  

I don't think this is a bad hotel to come to. It is an average experience for staying at an all-inclusive, which it's almost impossible to stay at an all-inclusive and not enjoy yourself. I had a wonderful and relaxing time while staying at Paradisus.

findings.title: Lisa C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I'm trying to think of one good thing to say about this resort, but actually the only positive thing I can comment on is the housekeeping.I have stayed here before and had a good experience, but after this one I will never be returning here and neither will any of my family. We stayed for eight days and seven nights and was ready to go home by the fourth day. I came with four family members and a 2 1/2-year-old. It took forever checking in and there was nothing stocked in the room so I immediately had to call room service just to get a bottle of water. to my horror, half the beach was gone and what was left on it was covered with brown seaweed. It was also about 20 feet out from the shore and I was told that because of two recent hurricanes the beach was eroded. My daughter was scheduled to get married on the beach and they did not even tell us. She also had to pay a fee to rent the beach for the wedding and they did not return that money to her. The service was horrible at the restaurants and when we went to Fuego, we actually had to wait for 2 1/2 hours to get our food. I got so disgusted I just got up and left to go see the show. My granddaughter was constantly whining and crying because everything took so long and every single time we went to eat I had to get up and go look for a highchair because my request for one got ignored. I even complained to the manager about it twice. When getting up from the Buffay to go get another plate of food our table was actually occupied by another couple when we came back to sit down even though my purse was still there. The service was horrible down by poolside, because it was like pulling teeth to get someone there to get our drink order. The two days that we rented a cabana we got absolutely no service and I had to walk every 30 minutes to go get drinks for everyone. It was horrible I could've stayed home for this crap. I absolutely would not buy any excursion from otium travel. They have a booth set up inside the resort and we booked a sailboat adventure and paid $545. We went to go the next day and the weather was storming with thunder and lightning and terrible rain and they refuse to give our money back. We are still fighting them over this now. I am a club Malia member and I still can't get help with this. May actually have to go to small claims court. I was actually told that if we would have paid by credit card they would have reversed the charge back to us, but because we paid cash they could not give us the money back. I have never heard of such nonsense in my life. This whole week was outrageous. Never ever again! Find another resort!

findings.title: Teresa N. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Not sure where to begin because I loved this place 4 years ago IN THE WINTER. The extremely long, hot check-in process with a time share representative on our heels really made it miserable. There is no air conditioning in the 8 floor lobby or many of the public gathering spaces or MOST OF THE DINING VENUES!  In July it was an impossibly warm situation with the only escape being a hotel room that only cools to 76 degrees. The ocean in front of all the hotels on this strip in Cancun are unable to deal with the massive amounts of washed up seaweed. So swimming in the surf felt pretty strange and was unsightly. This hotel seems to have decided to turn from a family oriented theme to a more party atmosphere. During the day the swim up bar was frequented by large groups of young adults drinking heavily and behaving badly. Then there is a DJ playing extremely loud bass on the beach continuously. This area is very peculiar as it seems it's even too loud for the young adult scene and nobody is renting the large tanning beds that take up much beach space. We didn't do the reserve because I read so many negative reviews about the lack of fulfilled promises. The staff is really the best asset here with many eager to please and we did enjoy Malva and the taco restaurant but the others were just too warm to even enjoy a meal. Sad because the staff is also very uncomfortable working in the hot atmosphere. In the future I'd avoid Cancun in July. I heard from many the air conditioning never cools properly and power outages are common. Good luck if you're used to cool comfortable air at 68 degrees. We even joked about needing ice collars!

findings.title: Hannah M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Ruben was the best person here. He had such an amazing attitude and always made us feel welcome and taken care of. Our concierge could have been better but he was nice. The food was better than ive had at some resorts but it still made me and my boyfriend sick. They advertised that there were like 3-4 bars and there was only 1... they also advertised the asian restaurant and we got there and it was being renovated. They also have the hours on the app of closing wrong bc they have to close at 11pm due to covid. Also had a problem every single day with the bali beds and the pool concierge. The place was absolutely gorgeous but its not all about looks. The room was nice but the shower was not practical. You walk in the shower and would have to run out in order not to get wet while waiting for the water to heat up bc the nob was on the other side of the entIt also had no pressure and conditioner was stuck in my hair for 5 days. The portable shower head did not work in addition.

findings.title: Tammy D. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I'm a little late posting this review but better late than never. We stayed at the Paradisus Cancun in November 2020 (Thanksgiving week).  We stayed on The reserve side  (adults only) and it is definitely worth the splurge. With your reserve stay, you get a personal butler. We had Rodolfo and he was AMAZING! He went above and beyond to make a memorable trip for us. I would highly recommend asking for him. 

At the pool bar Moises and Miguel just to name a couple were awesome but everyone was so attentive from day one! The customer service provided was one of the highlights of our trip.  We cannot say enough good things about the quality of service we got from everyone at this resort "even during COVID". On the reserve side the cabanas are well-placed to give you privacy and you are able to relax and enjoy quiet time if that is what you are looking for. We never had to wait on a drink either . If you want to join in the fun they have activities going on at the main pool with Diego (lots of energy and fun).
The food is average but the quality of service customer service made up for that. 
Highly recommend this property!!!

findings.title: Nicole S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Review for Paradisus 

Diego 
Josue-cured the hang over 
Step 
Wa x
 
 
Just finished our 7 day trip! It was absolutely amazing! We felt very safe. The hotel and staff go ABOVE and BEYOND to assist you with anything you need.  The hotel was VERY CLEAN. I'm a bit of a clean freak and was very impressed with the efforts they took to keep everything sanitized and fresh! 

- [x] We stayed in the reserve section. I loved it and think it was totally worth it. We arrived to the hotel at 7am. Our room wasn't ready as expected and ended up still having a great start! I always travel with a change of clothes on my carry on. Just in case my luggage is late I have what I need to hold me over. So we changed into our swimsuits and started to explore the hotel. 

We enjoyed breakfast outside at The La Palapa. Diego greeted us immediately and made us feel very welcomed. Our whole trip he remembered us and checked in everyday to make sure we were doing well. Josue was also super wonderful and provided excellent services to my husband and our family while we were there. 

We went for a walk on the beach before heading to the pool while we waited for our room. During the first part of our trip the beach had too much seaweed. It looked like it cleared up quite a bit towards our last day. We walked on the beach but did not swim much at the beach. We mostly spent our days at the Bali beds by the pool on the reserve side. Had lunch service to the cabana with food and drinks. It was great! 

We traveled with a total of 12 people. Stef was our butler. Let's just say, if you get her as your butler, you are set! She went above and beyond throughout our trip. She even helped us make reservations on her day off and kept in touch with us to make sure we didn't need anything. She was truly wonderful along with all of the other staff.

We loved all of the restaurants! Our favorites were Bana (Sushi), Italian restaurant and Enzo ( international). The taco restaurant was really good too! I'm a huge coffee lover and the lattes were some of the best I've had! So that really made my trip! 

Overall, I would highly recommend this resort. They take COVID very seriously. Stef made the Covid test process also very easy. We tested negative and had no problems at the airport with the test and confirmation papers they provided.

We visited XCARET Park on our last day. We swam in the caves and walked the grounds. It was an unbelievable experience. On day 5 it was nice to have a change of scenery. The food was not my favorite( we ate at the Mexican buffet) but the actual park was pretty cool and nice addition to our trip.  

Paradisus hotel have vendors at the resort who sell tickets and provided us with safe transportation there and back. I highly recommend this if you have time. While we were there we also went to the evening show that XCARET is known for and it was absolutely beautiful! Great mix of culture, dancing and entertainment. 

We still are in AWE of what a beautiful trip we had! The whether forecast said it was going to rain everyday. It ended up raining for 2 days out of the 7. The rain was on and off. We still made the best of it and had a great time. 

When it rained I noticed the hotel started pulling out crafts for everyone in the hotel. So it's nice that they keep activities going, especially if you have children. 

We did do a photoshoot and purchased a book! I'm really glad we did. The quality of the photos and the book were beautiful and totally worth it. The photographer Diego made the shoot really fun! My husband wasn't too excited at the beginning, but ended up having a blast and that's a huge thanks to Diego and his good vibes. 

It's a beautiful hotel and we look forward to coming back! Thank you Paradisus for a wonderful vacation!

findings.title: Wanda B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great stay! Food was great service was outstanding. Property is beautiful. Definitely recommend the reserve upgrade.

findings.title: Ani A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This has become my home away from home. I'm obsessed with this place. The most comfortable & beautiful resort with the best service. Every time we come, I can't believe we get it at the price that we do, with everything included. I can't wait to go back & take my parents.

findings.title: Mindy L. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Because I had a different resort bracelet on, Gatekeeper Miguel wouldn't let me past the stairs to check out hotel prior to checking in today (while I was on my run).  I showed my reservation to him on my phone, but evidently, no comprehendo for the workers representing hotel.

findings.title: Amanda T. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I would have loved to have given this place 5 stars but it needs a lot of improvements. Before scheduling my vacation I went on Yelp and other sites to review this place. I saw all 4-5 stars which was surprising now that I have visited myself. From the start we wanted the adult side with the upgraded room which we thought we booked. when we got there we were told we had a basic room and it was not going to be on the adult side. It was just my boyfriend and I we did not want to be around a bunch of kids for our vacation. After spending almost $2k for 5 days we thought that we would get more than a basic room on the adult side. We ended up spending an extra $350 to get the luxury reserve suite. The only difference is the room is upgraded, you get a butler and a separate restaurant. The restaurant was nothing special. Every time we are there we did not enjoy the food. The food on the free side was better. However, our butler Rodolfo was great. He was very accommodating. However he was not just our butler he had many other families, etc. so it seemed he was stretched thin. We spent much of our time at the other side which was what we originally booked. It was more lively and had a DJ and entertainment through the day. The reserve side no one was there. It was like a ghost town and the food was not even tasty. We wish we would have stayed with our original booking. When we looked at pictures and reviews of this place we saw some lobster and seafood which looked amazing. When we got there and asked the restaurant where the menu is for the lobster, etc they said it was a separate menu and it would be $50 per lobster per person and we would have to rent out the Bali beds which was another up charge. We were very disappointed when we heard that. 

The food overall at the restaurants were just okay. There was a couple that was not open due to COVID. But, we found out they were opening a week after we left. We would have loved to try something different. The food for some reason seemed to taste better during the week. We thought maybe because there was less people during the week and they took their time to prepare the food. The weekend we were there the food was bland and we could never get warm bread with our food. We asked several times and still came out cold. They close all the restaurants and bars at 11pm. Which is too early in my opinion. We couldn't get drinks or food after 11pm. The all inclusive should last all the time there should not be a cut off time. We walked over to other hotels that were more lively and came back to ours and wished we would have booked elsewhere. 

The positive was the drinks were great and kept coming. The hotel was very clean and well sanitized. Our cleaning lady came everyday and kept everything stocked. We did have good breakfast from time to time which was the omelets. We had omelets pretty much every morning since we knew that was the best thing on the breakfast menu. 

Overall, this place is okay. I would look somewhere else especially during Covid as there is not much going on at this hotel. If you are looking for great food this place is not it. If you want good drinks than stay here that's really the best part of Paradisus.

findings.title: Thembi S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The Paradisus is a grand resort comprised of 5 pyramid structures (though it looks like 3) that are a plant lovers dream! The front of the resort faces the main street in Cancun, and the back faces a very nice beach with tons of straw umbrellas and chaises. Apparently there used to be cabanas on the beach but a tropical storm swept them away.

Due to the fact I was at the hotel with a person who has a timeshare there, the check in process was long and tedious. However it was all worth it when we got to our room which was a spacious one bed suite with a pull out sofa bed. The view from the patio was unfortunately of the parking lot, not the beach, but it had a hot tub and I didn't plan on spending much time in the room anyway! That said, I found the bed to be just ok, and the pillows so flat they were uncomfortable.

The resort is truly beautiful, offering a variety of food venues and options. Right away we visited the buffet and I was wondering how a buffet would work during Covid. As it turns out, resort guests are not allowed to initially pick up a plate, nor touch tongs or spoons/forks to put food on said plate, the staff do all that. It seems effective with the only drawback being they almost never selected the piece of food I was personally eyeballing, and there was occasionally a language barrier. Anyway, the staff there were always lovely, even as I was unintentionally behaving like an ugly American as I figured out their new serving system.

Prior to the beach is an enclosed area around a snaking pool and outdoor eating places. Tons of umbrellas and lounge chairs are scattered about, as well as cabanas. I didn't spend much time there but it was nice to pass through on my way to the beach.

The beach is...well, the beach. Very well maintained and staff would come out the chaises back in place every evening regardless of where guests would move them during the day. In the afternoon, servers would hit the beach and bring drinks and such, it was great.

Every night there was some kind of entertainment. My favorite was the silent disco, where we got [sanitized] headphone with access to 3 stations piloted by 3 DJs. We had a blast dancing around and switching stations to find songs we liked! 

It was a great stay, I would absolutely return!

findings.title: Lori C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I  paid in advance in November 2019 for a trip March 18- March 26, 2020. As COVID increased I contacted the hotel and asked if the trip could be refunded or moved to a different date. I was told they don't have a problem and there are no refunds or vouchers for different dates. So we showed went. Fast forward to Friday, March 20th when another guest informs me that the hotel is closing Monday, March 23. No letter under my room door, no phone call from staff, nothing. I go to the front desk and they confirm this and tell me I can go to another property in Playa Del Carmen or get a voucher. I said no, I didn't book a room in Playa and I don't want a voucher, I paid you in November in full and I want a refund for the three unused nights. He tells me that Playa and Cancun are the same city and I have to talk to someone else. Then he blames the Pandemic. I said look, you wouldn't let me cancel or reschedule so I'm here and now you are closing and kicking us out. I then have to convince him to give me something in writing and another contact person. I repeat the same information to Mendez Perez,  de la Cruz Martinez, Joel  Camacho Chavez, Miguel who on March 27th email me and agree to a refund, but the refund will be up to 90 days. It's now 60 days and nothing. I'm working with my credit card company for a refund and the hotel won't respond. My friends received vouchers with numerous restrictions. The place had 21 guests when they kicked everyone out, the restaurants were closed, and one of the pools was broken the entire time we were there. 

Do not book with these unreputable people.

findings.title: M A. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
If you are even considering booking here, for the sake of your vacation, please keep looking. I have traveled to Mexico every year for the past 5 years and this was by far my worst experience and it's not even close.

I'll preface this by saying I stayed at a Melia property in Cabo San Lucas, a 4 star, which was absolutely amazing so naturally I expected nothing less from their Cancun 5 star location. That proved to be a mistake.

This resort is dirty, has a poor smell, the rooms are poorly cleaned, you are nickel & dimed for everything the minute you get to the property, and their service is horrible.

Starting at the beginning -- check-in. They are constantly trying to up-sell you for higher priced rooms, services, etc. They offered a "luxury" room for an extra charge of $260. I negotiated it down to $180. Fine.

Upon arriving to the room, I immediately notice a dingy, dirty looking rug in the seating area. Stained throw pillows on the bed, and stuck-on food on the spa brochure (shown)

I went downstairs and asked for a new room, hoping that had just been an isolated incident. They check me into a new room. 
Same thing -- dirty rug, stained pillows and this time I even found a blonde hair in the bedsheets. I have black hair. 
Even more disgusting -- I turned over the comforter and found a dried yellow liquid stain on the inside (pictured). 
I was absolutely horrified, especially with the serious concerns over coronavirus and the spread of germs. 

From then on, every minute I spent in the room was miserable, wondering what had actually been cleaned or replaced and what hadn't. That is no way to spend a vacation you spent your hard earned money on. 

I expressed my concerns to their management and I was told that they "looked into their housecleaning processes and found nothing wrong". 
They offered absolutely nothing to remedy the situation. 

In addition, the nickel & diming was pathetic for a so-called 5 star resort. Never have I been to an all-inclusive resort that charged for room service, especially since it's the only food option after the restaurants and buffet close. They charge $5 per order and the best part -- there's a good chance your order will be wrong, as mine was all 3 times I ordered.

They also charge a whopping $200 per day to use their beach beds. You are forced to a purchase a "package" which includes a bottle of champagne. Tough luck if you don't drink
I guess. 

Also, you will be turned away at their restaurants if you don't make a reservation even if there's barely anyone there. 
And to top it off, the food is extremely mediocre, except for the taco restaurant. 

In short, it seems at this place their goal is to make your vacation as difficult and expensive as possible. With emphasis on the latter. 

There are too many resorts in Cancun with way better value to waste a minute of your vacation or spend a penny of your hard-earned money here. 

But if strangers' hair and unidentifiable stains in your bed, and poor food and service sounds like your dream vacay, then book away!

findings.title: Anji R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: We booked a hotel/air package directly on the hotel website and have  now spent 40+ hours on the phone trying to get it cancelled over the last two weeks.  All flights were cancelled and US/Mexico border was shut down.     It should be a very simple transaction to either change dates or cancel but it was a horrible experience.  We finally got confirmation of cancellation for the hotel however the air reservation was outsourced to Funjet Vacations and we have been on hold with them for over 6 hours today to get our air cancelled and refunded.  We planned to go back to paradisus Cancun as soon as the Coronavirus clears up but because of the horrific experience with melia customer service we will never go to a Melia resort.   We really looked forward to the family concierge service but the treatment from melia customer service was so bad that we will never go to this hotel.

findings.title: S D. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Very nice hotel with wonderful beach and water front. 
However they are continually making noise throughout the night, whether it's music or moving heavy furniture, which makes it sound like elephants trumpeting at 4am. 
Even if they lacked the common sense to be quiet while people are trying to sleep, the doors to the rooms are clearly very cheap and have zero sound insulation. 
Something to consider if you like to rest on vacation

findings.title: Cailun G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Something is fishy about this resort and their ethics. Was here with a large group for an event and they claimed that we hadn't paid for our rooms, therefore we couldn't check in. Sometimes there's a mix-up in communications, which I can understand, but this was a complete and utter lack of morals and hospitality. We had full documentation from our bank that we did, in fact, pay for the rooms and all the front desk could tell us was that their bank had "lost the money". We waited 7+ hours trying to resolve this issue, but since this resort's bank is in Spain there "was nothing they could do". They insisted the only way to resolve was to pay in full again and they'd "try to find the money tomorrow". So, being that we were a large group from out of the country without a place to sleep, we paid for a single night. The next morning, the staff we were speaking with the day before wouldn't even speak directly with us to try and keep resolving. We ended up finding last minute rooms at the resort next door and it was 10000% more accommodating and our trip ended up being fantastic.

Beware of this place. You'd be better off building a sand castle and staying on the beach!

findings.title: Lucy G. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Overall this is a very nice resort. If you stay in the main big building, they have live music until 12-1am so if you're there to relax with your kids this might get annoying when you're trying to sleep at 10-11pm. 2 of the restaurants were under construction when we went and another was adults only, we were not told this! If I go there with my kids to a family resort I was expecting ALL of the restaurants to be family friendly as well, as this wasn't an adults only resort. Had a very hard time making reservations to the authentic Mexican restaurant, but once we finally got in the food was exquisite! The food overall was pretty okay, the breakfast buffets were all pretty much the same every morning, thank God they had a omelet station. The sushi place was just okay, they need to work on making the rice for the sushi as it was always so very mushy. The shoes are great at all. They did one of the shows twice, once in the conference room and then any night in the pool. Little tip**they ALWAYS had some kind of food at the shows, so if you can't why a reservation to one of the restaurants and don't feel like going to the buffet, they have pretty good food at the shows. Our hands down absolute favorite food was when they did the fresh grill by the pool at lunch time daily.

findings.title: Alex S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
UPDATE to Amy D's review from Feb 2019


Since our trip to Melia Paradisus in December 2019, I have been debating how to write this review because when we originally stayed in Feb 2019 we stayed as not the full Royal Service but as an add on when checking in. Since both services were so different and we returned due to a previous negative experience that corporate wanted to remedy, see previous review, this isn't an updated review, but a new review based on our second experience returning in the full Royal Service.

Much better!! No upsell's this time! And same great service from the staff! Daniel was there once again leading his team to victory but now there was a new fabulous addition; the new manager, Ramon. They are a dynamic duo and trying the highlight of both trips. 

Wasn't worth the butler service... While the butlers are very nice, they weren't really around to build that personal connection, and if you're there for a week the butlers do have days off. Our butler was very responsive and very sweet and we enjoyed getting to know her but unfortunately we only had 2 days from the week with her and then we were passed off to another butler and two days later another. Also, one of the big downfalls in my last review were the restaurants and how hard it was to get a reservation so most of the time you're eating in the main buffet. It was still a huge challenge this go-round even with a butler to make your reservations. Again, most meals we ate the snacks the Royal Lounge or at the poolside Royal restaurant La Palapa. 

The staff was raving about the new international buffet a.k.a. the main buffet, it was newly renovated since we had been there the first time, and while it was fine and offered many many many options, it's a bummer that they took out an actual restaurant to make the main buffet larger. Maybe this is how they intend to accommodate the lack of reservations...

AND FINALLY, OMG PLEASE CHANGE YOUR TOILET PAPER TO UNSCENTED!!! - thank God I remembered this from our last stay and brought my own toilet paper roll, but this is a huge problem! I ran out of my roll the last day and had to use a very small amount of the hotel toilet paper in our last hours and yet again (both trips I encountered this from vacationing here) suffered a UTI when returning home. Women's bits are sensitive and scented toilet paper is not good for anyone's health; leads to UTI's and yeast infections (I know bc I got one both times after returning from our week stays and had to see a doctor). 

All in all - great experience this time and it was 100% better, but I would be curious if it's only bc of our complaint to corporate or if this will be the new standard for guests going forward? And although no improvements this trip were gigantic I do think the improvements made were vast. 

Recap:
No upsells which was GREAT!
Still lacking at dinner reservations
Consistent incredible restaurant staff!
CHANGE TOILET PAPER

Last plug: splurged on Tempo and it was worth every penny. Excellent job. Look for a separate review.

findings.title: Rob F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing resort, and in incredible condition. You would think it was only a couple years old. The design and decor is amazing.  Beach is soft white sand that doesn't even get hot to walk barefoot.  Great pools that are heated large and clean.  Workers can be seen constantly cleaning and doing maintenance without disturbing guests.  The restaurants are all okay and probably their only weak point. some better than others. I would recommend the Japanese sushi restaurant. Amazing service and everyone is very helpful and polite.  I will certainly return to this place on my next trip back to Cancun.

findings.title: Erin G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I'm super disappointed in this hotel. We were set to leave November 30th at 8:40pm from LAX and check in Dec 1st. Unfortunately the morning of November 30th I had a family emergency and my grandpa was put on life support with a 5-10 percent chance of making it through the night. After explaining my situation and providing the proper documents from the hospital, this hotel has refused to give us our refund of $1073.20. Shame on this hotel for being so cruel and careless in such a difficult time. Don't waste your money here.

findings.title: Albert D. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
They killed my nice vacation !!
3 restaurants out of 7 was closed for remodeling - that's almost 50% don't you think you should mention that when we booked that dates??

I've been in 2 more all inclusive  vacations, 
I never been asked to pay extra for pool beds or stake at the restaurant.
Since the moment we got there I felt like all of this deal is wrong - it's like whatever you paid online when you booked this vacation was just the beginning not the total.

The employees and stuff are great

findings.title: Ryan H. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The GOOD:
Paradisus Cancún is great. The staff go out of their way to make sure you are happy, having fun and well taken care of. 

The beach is pearly white, soft sand and the most turquoise crystal clear water I have ever seen in my life. Waves are big enough to body surf or and the beach is shallow enough for little ones or light swimmers to play around in. 

Housekeeping did a wonderful job everyday. 

Liquor selection was plenty. Jack Daniels, Crown, Absolut, Hornitos, Don Julio, etc. Heineken on tap at the pool and specialty mimosas at breakfast! 

Food was what you'd expect. Nothing Michelen Star but good food. The buffets were always plentiful, clean, and varied. 

Gym was clean, lots of machines, and had two rooms for HIIT or spinning classes. 

One of the BEST things about Paradisus hotels are that you don't have a limit of the a la carte restaurants based on your length of stay like other resorts we have stayed at. At Paradisus' if you want a sit-down-and-they-serve-you dinner experience (as opposed to a buffet style) all you do is press "0" from your room phone and make a reservation.

Mole (Mexican food and in an A/C room) and La Palapa (Seafood, open air restaurant) were our favorite sit-down restaurants. Blue Agave is also A/C and had great street tacos/quesadillas and Guadencio! Our favorite sever ;)

Bana was the sushi restaurant in the middle of the main pyramid (building 3). Eduardo was fantastic and took great care of us. Sushi was good for being in Mexico. This too is an open air restaurant so it can get a little humid. But it's Mexico, seriously what do people expect? lol 

*************

That being said, I have visited Mexico 7 times now and have been to 5 different all-inclusive resorts. I won't say I'm an expert, but my eyes see more than most who are enamored by their first all-inclusive. 

The reason I gave the resort 4 stars instead of 5 is because of a few key factors: 

1. The pool chairs. 
I know that sounds dumb but all the pool chairs have been modified so they don't lay down completely or sit up completely. You cannot change the position. You are in one permanent slightly recline position the entire time.

2. Room noise if you're in the big pyramid.   
The room noise didn't actually bother my husband or myself. But, if your room is in the main pyramid (building 3) they play live music in the center of the building at night. Pyramid 3 is the lobby, most of the restaurants and shops, etc AND a good portion of the rooms. We were on the top/8th floor and because the pyramid acts as a sort of amphitheater the music that was blasting on the bottom level traveled, very clearly, into our room every night. Each night they would play until 11 or midnight. We are heavy sleepers and night owls so we were fine. If you are a light sleeper or have small children I would advise making sure you are not in pyramid 3. 

3. The cabanas/Bali Beds and "the pitch."
This didn't bother me but it irked my husband. 
Upon arrival you are given your room keys and a map, etc. You are also given a very gentle sales pitch from a staff member about their time-shares. They want you to meet with them the morning after your arrival, during your breakfast, so they can pitch their stuff to you. In exchange they offer the cabanas or the "Bali beds" which normally run $100-200 a day! NOT pesos, dollars. So silly.

Anyway, it bugged my husband that these Bali Beds on the beach and near the pools were virtually unused each day unless you paid the ridiculous price to rent them or you gave up 2 hours of your trip for a sales pitch. 

If we had more money we might even participate in the time share program. BUT we knew the pitch from previous Paradisus' and didn't really care about the Bali Beds so we were kind but firm and said NO. And that was that. No stalking, no high pressure. They respected our answer and left it at that. 

(Pro tip: Say no right away. They tend to "up the ante" in terms of their offers if you're willing to sit through the presentation.) 

**************

All in all it's a great resort. We slept and ate and got catered to like royalty (even without the Royal Service package.) 

We love Paradisus resorts and will definitely be back. We prefer Paradisus La Esmeralda in Playa del Carmen but if you need a quick vacation you literally are at your resort from the Cancun airport in 20 minutes. And you can't beat that!

findings.title: Frances S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Paradisus Royal Service exceeded our expectations! My husband and I had the privilege of staying at Paradisus Cancun for our 4 year wedding anniversary and we thoroughly enjoyed our week long stay here. My husband communicated with Karla from Expedia weeks leading up to our trip as well as during our stay and she ensured that logistical details like departure/arrival, transportation to and from the airport, and to and from excursions were taken care of. We were wary about going through Expedia but it was very smooth. 

Upon arrival, we were assigned a butler, Hector, who was very kind and hospitable and truly "at our service" throughout our stay. He helped us make reservations, communicated with the Pool Concierge for our Bali beds, and checked in with us periodically to ensure that we were enjoying our time. I even lost my sunglasses at one point on our vacation and Hector and the Royal Service team found and returned them to me! I thought I lost them for good, so I was extremely happy when they were returned.

Royal Service definitely made our vacation very memorable. Melina at the front desk upgraded us to an ocean view room which was on the ground level and very central to everything we needed at the resort. With Royal Service, you get:

* A Royal Service bracelet & beach bag (for the duration of the stay only)
* A personal butler
* Food bar, premium alcohol bar, Nespresso bar (thank you Oscar and Ramon for your hospitality!)
* Pool & Bali beds exclusively for Royal Service patrons (Aaron provided excellent customer service and we enjoyed the Bali beds very much) 
* Access to the Gym and Yhi Spa amenities (sauna, steam room, showers, massages are separate cost)
* Access to La Palapa for lunch - for Royal Service only. Stunning view of the beach. And Fuego for Dinner 
* Night shows from 8:30pm-9:30pm every night, kids are welcome 
* 24/7 Room Service from the Royal Service menu - I don't recommend lunch or dinner through room service. The food is so-so, but the breakfast is light and tasty.

A few downsides: 
* Overall, the food was decent but could have been better. The drinks were far better in our opinion! However, the one night we went to Tempo (not included in the all-inclusive) was the best food of our stay, hands down
* Yhi Spa felt a little dated, basic toiletries were missing like shampoo, soap, lotion etc. The 'car wash' shower wasn't working either in the women's bathroom. Sauna and steam room were nice though
* Several restaurants closed during our stay, but enough were open to enjoy our meals
* Construction obstructed our ocean view for the duration of our stay

Overall, Paradisus Cancun Royal Service was fantastic and it felt like a taste of paradise, with the beautiful weather, Crystal clear blue waters and the softest sand. The staff were extremely hospitable and kind and we highly recommend bringing cash to tip the housekeepers, your butler, pool concierge, waiters etc. as they work extremely hard to provide the most outstanding customer service. If we have the opportunity to return, we will gladly do so! Thank you, Paradisus, for making our wedding anniversary one to remember!

findings.title: Faye D. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I've been to multiple all-inclusive resorts in Cancun and playa del Carmen, and this is by far the worst of all.  It's hard to access food. They make hard to access food. For being all inclusive, this place have is the worst and the restaurants serve almost the same type of food. U can't tell the difference between restaurants. There are only 5 restaurants and 2 of them requires reservation..1 is almost always close for dinner due to events. Never going back!  Not only that, when we checked in, the front desk lady said she offered us a free upgrade to a better room to find out it was not even ocean view (which was our original reservation).
