She said no ocean view was available and that the new room was an upgrade. Total bs. I complained and demanded to get ocean view as that was we paid for. Another guy fortunately was nice enough to give us a new room with ocean view.

findings.title: Keyur K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I don't know how this place the reviews it has bcuz it's not good. Food is absolutely horrific, been to many other cheaper resorts with much much better food. They've literally shut down half the restaurants they advertise, most are closed for lunch. Bars are not open till 11am, literally nothing is open till later in the day. Long lines for restaurants because too many people and not enough restaurants. Room service was the last resort which was awful, Simple cheese pizza tastes like ketchup and pita bread.......6 day vacation will be hard to do so I encourage anyone looking at this review to look elsewhere!!!!!!!!

findings.title: Andrea C. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Front desk

Rude, not helpful and after requesting a late checkout (1 extra hour) we were told not.  Even after you can tell the hotel is not at full capacity.  

The room is nice but don't expect it to be cold.  The hotel is very hot. 

Fabiola at the front desk was not at all helpful 

Food:

Don't expect Mexican food or anything that will wow you.  The food was eatable but nothing to rave.

findings.title: Shital K. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Always a treat here! This is our 3rd time at Paradisus and we would come back again and again. I see a lot of bad reviews because of the construction happening at the resort but we're here right now and we're having a great time despite the construction. The food, service, decor, ambience and THE PEOPLE here are great. Trying Royal Service for the first time and it's been a treat! :)

findings.title: Candace S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Hope this review saves someone from having a less than amazing vacation while staying at the Paradisus Cancun. I am not a person to usually be bother or complain on much but the hospitality at this resort warranted a complaint.
The check in process was not efficient and our room accommodation were not what we booked. When asking to be moved into a room in which our booking was made, we were given excuses on how they were expecting a big group and couldn't accommodated a move to another room on which we booked originally. After a hour of getting sorted out we (group of 5) were able to head to the pool to start our vacation only to find out we needed a towel card to check out a towel that was to be given to us at check in that we did not receive. Food was average, drinks were horrible, no music at the pool or beach and the lounges were not lively in the evenings. Entertainment was scheduled between the hours of 7pm and 8pm which are typical dinner hours for most, and we were not able to make the entertainment.
After returning to our room to get ready for bed my roommate and I both noticed sand in our sheets. Housekeeping did not change the sheets from the previous guest that occupied our room, unacceptable. As it was midnight at the time, we called to complain to a manager we decided to sleep on towels for the night and to have our room cleaned first thing in the morning. The next day we returned to our room after a full beach day at 3pm to find our room had not been cleaned at all. Again, we complained to the manager and she sent for the room to be cleaned. There was a huge disconnect because as we complained it seems like staff was not following up on the request. Even after expressing our frustrations and how the lack of hospitality was putting a damper on what should have been a relaxing birthday vacation, staff did nothing more to go above and beyond to make sure the rest of our short stay was anything less than amazing. Paradisus Cancun really dropped the ball on this vacation and it effected our vacation in a negative way. 
Also, please know there is only a/c in a couple of restaurants and in the guest rooms. Be prepared to sweat while walking through the halls or hanging in the atrium and lounges. It was much cooler outside of the building than in.
The only good things I can complement on this property is that the décor was beautiful, everything at the restaurant Mole was delicious even the drinks, staff was friendly, and the Yhi Spa was amazing.
I travel often and had the pleasure of staying at the Melia Paradisus in Punta Cana, Dominican Republic a few years back and had such a wonderful time. I was completely disappointed with my stay at the Cancun resort.
Overall, I would not recommend this property to anyone. There are so many other resorts to choose from, save yourself the disappointment. 
Melia, you lost me as a customer for any future travels. Work on your hospitality.

C.S.
Travel Dates 10/12/19-10/15/19

findings.title: Ty T. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Anybody coming here on November 19 for one week stay?  After  reading these review I'm nervous about this place!

findings.title: Arsham H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Update on day 4: with added food poisoning, shower head literally falling off, lines for food at breakfast, this is simply the lowest quality we've seen in an all inclusive or otherwise. Lowering to one star.

findings.title: Ashley F. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Excellent service. Leo and Josue at the swim up bar are amazing! Martin at enso's is so friendly and animated. He told us stories about regional food and was super accommodating. Def recommend this resort, the service is excellent

The only complaint I have is that the room and resort grounds were HOT and the AC won't let you lower it under 65F - which was still not cool enough.

findings.title: Katherine L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Wonderful family vacation at the Paradisus Cancun! All of the staff was amazing! Food in the individual restaurants was also amazing!

We absolutely had the best experience at the restaurant Enzo because of Carlos Gonzalez. He went ABOVE and beyond to welcome our large family two nights in a row. If you do go visit Paradisus make sure you visit Carlos at Enzo's restaurant for a fabulous experience. Don't forget to tip the wait staff :)

findings.title: Greg M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I am reviewing this place as an all inclusive resort in the price range of the Excellence Resort and other high-end resorts.  I am aware there is a way to get this place cheaper and pay a-la-carte.  It is a horrible deal for the money for all inclusive.  1.  Crickets and pigeons are on the menu.  2. Almost none of the staff speaks any English.  3.  they will constantly harass you to come to their time-share rip-off seminar.   Mario begged us to go despite us having very little time to enjoy our vacation, and it became very awkward to keep telling him no.

Take your money to one of the excellence resorts instead where you will get good service and better food.

findings.title: Renee C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My husband & I recently stayed at this Meliá property. We have been to many other Meliá resorts & while this one was not the newest, we found it to be the most friendly. Norma with Royal Service was an angel. She stayed in constant contact with us, she set up dinner reservations, local events & a spa day. She kept track of our day, ensured we never needed anything & was simply a joy to be around. Cesar & Julio from the pool service were both sweet & always willing to help. Liliana in the Spa did a fantastic job, her massage was relaxing & healing. All in all, the resort was great. Of course the humidity was high but the strategically placed fans & air helped. The rooms were very nice & service was efficient & prompt. The evening shows were entertaining. Keep up the great work!

findings.title: Alaya D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Always my favortie place to vacation.  The staff remembers us everytime. Even if its been a while. Drinks are great. Food is exceptional. Views are amazing and room is above expectations. We had a small issue trying to book last time and were unable to book royal service. However they fixed the issue and took amazing care of us. Highly recommended

findings.title: Stephanie S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: My friend and I were so impressed by the Melia Paradisus Cancun resort that on our first day  we decided to sit through the sales presentation about their rewards program, and were even seriously considering purchasing the package for both of our families. We were having this discussion by the pool under an umbrella, when an hour and a half later, another guest and her family came "back" to these chairs and hovered over us for over 30 minutes, causing a scene and even speaking to the waitstaff and pool staff about us. (We had done nothing; it was embarrassing.) When we spoke to pool management all they said is they accommodated the other family so we should be okay now. While I can appreciate this, nothing was done to help us. It certainly left an impression... accommodate the load screaming lady by giving her an upgrade or cabana... tell the innocent guests they are "ok" now. That said, we have found a super sweet pool server in Asunción.

findings.title: Caroline R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Took happy shuttle from the airport 20 minutes away, $50 for one way. Check in at 5pm was easy for the 6 of us, didn't do the Royal service. Stayed in rooms 3328, 3330,3331 in pyramid one, same as check-in. My 3330 room smelled like mildew as soon as we walked in. It's true they burn incense to cover up the smell, hate the incense. The room was clean though except stains on the couch cushions, no cockroaches in our rooms that we could see at least. Light switches are confusing and some do nothing. A mosquito did manage to get in once. The maid organized all our stuff but I don't like that. She also threw away my plastic water bottle that still had water in it, and my sleeve holder for cold/hot drinks. 
All the food was ok, glad we didn't get sick, only ate at bana for Japanese, blue agave for mediocre tacos that are tiny, and enso for breakfast and dinner which is the outside buffet. Do not eat outside for dinner at all because the mosquitoes ate us alive. The waiter gave us off spray after he saw us scratching. It's true you have to make reservations at other places. Made one for market grill but it's mostly meat so we changed to bana. did trivia at the pool to try winning t shirt and saw a couple aerial performers and pool dances at 8pm. Overall good for a bachelorette group getaway if u can stand the smell and mosquitoes. Went to downtown Coco bongo by taxi, way too crowded and unsafe unless you pay v.i.p. For seats. I almost got trampled and they allow smoking inside. Girls are at risk for getting sexually assaulted since you are up against anyone, packed in like sardines. We left that lower room and snuck upstairs, then got led on stage to dance later after performances. Wouldn't go back to this club or hotel. Would stay somewhere else to try something new next time

findings.title: Krystle T. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
August 16-23, 2019.

This was my second visit to Cancún in 2019. I was staying at a different resort back in January & I remember passing by Paradisus thinking that this would be a nice resort to look into if I were to visit again. So when booking my family's annual trip, the group picked Cancún & Paradisus was the first resort that came to mind.

[LOBBY / MAIN PYRAMID]
This place felt like a green house with a heavy scent of incense. The plants that hang around Bana (restaurant) were beautiful but we were too distracted by the heat to fully appreciate them. There was a Nespresso Station on the lower level by Blue Agave (restaurant) but you can only order coffee during certain hours of the morning & afternoon. There was also a Gelato Station but was also open during certain hours of the evening.

[CHECK IN]
Required a lot of patience. Have all questions asked prior to leaving the lobby because they will not give any information (how to get towel cards, where to go to find the list of activities, where to make reservations for restaurants, where to book excursions/spa, etc). The most important question to ask is how & when the bags will be delivered to the rooms.

[ROOMS]
Dated. We had a large group & booked 5 rooms. Each room had their own unique situation happening. Room 1 - flooded one night of the trip. Room 2 - fridge, AC & outlets did not work (moved to another room the next day). Room 3 - certain lights did not work, shower with poor water pressure, room flooded one night of the trip, AC made strange noises & did not fully cool the room to the settings set on the thermostat. Room 4 - cockroach found in the bathroom. Room 5 - battery on door died & needed to be replaced for us to use the key card.

[POOL]
They have an extremely limited number of umbrellas & people definitely woke up early JUST to reserve a space with an umbrella. The main pool was where the swim-up bar, music, inflatable floats (for sale), & activities happened. We rented a cabana one day & the staff decorated it with balloons for a birthday we had in our group! Kudos!

[RESTAURANTS & FOOD]
During our visit, 3 of the restaurants were closed for renovation - Fuego, Naos & Vento. They did or still do not advertise that anywhere online. This significant for a resort as large as Paradisus. There was a long wait for every single meal & for every single restaurant that was still open. Make reservations for your entire stay on the day you check in. Mole was booked during our entire trip. In my opinion, I would recommend eating at Blue Agave for breakfast (specifically for the omelettes & air conditioning) & Enso for dinner (specifically for the spring rolls). As for food, do not expect much. Poor quality & just made for the masses. 

[ACTIVITIES]
Shout out to Alan for being an awesome member of the team! Whether we saw him at the gym, by the pool or running one of the activities in the evening, he always tried to reach out to everyone & get as many people involved as possible. Our family had fun participating in water aerobics, beach volleyball, trampoline and stretching class with him.

[NIGHTLIFE]
Around 7/8pm, there was usually a show going on outside of Market Grill, depending on the weather. Around 9pm, there was live music at Avenue Bar. Usually that was it in terms of nightlife. There's the Red Lounge but it was empty on most nights we passed by. If you're lucky, you'll be there when they have Silent Disco.

[DRINKS]
The swim-up bar, Avenue Bar & the bar at Bana were our places to go depending on the time of day. When it gets busy, the options of drinks you could order becomes limited. I appreciate that Paradisus did not hold back on their alcohol. Our drinks were not watered down, but I guess that's to make up for where improvements could be made elsewhere. 

[CHECK OUT]
A nightmare. There were many random charges attached to our rooms of things we didn't even buy. The staff had no interest in resolving the issue at all. The back & forth dragged on so long, we ran late to get to the airport. 

[FINAL THOUGHTS]
Do your research. If everything mentioned above is what you're looking for, go ahead & book away. From what I've read, they take care of their Royal Service customers well. I personally would not recommend coming here and we will not be back.

findings.title: Greg C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
First off let me tell you we've stayed at numerous Paradisus and Melia resorts in different countries. They have all been fantastic. This trip was VERY different. It was to be a special family trip having brought my 9 month old daughter. It ended up being more of a nightmare. For any new mothers and fathers, let me give you the inside scoop.

First, for nearly 3 days we had to ask them to come fix our door. You didnt even need a key to access our room You could simply walk in. ALL FATHERS!!! - How would you feel knowing anyone could access your room with your wife and baby sleeping inside???!!!.

At one point when we really tried making it an issue, they told us we had to wait by the door for security. Of course, after we told them we have MILK inside the room and our child needs to EAT! They made us wait 45 MINUTES!

Next, for all of you mothers still feeding via breast milk, I'm sure you understand that you need to drink lots of water to keep this going. We asked for nearly 3 days to refill our water in the room. From guest services, receptionist, the maid, the maids in the hallway and even the FRONT DESK MANAGERS - ALMA AND JUAN!!!

Next, the AC goes out in the entire hotel. Our 9 month old cant even sleep in such heat! Of course, After the numerous occasions of trying to address the issues with the "Front Desk Manager, JUAN... I never hear back from him so I have to chase down someone new. This time is was ALMA. Didn't get very far with her either.

"ABSOLUTELY PATHETIC!"

Countless hours later, nothing has been resolved, no phone calls to check on us, not even a knock on the door.

TO HELL WITH THIS RESORT!

If you have a family, small children and especially an infant or baby, let this be your warning. This hotel is not a place you want to be.

p.s. We also found BLACK MOLD on our balcony.

findings.title: Sara G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Our overall stay was horrendous. 

Pros:
-beautiful landscape
-rooms were clean 
-bartenders at the pool were outgoing, friendly, and quick. Best staff at the resort hands down. 

Cons:
Everything else
-AC didn't work in main building or in our room. When we called down they said it hadn't been working for days, if we knew that we would have asked for a room that did have working AC
-food was terrible. Room service can sustain you for a day, but other than that - the McDonald's across the street is worth the trip
-as an all inclusive guest, the mini fridge was not stocked daily. We had to constantly call down to the front desk asking for bottled water (which should be a given - no matter where you are). 
-room service will say "30 min" no matter what, but usually takes close to 2 hours
-impossible to make reservations at the restaurants (but the food isn't worth it)
-the staff is not helpful at all. They would stare at us and then walk away with out answering a simple question ("what time does the restaurant open?")
-front desk calls every morning (early for vacationers) to claim your welcome gift -- which is a breakfast while they sales pitch for a timeshare. EVERY.SINGLE.DAY. 

I would recommend any other hotel, or go in with the above expectations.

findings.title: James L. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Honestly not impressed by this "resort". The only thing that lived up to par was the bartenders at the pool. Those guys really were hussled and earned their money. The food was terrible, but if you get suckered into staying there go to the Mc Donald's across the street. Go down at 6 am for a chair at the pool otherwise you will be laying your stuff on the ground in the sun. The mini bar was not stocked ever with water... so figure that out too. Hopefully, you will be fortunate to have a room with working AC because mine was not, however, other people's in my party was. DO NOT TAKE THE MORNING PHONE CALL OFFERING YOU A GIFT FROM RUBY FOR BREAKFAST. It is a sales pitch for a timeshare.... just all around a joke of a resort.

findings.title: Peter K. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
A very dated resort.  The entire hotel smells like mildew and they try to mask it with so much cleaning fluid that it has a terrible overall smell.  On the lower level they actually burn incense to try to cover up the smell.

Very little of the experience at the hotel was good.   We couldn't get any reservations at the restaurants but they were very always empty, which made no sense.   And on the last day the closed the main buffet so everybody was forced to other restuarants.  We waited over 45 minutes for breakfast before walking out after never being served.

The drinks were horribly watered down and the food was terrible.

I think, back in the day, it may have been a nice resort, but it's way past it's prime.

Other problems included a very long check in only to have to go back to get our keys and wait again, being harrassed often to buy more things like their club and tours and other related problems.  

My recommendation is to stay somewhere else.

findings.title: Be E. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Pros: -BEAUTIFUL BEACHFRONT HOTEL
-Blue Agave restaurant (only felt safe eating here) 
-Royal Service Cabana reservations
-beautiful room
-some great service very nice staff
-hotel security

Cons: -boyfriend got sick at the buffet within 5 mins, 2 hours later fainted from being so sick
-AC went out throughout the entire hotel 4/5 hours 
-Food was horrible every single thing especially room service. Food would be cold by the time it got to the room, and told them we wanted well done burgers. Practically raw when we got it
-took almost 2 hrs to check in and actually get in our room

findings.title: Rhonda Y. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We just checked in and immediately regret our decision. I wish Hyatt Ziva was available for a quick book but it's too late to change. (We stayed there last year and doesn't compare) Strongly advise going elsewhere with the money you spend. Juan (front desk "manager") and Rosi at the front office didn't even greet us with  a smile or look at us. We had booked a king room with ocean view and they first said it wasn't available for another hour when our Check in time was suppose to be 3 and we got there at 5. Then she goes somewhere and comes back and says it's actually not available at all... Then they're like it's not going to be available til tomorrow. I don't understand this if we've made reservationsssssss- can someone explain????!!! 
Then we get to our room without assistance whereas Hyatt ziva or anywhere else usually has a bellboy and even offer you drinks. Our room is a flashback to the 80's (minibar isn't even stocked) with a corner view of the ocean. 

Oh we have "towel cards" for every time we need towels and if we lose these cards we have to pay for a replacement. I mean I could literally go on and on about how awful it is and how much we wish we booked elsewhere. 

Shower head was broken, Bathroom had leaks everywhere. They never replaced our hotel room towels for some reason? I had to call every single day to get new ones which was bizarre. 

Im gonna keep it short. My main issue is people like my family work hard everyday- we plan these vacations to look forward to something. These are suppose to be precious vacation time that we work hard for and rightfully deserve. We're not rude, snobby or inconsiderate people and I expect the same in return when I'm on vacation. It's a big letdown and I hope you other vacationers have better luck! Cheers-

findings.title: Justin Y. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I really wished I would have read more negative reviews on Paradisus Cancun but we stayed at their Cabo resort two years ago and my kids really enjoyed it. We decided on a last minute trip and came down to 3 resorts and we chose Paradisus.

Check-in
Took almost two hours. We booked the trip with our travel agent and he paid with his card, we had the forms for that, etc. etc. Would have booked it with ours if we would have known there would be an issue but hindsight is 20/20, and when you have issues at 6pm on a Friday, there's little you can do. We were able to contact our travel agent and he got on the phone with them but they wouldn't budge and we had to pay with another credit card even though our reservation was paid two weeks prior. By paid, I mean we showed them that we paid and everything, but they were not having it nor did they show payment. This was weird because they did refund the travel agent's card within 24 hours(very shady), but my suggestion to you is to pay for it yourself. Also, try not to check in on a Friday. Had to wait in line to be seen, you get the false impression that it's going to be fast but all their welcome ambassadors are doing is letting the front desk know you're there. After the payment fiasco(more to come on this) they want you to sit down so they can upsell you, even though when you book online you took care of it all. I didn't know they did timeshares, or I might have chosen another resort.

The staff
Maids, room service, pool service, bartenders, waiters, all were outstanding. Always smiling and always willing to help. Our maid did an exceptional job everyday, she even arranged my daughters dolls in her bed after she made it. The front desk customer service SUCKS. They can't break a $5 bill for you if you needed to and they wouldn't do anything to try and find change. That seems weird doesn't it? Any hotel I've ever been to has some petty cash.  I'd give most of the staff 4 stars and the front desk 0 stars. If you're not the high level, whatever it's called, you're not really given much attention. 

Restaurants/Food
For the restaurants, you need a reservation. My wife made 3 reservations, and none of those, even though she had email confirmation, had us on their list. I'm sure this happens often because the host/hostess didn't make a big deal about it. Enzo was our favorite, I wouldn't suggest any others. I can't tell you how underwhelmed we were with the food.  Mole was pretty good, but the food here isn't kid friendly. Air conditioning in the restaurants is non existent--you're going to sweat it out. I'd give this 2/5.

Beach/pool/activities
The beach was great, beautiful water. We didn't get there most days until 11 and all the chairs were taken. Even though signs say unattended chairs will have belongings moved, that's not enforced. Just like at the pool, once a towel is on a chair, it's occupied. Get to the pool and the beach early to stake your chair/area. If you do timeshares or whatever extra upgrades, you can get some really sweet cabanas at the pool and beach and if you pay that much and go that often, more power to you. I'd want that type of set up too. The main pool is good, pool bar and it's where most people go. The other pools just don't have energy. Service at the beach and pool are good whether you have a waiter or at the bar. Those guys at the bar earn their money, they're in constant motion. There was a lot of seaweed but I can't blame them for that. We went in the water and it was great. 
3.5/5

Rooms
We had two rooms and no complaints on either. To keep your room cool, you have to keep the drapes closed all day or the a/c just can't keep up.  4/5

Checkout
Nightmare. They charged our card when we checked in--I want to be clear on this that it wasn't a hold, that shows up different on my Amex. They didn't even show in their system they did that much, even though we showed them they charged us. Let's use logic for a moment--would any hotel let you check in without charging you or putting a hold on your card? Apparently the guy at the front desk wasn't using that logic or probably deals with this every day so he had a short temper. Wouldn't even get a supervisor. Wouldn't call Amex to verify they charged us. The company is based in Spain, that shows up on your credit card as well, so there must be some issue with systems or something. The check in for our Cabo stay was so much faster and more pleasant. We had to get charged again, and my wife casually mentioned if the charges weren't taken off, she'd dispute with our credit card company. The agent then said he could have her go to the ATM and pay the $4k in cash and threatened they could hold us there until we paid. 0/5

Don't stay here. Try somewhere else, a place that doesn't have any 1 star reviews. I believe them all 100%.

findings.title: Dianna L. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Let me start off with the good:

Beautiful landscaping
Scenery
Steak house 
Amazing hospitality 
Comfortable bed
Lounge was nice and cozy (although warm in that area)
Entertainment was ok 

The bad:

15 of 20 family members got sick during our 7 night stay
Sheets on beds were not changed during our stay
Food options were almost always the same every day
Had to get up at 5-6am to secure pool seats
Family member witnessed an employee not wash her hands after she entered the bathroom stall
Had to call daily to have fridge stocked even though there is a sign that clearly states they do this automatically 
Resort credit that we were suppose to receive at checkin was not received, we went back to get it and they said they were out and to come back.  Turns out they were coupons we could use for services at the hotel 

Overall I decided to give the hotel 3.  This was given mainly because of the waiter and waitresses.  The staff made us feel welcomed while we were there.

findings.title: Jennifer W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I came here for my 30th birthday and let me tell you from the moment I walked in I was in heaven! The scenery was just absolutely beautiful and breathtaking! It did however take some time to check in about (1 hour) but once it was done I dropped my luggage off in my room changed and went to tan! The drinks were amazing so was the food and staff! I'd definitely come here again.

findings.title: Sonia G. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Royal Paradisus Cancun 6/17-6/20,2019

CHECK-IN
The hotel has one main entrance (in contrast to Royal Paradisus at Playa del Carmen, which has its own entrance) so upon arrival, we "checked-in" with the hostess and were escorted to Tower 5 (Royal Service) for the actual check-in. Then we were escorted to another desk to get information about Royal Services and were introduced to our butler, Leyner. We reserved a suite with a lagoon view (due to availability), and fortunately a room with a partial ocean view was available, so we upgraded at no charge!

RESTAURANT REVIEW:
*Breakfast was best at La Palapa (very relaxing, good food and service)
*Naos buffet has everything you want but it's crowded, and there's a long wait for the omelet stations.
*Vento was not to our liking, small portions but the worst part was the AC wasn't working inside, so we ate in their open seating area (basically in the courtyard by the hallways and elevator/stairs)
*Blue Agave was good and quick! But you cannot go in with a swim suit and cover up, you have to be dressed.
*Bana is supposed to be good but we skipped it because it's in the middle of the building (no air conditioning)
*Fuego has the best dinners BUT even though we had a 7pm reservation, it took them 15 minutes to bring 1 small roll of bread, another 30 to bring our appetizers, and we got our main course at 8:15pm. The martinis were horrible!! I tried two: a dirty martini and an appletini. Probably the worst I've ever had. I could only take one sip of each.

ENTERTAINMENT REVIEW:
There's really only one bar with music to dance to, and that's Red Venue. All of the other bars listed on the website, are just a bar, so don't expect music or dancing.
*About Red Venue...we went two nights and the A/C wasn't working either night. But apparently they were prepared for this and pulled out a large stand up fan, placed by the front entrance and next to the bar, which made that area very congested. And if you were on the other side of the club, you didn't get ANY air.
Also, the place is obviously getting very little attention during the day: the chairs are smelly, the windows dirty, the carpet is filthy and there's a busted up chandelier full of dust hanging over the bar. Ew! I complained about the AC to a "manager" and he said they had already submitted a work request, and I suggested they at least bring in another fan!
On a positive note, DJ Noe was there Tuesday 6/18 and he's one of THE BEST DJ's I've ever experienced. He was taking song requests and dropping songs quickly. We had a BLAST!!!
*Avenue Bar has a bar and lounge area, but doesn't have A/C, and there were some singers there Monday night. 
*Coco's Bar is outdoors, facing the beach, so you have a nice breeze, however there wasn't any music playing there at night.

POOL REVIEW:
If you're staying at Royal, bali's (cabanas) are included, so make your reservation with the pool concierge upon arrival. We made the reservation through our butler but the concierge said they didn't get the message, and our butler said he submitted the request. Long story short: we were by the Royal pool Monday and Tuesday and facing the beach Wednesday and Thursday morning (only 5 Bali beds face the ocean and get a nice breeze). The Royal pool area is quiet and relaxing because it's adults only. If you want more of a party atmosphere, then you have to go to the main pool, but even though it's big, it is very chaotic and crowded. It's hard to find a place to sit!
Both pools are incredibly warm, like a warm bath...the ocean is far more refreshing! Also both pools need to have some cosmetic up keeping.

BEACH REVIEW:
The ocean had a considerable amount of seaweed and there was also a good amount of seaweed on the beach, close to the shoreline. Apparently seaweed is a problem along the Cancun coastline during the month of June, so if you are a beach lover, please keep this in mind. 

SPA REVIEW:
Regarding the Spa...be sure to go by and enjoy the hydra therapy pools. They're very relaxing!

findings.title: Edgar E. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Food sucked... couldn't wear a tank top to a buffet... overall bad experience with the food don't come here if you want to have food poisoning. Would highly recommend staying away from this resort.

findings.title: Danika F. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
This was my first time in Cancun and the Paradisus was amazing. From the rooms to the restaurants to the pool and beach, I had a great time and would highly recommend this all-inclusive resort to anyone. The staff was very helpful, whether it was the bartenders or guest services, who helped us book a night out and a day trip. The restaurants had good food - some better than others. I would highly recommend Fuego and Blue Agave. 

My biggest issue was with checking in. The entire process was not efficient or organized - they had our information/details wrong and there was confusion throughout the process. They also don't tell you about the towel card - to get a pool towel you turn in a card, then you have to turn the towel back in to get your card back. If you don't have the towel card when you check out they charge you a large fee. The problem is that they don't tell you that at all AND they put out bins for used towels to be dropped off, making it seem like you're supposed to just dump your towel.

I would definitely go back to Paridisus Cancun.

findings.title: Nicole O. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I recently stayed at the Paradisus 5/29-6/2 for my bachelorette party.  We upgraded to royal service when we got there and it was an amazing trip until our last night when apparently due to Cancun elections no alcohol could be served.  The hotel was aware of this a week prior yet the information wasn't relayed to us until we sat down for dinner on the last night. They said we could have drinks during dinner yet they were still giving us a hard time about it and would walk away and not come back till we asked again.  We were then treated horribly by the staff, specifically Sonya at mole and Karla in royal service.  Nobody offered us any apologies and any contact made with the hotel has been completely ignored. We were never notified of this government ban on alcohol so we paid for an all inclusive that was denied to us then treated like we weren't welcome at the hotel by every single staff member. There's so many other nice hotels in Cancun, I'd skip this one if you want to be treated with any sort of respect.

findings.title: Rodrigo A. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Great service at restaurants, pool, and beach. But at the front they need to step up their game. Horrible service with rude attitude. Customer service needs to be at its finest but not shown on our stay.

findings.title: Melissa R. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I've been waiting to write this review until we reached the end of our vacation. I wanted to see if my opinion would improve, but unfortunately it did not. Let me start off by saying we chose this hotel because of wonderful reviews, and we stayed there along with several family members because we got married near Cancun. The hotel itself is beautiful and well maintained. The pool is nice, beach is clean, rooms are fine. It is the staff that needs severe improvement in their attitudes. From the moment we checked in and told the guy at the front desk we were getting married and would be on our honeymoon we were received with blank stares and no feeling of welcome. The check in process was ridiculous and took much longer than needed. Someone spilled a glass of milk in our room when they dropped off room service and it took 15 minutes for another person to come with a new glass of milk, yet not to clean up the mess. Another 15 minutes passed and someone finally showed up. The day of our wedding I asked if they could please cut off our wrist bands because I did not want them in pictures. The guy at the front desk was hesitant to cut them off and said he needed to go ask. He said it might cost money. Huh? No congratulations regarding our wedding either. Standing outside waiting for our car to come pick us up, another man in one of the white uniforms asks me for my name and last name. I tell him, and he asks if I have checked into the hotel and I reply yes it's my wedding day (hence holding my wedding dress as well as my bridesmaids) and my shirt clearly said bride. He looks up and down at my bridesmaids and asks where their wristbands are and I explain to him that I'm getting married, we asked permission to cut them off and they are in our bags safe and sound. He rudely says "And are they getting married today also?" Indicating why they don't have their wrist bands on. He then asks for my name AGAIN and overall his demeanor was super rude. For the amount of money we paid to stay at this hotel we expected better treatment. The waiters were phenomenal as well as the staff pool side. But the people in the "white outfits" and front desk need to learn what the meaning of hospitality is. Check out was also horrendous and time consuming. For such a big hotel you would think they would have more than ONE single person checking people out. It's sad because overall we had a nice time but the attitudes of many people tarnished our view on this hotel. We will try a different hotel next time.

findings.title: Mia R. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
An all inclusive resort in Cancun! 

This review is based off of my stay with the upgrade to Royal Service. 
I only say this because I feel like the upgrade made a significant difference in my review. 
I came here for one of my life long friend's bachelorette weekend trip and I couldn't have asked for a better trip with these girls. 
In all honestly, I wasn't too sure what to expect. I've never been in an all-inclusive resort before. 
This place went above and beyond with service and experience. 
We checked in and although our rooms weren't ready at the time of our arrival, we joined the rest of our group for lunch while we waited for our room. 
With Royal Service there are some perks. Well, a lot of perks. 
Each group is assigned a personal butler. If you're international they set up a group chat on Whatsapp with your butler to make sure he's readily available for anything you would need or desire (Between the hours of 11-7, that is.) 
You also get access to a restricted pool area, access to a restaurant called La Palapa, secluded part of the beach and pool cabanas that are significantly easier to book than in other parts of the resort. 
Over the course of the weekend, we ventured off into the public pool area of the resort and there was a big difference. The main area is very family friendly, loud and rowdy. 
The Royal Service area was more relaxed and peaceful. 
This tone made all the difference. 
Royal service also includes premium liquors for all the drinks included with your stay. I'm sure there were more perks than this but this was really all we needed. 

If you're looking for a relaxing stay, I would recommend Paradisus. 
If you are considering upgrading to Royal Service, I recommend that, as well. Super worth it!

findings.title: Kevin C. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Came middle of May for 4 days for the Royal Service option. Forecast projected thunderstorms, but it only drizzled for half an hour the entire stay. 
Pros: food was above average for an all inclusive resort. Restaurant Tempo is a fine dining restaurant you have to pay additional but was amazing. Massage at Yihi spa you have to pay for but was also amazing. All staff was very friendly and accommodating. Service was excellent. Rain shower was nice in rooms. Royal service was a must. They had an exclusive section with food and drinks away from the masses. rooms were clean and above average decor.
Cons: Cocktails were average and were the same drinks no matter the bar or restaurant. The premium Liquor options were only slightly above average. No infinite pool. Beaches had a lot of seaweed, which obviously cannot be controlled due to climate change, and this is a problem at all the resorts in Cancun. The butler service part of the royal service seemed redundant. Dinner reservations were made for us and we were shown around the first day but that was about it. Only beer they had was Dos Equis and Heineken, no modela or corona. guacamole was bland. Soap and shampoo in the rooms were average. 
Overall, definitely recommend. For an all inclusive resort, it was worth the price.

findings.title: Jamerson W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We ended up here by accident. Cancún was actually just a launching point for Havana. Our original plan was to stay at the resort for two nights (one to sleep before heading to Chichen Itza and the other to sleep before heading to Havana). Because all of the flights were booked to the entire island and we didn't have a non-US credit card, we were stuck in Cancún for five days. And Gran Melia (as it was called back then) actually made our stay quite pleasant.

The resort was gorgeous. The pools were great. The service was good. The ocean was pristine. The weather was perfect. Even the sales pitch to get us into a timeshare wasn't terrible (and we got a really good breakfast buffet for our time). 

The thing I loved most though was the architecture. The exterior is designed to resemble the pyramids and inside has a rainforest motif. Based on what we heard from people staying at other resorts, we got quite a deal for a beautiful space in a great location. It was a bit far from all of the action (Punta Cancún) and from the city center (where all of the regular folks live with the plaza, supermarket, parks, etc), but the resort had just about everything you'd want if your goal was to relax on the beach all day. And we got around quite effectively using a combination of buses, taxis, and New Balance. 

On God, we'd never willingly go back to Cancún (it's just not our vibe). But, if we did go back, we'd definitely check out the Paradisus Cancún again.

findings.title: Doug H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Amazing Resort! Upgraded to the royal service with the junior suite ocean view and it was first class all the way. The interior of the resort was gorgeous with all the little details. The rooms were super clean and the balcony was very private overlooking the ocean. I've been to many all inclusive resorts and this place had some of the best food around. The entire staff was so friendly and made some delicious drinks. This is a family friendly place but also have an adults only side which is where the wife and I spent the majority of our fine during the day. So peaceful at both the pool and the beach. Nothing at all wrong with the family side as since we loved it so much, we talked about bringing our daughter back here in the future. I recommend this place to couples only and families of all sizes. My wife is extremely picky and she loved every second of the trip. If you're on the fence between a few places as I was myself when looking, don't think too much longer and book this place. You will not be disappointed.

findings.title: Christian B. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This resort has fantastic service. Everything is done fast and to your pleasure. However I would say that the restaurants and the food are very Disappointing. I feel their excellent service is to make up for the fact that they serve cheap, easy to make food that isn't very flavorful. All the restaurants get all their food from the exact same source so their isn't much Variety as you can tell if you go to all the restaurants like I did. Admittedly some food was good here and there but overall not very good. Alcohol was plentiful though which was appreciated.

findings.title: Emily D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Best Resort ever! Customer service is top of the line, the room we stayed in was gorgeous, and the minibar was well stocked. 

The ambiance of the resort the minute you walk makes you feel welcomed, relaxed, and already in paradise. 

The food was great. There's a buffet restaurant that had many options and everything laid out looked delicious. Being a vegetarian I felt I had many options to choose from (definitely a pro for me). 

The nightly events were a lot of fun! With different types of Performances one night, mini shops kiosks another night, and traditional Mayan and Mexican dance shows the last night we stayed. 

The service on the beach was pretty good but, at times kind of slow due to the many orders they had and the walk the servers had to make from the pool bar to the beach area. Only personal note I would add is, for a DJ booth and tiki bar at the beach area currently they are located at the pool area only. 

Finally, after our amazing stay here, we are sure to come back again! Thanks Paradisus for such an incredible time.

findings.title: Kate Z. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had the BEST visit!!! Went for a bachelorette party and we were taken care of let me tell you! Amazing service, gorgeous hotel, great food! Loved this place can't wait to go back!!

findings.title: Star S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed there for 4 nights in April 2019. 

Pros:clean, safe, location is great, beach is beautiful, and transportation outside of hotel. 

Cons: room Paid for was lagoon view, room given that faced another building. The rooms are set up is weird. We had room 4016, for them number in hundredth place means your floor number. 

Also staff is rude, they only come to ask for drink orders by the beach if they see you have your wallet. I set by the pool for 4 hours, I didn't get ask for any drinks but when my husband left his wallet with me, I had 3 staff stop by in 30 minutes to ask if I needed a drink. 

Also there are certain seating areas that have to be paid extra and reserved, cabanas and if you sit there, I had a staff member Jorge come up to me and tell me he covers that area and I need to pay or move in a rude fashion. Staff only smile when they see money, except their service feels poor. 


Food was okay, a lot of restaurants but average. Boring after few days of eating the same stuff. I wish they had more food at pool area except burgers and fries. 


Overall, Cancun's economy runs on tourism and that is very evident all around town.

findings.title: Gretchen K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: If I could give this place 0 stars, that would still be too many!! This place has nothing to do past 4 o'clock, and even though it's beautiful, is exclusively for people over the age of 60! If you are considering bringing your teenagers/kids here for spring break, I would beg you to reconsider, for their sake. The entire resort is excluding people who haven't payed extra for a butler, teenagers and young adults, and has the worst food I have ever tasted. Their pizza genuinely tastes like play dough. Even though you have to pay for an all-inclusive stay, it's a $5 room service charge, which adds up when there's nothing to do outside of your room past the crack of dawn. I'm very disappointed in my stay, and would not recommend this "resort" to anyone but my grandmother.

findings.title: Sana K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This place has the WORSE customer service that I have ever dealt with. Had to cancel my trip due to a medical emergency and was not able to get in contact with ANYONE at the resort after multiple emails and calls. Even provided the resort with a letter from my dr stating I could not fly last minute. They offered no customer service, no refunds, no transfer of funds to another resort, they weren't willing to do anything other than send me generic automated messages. Will No longer be booking with Melia resorts anywhere, not customer friendly or compassionate at all! Do not book here there are many better resorts out there!

findings.title: John G. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Summary - Great pool, beautiful beach, helpful waiters, very nice hotel rooms. Poor quality food, aggressive and annoying sales people: be prepared for a stay in a comfortable and well appointed room and for a relaxing time at the pool and beach, but also be firm at managing and walking away from the sales pitches people will constantly be giving you and brace yourself for bland and poorly cooked food that should be considered unacceptable for a resort of this quality.

We stayed at the Paradisus for 5 nights, overall we had a good stay. We upgraded to an ocean view room for $50 extra per night and thought it was totally worth it. We declined an upgrade to Royal Service since we didn't think we would use it and didn't want to spend time in the quiet adults-only section of the pool. There are many pros and cons to our experience, here are the most important ones:

Pros:

- Hotel aesthetics and decor: the hotel is designed nicely for a massive resort hotel and the decor is pleasing. The garden and koi ponds in the atrium are a plus as are the amounts of natural sunlight in the hotel.

- Room comfort and quality: the room was updated, clean, had a great A/C, excellent bathroom, and an amazing view with a very private balcony. The bed was comfortable and the drinks/waters we took from the refrigerator were replaced daily. 

- Pool and Beach: the pool(s) are great. They were never too crowded, have a swim up bar that we can easily access, and are clean. There is a shortage of pool chairs, so get to the pool early if you can OR reserve a Bali bed. We chose to reserve a Bali bed each day and it's worth it to have some private space, waiter service, and guaranteed shade. Beware that they will try to get you to pay for bottle service, a seafood platter, and snacks for $175 for the day. You can opt for just the Bali bed and a bottle of Prosecco for $60. The beach in front of the resort was kept very clean and was raked daily. There were usually plenty of beach chairs available. 

- Hotel Staff: the wait staff were friendly, eager to help, and very attentive to our needs. Their responsiveness to our needs and requests made a big difference in our stay. The front desk staff was mediocre and slow during check in and wouldn't give us answers to question we had and continuously decided to defer us to "guest services" (aka, pushy sales people who did at times provide helpful information).  

Cons:

- Food: this is by far our biggest complaint. This resort is a culinary mess! The food was absolutely terrible and the blandest stuff on earth. It's like it was made for a person whose palate requires zero flavor, zero seasoning, and no spice. The Naos Restaurant buffet had a lot of poor quality selections that were obviously not fresh, had obviously been sitting out all day, and were from reused pieces of leftovers from prior meals or the prior day(s). It was a challenge to make a reservation at any of the specialty restaurants and it could only be done prior to 5pm on the same day by calling from your hotel room. While they claimed that they were nearly booked solid and they had only limited availability at many of the restaurants, we noticed that they were only about half full. A few that I'm going to call out:
- Restaurant Blue Agave: tacos were very average and somewhat flavorless, I've had better at countless places in the United States. 
-Restaurant Fuego: they claim to be a restaurant that has spicy Latin American cuisine, but each of our dishes was mild with no heat and little to no seasoning. 
- Restaurant Enso: almost none of their main dishes on the menu were what they claimed to be (for instance, spicy Pad Thai does not consist of Italian linguine noodles mixed with a few vegetables and peanuts in a flavorless brown broth). That wait staff was great here and picked out a super bottle of wine for us, so that made up for the horribly misleading/false menu.

- Aggressive and Annoying Sales People: everyone from the people handing out beach towels and info on extra activities, to the guest services concierge rep, to the front desk staff is focused on a hard upsell. They are persistent to the point where they are annoying and offensive. Be blunt and do not let the "guest services" rep badger you, walk away. 

Overall it was a pleasurable and worthwhile trip and we had a great time. I simply warn future Paradisus visitors to be blunt with the sales/service folks and not to engage in conversation with them.  Also, don't expect a culinary adventure. It's a place that's great for those who looking for a comfortable and relaxing beach visit.

findings.title: Sarah R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I booked this vacation with nothing but ease on Cheap Caribbean after being hesitant since I've never planned a vaca on my own before. The website promotes daily deals & other offers that would attract just about anyone who needs/wants a getaway. After finding Paradisus Cancun there was no doubt in my mind we would be staying there. Once the trip was booked, I called the hotel to see if we could be upgraded- I wanted the trip to be as special as possible for my significant other & I since this was our first big vacation together. They offered Royal Service at the resort which allows you to stay in a private section of the resort with access to private pools, bali beds & exclusivity to specific restaurants. I said yes without hesitation which surprisingly only cost us a few hundred extra dollars. We arrived at the resort & were escorted to Royal Service where we were checked in & promptly greeted by a gentleman who sat us down & explained the whole resort to us & gave us a map of the property. We were then greeted by our butler, Maria who took us to La Palapa for lunch (most stunning views you'll ever see) while our room was being prepared. We were told we couldn't get to our room until 3PM but within an hour we were in & already in heaven. The view from our room was PERFECT as we could see the beach/ocean & sunrise each morning. Maria was nothing short of spectacular..... she made all of our dinner reservations, reserved our bali bed by the pool & when she discovered we got engaged on her day off, she made sure to go above and beyond and send chocolate covered strawberries, champagne & a beautiful hand-written card congratulating us to our room. When I say that Royal Service is 1000% worth the money, you will never experience better service than we experienced here. Every single person we interacted with was kind, helpful & always willing to go above and beyond for anything we needed down to towels. This was our dream vacation through and through and the best part of it all was we got engaged here. This resort will be a part of our lives forever & we will absolutely be back very very soon. Thank you again to MARIA in Royal Service for being incredible along with the entire staff at Paradisus Cancun.

findings.title: Jai L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Greeted by attendants upon arrival. They may be too talkative but helpful. Info provided in a brochure, what's off limits and what's not. We have the all-inclusive package which is good if you intend to stay on the resort. Clean rooms and bathrooms. Tons of restaurants and bars, including the buffet at Naos. The breakfast buffet food was not good, neither is the room service food. Always live entertainment during the daytime and nighttime. There are no activities, but you can walk right across the street for water sports, etc. Theres a bus stop as well in front of the hotel. I cannot think of anything I did not enjoy.

findings.title: Amy D. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Alex and I just got back from the sunny Cancun. Getting away from the snowy D.C. was sensational. We stayed at the Paradisus all inclusive. We chose this hotel because it was gorgeous online and had plenty of restaurant options. Here are the pros and cons of our trip:

Pros: 
1. Aesthetically: gorgeous hotel. The greenery, flowers and koi in the ponds all around the resort are exquisite. The layout is beautiful and it's right on the water. Looks just like the pictures online. 
2. Staff is so attentive and nice. While being there we learned about countless servers/bartenders/staffs families, where they are from and their way of life. There are plenty of people to help you out or just get you a drink! Every meal we had we had a friendly server who spoke English very well and was outstanding! Daniel was an incredible manager who really cared about his staff and cared about the guests. One morning I even asked for some citrus for my gin and tonic and he brought ALL the citrus LOL. Also, Edgar was very good as well. He was very attentive and kind, always going the extra mile. These two made the entire trip awesome!
3. Alcohol: free flowing. If you would like a bottle for the room you can just ask downstairs and they will give it to you with cups to enjoy on your balcony. My favorite was the Hendricks G&T (double) with a lime and an orange.
4. Restaurants: Fuego delicious (see pictures). Enso meh. Mole ok too good. Will have more individual reviews on their Yelp pages.

Cons:
1. While there are a lot of pools, there aren't a lot of pool chairs. We are not morning people, but forced waking up around 8:30 just to get a spot around the pool. 
2. Clientele: Rudest people I have ever encountered. EVERYONE staying at this hotel was a jerk. Most self indulged and insufferable people I've ever encountered, all in one place. I have been to Mexico several times, including another all-inclusive and never seen such ugly hearted people. I don't know if this is due to the cultures the brand attracts or because it was high season so the amount of people attracted to Cancun was higher, I can't pinpoint it. You are on vacation people, this is supposed to be the most relaxing time!!   
3. BIGGEST CON: Restaurants. As I said it was high season and every night 3 of the 7 restaurants are closed. Not to mention, it is IMPOSSIBLE to get a reservation. When we checked in we mentioned we had attempted to email reservations and was told you can only reserve from your hotel phone. We called as soon as reaching the room Saturday afternoon and all reservations were full until after our departure on Tuesday. This seems non-sensical. Either have a way to make reservations ahead of time and set aside tables for walk-in's or don't have reservations at all. Somehow later we snagged a 9pm at Mole on Monday night and half of the tables in the restaurant are empty. We also noticed this when walking by Vento. Thank God we did the Royal Service upgrade when arriving because we ate at La Palapa for nearly every lunch and thoroughly enjoyed the La Palapa lounge for snacks and drinks in the evenings. P.S. Tempo is $90pp extra, we cancelled. Tip: The hotel should provide a brochure of operating hours, what meals you can get at which and which you have to pay extra for.
4. Speaking of paying extra: This place is terrible with the upsell's, every corner we turned, upsell, upsell, upsell. Sat thru their timeshare presentation and the rates were awful; 50 vacations for 30K at 16.9%. As money savvy people no one in their right mind would take this. As soon as they realized we weren't going to buy they were done with us.
5. Lastly, Maid Service: minibar not stocked, no water in the rooms and no robes or slippers. Saturday, Sunday and Monday morning none of this existed. Maid came once a day and on Sunday, I even laid out a tip with a note about these things and when we arrived back from the pool nothing was there and the money was not taken... maybe the maid didn't read/speak English... not sure. Then miraculously, Monday we walked into our room and there were robes/towels and lots of water; money and note gone. Then while we were relaxing on the balcony we get a knock on the door and its the maid ready to do turn down service (wha? turn down service is a thing on our last night?!). She turns down and leaves we walk in and there are now more items and chocolates on our pillows, where the heck has this been the whole time?! Service is so spotty, but we chalked it up to being in Mexico!

Last tip before I leave you: They don't tell you but I realized the last day, when I was full out itchy, that the toilet paper is scented. May be a nice perk for some folks but unfortunately for a girl with a scent sensitivity would have been a great heads up! 

All and all was a nice time, but had we been given the level of service that was shown on Monday after 3pm and restaurants weren't such a disaster to make a reservation at we would likely be back.

findings.title: Jane D. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
All and all food sucks, staffs mostly aloof and powerless to change any given situation and if you're not a "member prospect" I think they'd rather you just go.

Security is nice and tight. Upcharge game too. 

The beach and the entertainment are great we had a lot of fun... I don't know it just lacks a brand and accompanying cutler? Something is missing. 

The cabana staff and spa folks -- superb.

We never got some of the "perks" we were offered and the staff made us feel bad for asking so we didn't.

If someone from the hotel wants to reach out I'm happy to review.

findings.title: Cara H. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We choose this time and location due to the desire to travel with friends who are owners.  Our reservation was for a King room on the ocean side.  When we checked in there weren't any king rooms available.  After seeing a few options we opted to keep our room and have the beds put together.  The first two nights were wonderful.  On the 3rd day a group of 600 conference attendees arrived.  During lunch the entire group came into the buffet at the same time and took over the restaurant.  They removed plates from tables that were occupied in order to be able to be seated.  Granted this wasn't their problem as the hotel and the conference planner should have had the fore-site to accommodate the attendees while avoiding interruption for the hotel guests.  The conference attendees were rude and pushed hotel guests out of the way in order to get their food first.  we decided to let this go and move on.  However that evening, the Red Lounge which stays open until 2:00 AM stepped it up a notch to entertain the attendees.  As mentioned before we had no issues the first two nights despite being in building 3 which is where the clubs are located.  The first night that the attendees were present the DJ turned it up and the attendees were so disruptive that we complained.  The manager on duty, Alejandro chose to do nothing despite the fact that the concierge admitted that they were trying to get the music turned down and the security guard said it was out of control.  Alejandro was rude and dismissive to us as we are females  The following morning we were moved to an "owner" building and given bracelets which allowed us to go to the adults only portion of the resort.  The front desk admitted the situation was handled poorly.  This would have been great but our travel companions/owners did not have the same privileges so we did not partake in the benefits (with the exception of being moved to a more quiet building.  
Thinking that all the inconvenience was behind us we went about our way meeting other guests/owners and enjoying the resort.  One challenge is tipping all the wait staff and we were running out of pesos.  I had previously gone to the concierge and converted dollars to pesos.  Knowing that the staff appreciate american dollars I went to concierge and attempted to break $20.00 bills into smaller amounts to tip the staff.  I was informed that I needed to check with the bellhop or bar staff.  the bellhop didn't have enough so I asked  front desk to again convert dollars to pesos.  I was informed by Guadalupe that  i would need to go downstairs in order to do so.  Mind you we had already done it at the desk as had our friends.  In my frustration I returned to Bana where we were eating dinner and the manager noticing my frustration immediately was able to get me smaller american dollars.  The next day I went to the front desk and brought the situation to their attention.  The day manager was out ill so they said they would take it up with her the next day and let me know what the plan was.  Today (Friday) we went to the front desk and after several go rounds with Margarita were informed that because we signed off for an upgrade on the noise level that nothing more would be done.  We were also informed that they were having trouble with the front desk staff and that the general manager was addressing it.  Neither the manager nor the general manager contacted us nor have they made any efforts to address the situation.  I was a previous owner at ME Cabo and can tell you that I would not recommend the resort to anyone until the management and front desk staff get their stuff in order and figure out that customer service means putting the customer first.  
Before any nay sayers respond, this is my 7th stay at a Melia resort, I paid full price, and have confirmed with the owners we are traveling with as well as the ones we have met that this is not appropriate.

findings.title: Joshua S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My wife and I spent our honeymoon at Paradisus in Cancun and it was an amazing experience. Relatively affordable, luxurious, relaxing, and fun!

Paradisus is an all-inclusive resort that has an all-ages family section and an adults only section.  We stayed in the adults only section, which is called Royal Service.  The resort has many restaurants, three pools, multiple bars, various activities throughout the day, and gorgeous decor.

As soon as you walk into the hotel, you notice the beautiful design.  There is foliage hanging from the walls and levels, trees throughout the indoor spaces, streams and ponds filled with koi, and incense burning.  During the day, the lights are all off and the giant skylights provide great natural lighting.  At night, hanging lights give a great vibe.  It really is gorgeous.

Royal Service comes with some really nice perks as well.  To start, transportation to and from the airport is included, and when you arrive at the hotel, your luggage is collected and delivered to your room so you don't need to carry it through the hotel, which is quite large.  You also get a personal butler that guides you through personalized check-in.  Entering the hotel, you see long lines of guests checking in.  In Royal Service, that doesn't exist.  They do it for you.  They give you sparkling wine while you wait. Super nice.

In Royal Service, there is also a private lounge with a private top-shelf bar all day long, fancy appetizers and desserts until 10pm, and a breakfast buffet every morning.  There is always a staff member at the bar to make you a cappucino or cocktail or anything else you want.  And they are super helfpul and generous; my wife ordered a drink and they didn't have the ingredients on hand but they offered to go get them and make it.  We declined because that was too much effort and had another delicious cocktail.

Royal Service also has a private restaurant: La Palapa.  La Palapa is open for breakfast and lunch and, only recently, for dinner.  This restaurant is a huge perk for Royal Service guests.  The breakfast there is AMAZING. Get the french toast. And the churros.  Breakfast options at the rest of the resort are pretty limited; a buffet with food that honestly doesn't look amazing.  We though La Palapa would have the same food, but it was completely different, freshly made at La Palapa rather than at a shared kitchen for the buffet, and the food was all delicious.  The restaurant is outside between the pool and the beach, giving you great views of the ocean.  Birds are very eager to get any falling food, so watch out for them.

Royal Service also has a private pool with little cabanas you can reserve free each day.  The cabanas have waiter service too, so you can be lounging and order really delicious food and cocktails without having to get up.  The food is really quite good; I recommend the tuna skewers and the nachos.

We had such a fun and relaxing time at Paradisus.  We were in the ocean and pools every day. We used their spa everyday, as well.  The spa has a hydrotherapy pool (a bit cold), saunas, steamrooms, and massaging shower rooms that are all free to use.  And we finished every day with a bubble bath prepared by our butler, and he always left the room with a bottle of sparkling wine, some desserts, and decorated with flower petals.  We simply had to message him during the day that we wanted a bath and it would be ready for us when we arrived at the room at night.

Neither of us wanted to go home after our stay.  It was the perfect honeymoon with great food, drinks, service, fun, and relaxation.

findings.title: Mohammed A. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I dont know where to start from:
1-Check in: it took about an hour to check in,room wasn't ready and we had to wait.
2-room:alot of ants on the floor and on the mini bar,i called three times in the beginning they said will change the room or will clean it,in the end they sent somebody with spray for ants to clean it,and still coming out and i was cleaning it for the whole stay.
3-fridge:they dont fill up the fridge with water at least unless you request( all inclusive hotel) !!!
I called one time to request and the front desk told me we dont restock the fridge and on pardisus website says we restock your fridge everyday!!!
4-safe box: it wasnt working and need to be programmed,somebody came on the first day to fix it and he said you cant set up a code you just need to use your room keys to close and open,the second time missed up he came and set up a code!!!
5-front desk:you need to spend 10 min at least to reach them,and sometimes need to call the room service to let the front desk answer your phone call!!
6-food:all inclusive hotel means eat whatever you want whenever you want but the reality its not,you have to make a reservation for the dinner a day before and in the end they tell you its full so you can go and eat from the buffet! Disgusting food.
One of the days we ate in blueagave its a tacos restaurant,my wife found a staple in the quesadilla!! The waitress came and saw that and he call the manager and everybody saw that we left,and I ignored what happend but after all of that happend to me I decided to complain for the manager,i talked to a manager his name is alex and said im going right now to the restaurant and i will call you back,he called back after saying that i meet the manager of the restaurant and he said nothing happened in the restaurant like that!!! Alex ignored and he believed the restaurant manager!!
The most disgusting i saw while i was setting on the beach,i saw one of waitress there picking up the plastic cups from the trash cane and take them back to the bar on the beach!!! 
I have more to say,but its enough for now,i will make sure that nobody go there from people i know.
And its not the end with Paradisus,i know how to get my right back.
Thanks for the worse staying in Mexico ever.

findings.title: Sahil M. (1/5)
findings.snippet: As an update, I would never recommend this place. We've had a string is awful meals and poor service. The entire experience has been atrocious and not even close to our other experiences in cancun. Even the buffet is empty half the time

findings.title: Karina O. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
So I totally forgot to write a review when we went back in August but here's alllll the tea! It was my fiancé and I first time in Cancun and our first time in an all inclusive resort. We got a little boujee and got the royal service package from just reading the reviews a lot of people either love it or hate it. We LOVED IT. It came with an absolutely stunning room and view and let's not forget the butler it came with. Shout out to Jesus for taking care of us ! He was amazing like completely amazing my fiancé's eye ended up getting infected and this man went to the pharmacy for us and got him medicine like we were soooo heart felt and definitely tipped him very well after that. We felt right at home. 

The food was a solid 3.5 out of 5 it was good not omg amazing but good. I mean I wasn't expecting a 5 star meal every time. There was so many restaurants on resort that we unfortunately didn't get to taste everything. 


With royal service we got the Bali beds on the adult side for free. Just had to call Jesus in the morning to book it for us. The food on the adult side was actually really good the spring rolls were A1!

Each night they had shows which was pretty cool. They have a on resort club. Played a lot of American music so like the top 50's which was nice wish the dj would of played more Latin music or mixed it up a bit. But it was fun drinks were good. They get even better if your tipping well. They also have a beach club outside with hookah you have to pay out of pocket for hookah but it was only like $15 bucks. That was almost my favorite part I mean drinks, hookah and sitting on the beach watching the waves doesn't get better then that. 

On our last night we came back to the room to a surprise, a bottle of champagne and chocolate covered strawberries such a cute and nice touch made us feel so loved

Overall I would definitely recommend Paradisus to anybody! We loved it and are excited to come back !

findings.title: Alison W. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Had a wonderful experience here. The staff was super friendly and super attentive. We paid for the butler service, which was a nice extra and having the private pool and beach area was well worth the extra money.  The private pool/beach area was quiet and peaceful and we never had a problem getting a bed by the beach/pool. We stayed 5 days and just booked another trip back there. I've traveled to Cancun about 9x's and this is by far the nicest resort. For me, I wouldn't bother going anywhere else. Money well spent

findings.title: Shanon T. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I went here in August for my sister's bachelorette party. It was most of our first time at an all-inclusive resort, so we were pretty excited. However, we were a little disappointed by the end of the trip. First off, the drinks were incredibly watered down. The number of drinks I had everyday probably should have killed me, but I didn't feel the slightest buzz. Secondly, the beach was nice except for the huge amounts of seaweed in the water. We expected crystal clear shores like the pictures showed, but it was just green muck everywhere. Also, the process of saving bali beds was tedious and made staying outside too hot without one. The food was okay, we expected better. The pool was by far the best part, and is where we spent most of our time. The rooms were very nice too. Overall, it was a good time because we made it one, but it definitely had potential to be better.

findings.title: Jennifer M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I stayed here for 3 nights and honestly had an amazing stay here. When I comes to hotels and staying somewhere, I don't ask for much: a clean room, good service, and a clean building. Of course, being a resort, this place far exceeded what I needed. 
I picked this place since it had good reviews and I also found an amazing deal online as well. The building itself is massive; there's 5 pyramids connected together. Inside the lobby is pristine and has a nice smell of incense throughout. The people at the desk were very nice and accommodating, and spoke English when needed. We were shown around the resort while we waited for our room to be ready, and were offered a free rental car if we listened to their timeshare presentation. The place is covered in hanging plants, which I thought looked amazing!
When our room was ready, we found it to be nice and chilled, clean, and had an AMAZING view of the ocean! The balconies are quite private. We had absolutely no problem with our AC in the room. 
The restaurants here at Paradisus were good. They offered breakfast buffets, then switched into lunch. Getting a table during breakfast and lunch was no problem, however you had to wait a bit to get a table during dinner since everyone was there to eat. Overall, the food offered was decent; we definitely had our share of favorites and dislikes. Good thing they have 8 restaurants!
The pools were clean and well maintained,  and the swim up bar was super chill. During the day, we had no problem finding a chair, there were plenty offered. The only downside was you had to rent the cabanas, which to me is no problem. There were shows at night, sometimes outside by the pool or inside in the bar.
Overall, I had a great time here. Its definitely family friendly if you want to bring your kids. We are planning to come back to Cancún in the near future, and plan on staying at this resort.

findings.title: Duandala V. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
First arrived... And not impressed. Our room is not ready for 1 thing, they walked us over to one of restaurants blueagave, and to no availability.. nobody served us after 10 minutes of waiting... With no instructions on what we need to do or anything. So we walked out and went to the buffet NAOS..  OH... the huge variety of the blandest food all in one place. Even a zucchini didn't taste like a zucchini anymore. It's as if they have a bland spice they use on all the food. Ugh... Friendly?? Seems more like they are looking for tips verses being genuinely nice.  3 more days of this... I'm afraid it's not going to get any better.   To be continued .. but I'm not just unimpressed.. I'm pretty upset.

There was no one to show us to our room, and everything is so commercialized!  Your treatment will be based on your package class...  I can easily upgrade but rather not put anymore money into this resort than I have. I'm itching to leave the resort tomorrow to eat an actual good or decent meal.  That upgrade unfortunately won't fix their nasty tasteless food.  I fear this post will just add by the day.

Day 2.. we had tried blueagave again as we really wanted some tacos, and Richardo had definitely made up for the previous day. Tacos were good and the passion fruit margarita was delish. We told him about our previous experience and he apologized and sang us a song.  So I went up another star for the resort. As I still find it very commercialized, segregated bte package class, no resort activities and bad food.

findings.title: Dundy V. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Just arrived... And not impressed. Our room is not ready for 1 thing, they walked us over to one of restaurants blueagave, and to no availability.. nobody served us after 10 minutes of waiting... With no instructions on what we need to do or anything. So we walked out and went to the buffet NAOS..  OH... the huge variety of the blandest food all in one place. Even a zucchini didn't taste like a zucchini anymore. It's as if they have a bland spice they use on all the food. Ugh... Friendly??
