This person will ensure your stay is great, and will go to great lengths to make sure you want for nothing. Ours was Juan, and he was awesome and I will most certainly be requesting him next year. I cant recommend this resort high enough, if you have any questions feel free to ask.

http://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g150807-d282106-r345819230-Paradisus_Cancun-Cancun_Yucatan_Peninsula.html#

findings.title: Toshira S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Excellent hotel.  The staff were amazing.  TURQUOISE waters.  Excellent service.  Food was delicious.  Love this hotel.

findings.title: Wendy T. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed here mid December for 6 nights and I'm already having major withdrawals. I seriously cannot wait to come back. I've been bugging my boyfriend for the past month about booking our next trip to cancun. 

We booked our trip online including airfare and transportation to the resort. When we arrived, all the staff was so friendly and treated us like royalty. We decided to go with the royal service option while booking, which I highly recommend. For the Royal service, you get a butler during your stay. Our butler was Juan and he took care of us during our whole trip. He welcomed us with desserts and rose petals when we arrived, and on our last day he surprised us with a champagne bottle and a rose petal bubble bath. Thank you Juan!!  Anything from restaurant, Bali bed, cooking class reservations, he took care of it! It made everything more stress free since I heard from other reviews that it was difficult to get reservations. Juan was able to get us dinner reservations every night. I really recommend Mole, we went there twice during our stay! 

Royal service has its perks, it's a separate area from the rest of the resort. There's a Royal service lounge where they serve breakfast, snacks and desserts all day, along with a premium bar! My boyfriend and I probably killed 2 bottles of Hennessy during our stay from all the henny and coke's we ordered. No shame at all...... 

Aside from the lounge, you have a pool area for Royal service guests only. There you can find the Bali beds/ cabana where you can reserve for the day for no charge! I believe for regular guests there is a fee. Free towels, sunscreen, tanning oil etc. We were able to reserve it for 3 days during our stay. There is also a restaurant for Royal service guests only called La Palapa, it's near the pool area! We didn't know about this until our second to last day here. I wish we knew sooner because the food there was amazing!! Everything here was made fresh. We literally ate there for breakfast lunch and dinner on our last day lol

Now the cons.. 
- The food/restaurant options were okay, or maybe I was expecting everything to be bomb. The only two restaurants I would really recommend are Mole, Naos (breakfast only) and La Palapa. All the others were mehhh.... (fuego, blue agave, market grill, vento) 
- Room service was extremely slow.. Took about 45 minutes to an hour for food to arrive
- The toilet seat in our room was flimsy but could've just been our room
- One of my makeup products went missing. I should've put everything away before leaving the room. Kinda bummed, but whatever. 

Overall the resort was wonderful & staff was great!! I would definitely stay here again! Shout out to our butler Juan and the extremely friendly servers at Naos, U da real MVP's!

findings.title: Gudia A. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We just came back from spending 6 nights here in tower 3: 

The good:

- the resort is beautiful inside and out. Very well maintained. The ambience is great with the flower walls in all towers.  The pools were clean and nice and the beach area was great as well. 

Not so good: 

- they really need to turn down that incense they have going inside. I didn't notice it so much in other towers but it was very strong in tower 3 at times I got a headache. 

- their reservation system is horrible for restaurants. They only allow u to make reservation for same day and next day but not beyond that. We stayed for 6 nights and would have liked to book it at one shot for all the days at all restaurants. The staff at restaurants needs to be more friendly with families with kids. Also some days, all restaurants can get completely booked. So you r left at buffet which can get old fast. 

- the room service was so-so. My q tips and makeup wipes were not replenished after the first day. The towels were not always adequate and need to provide small towels as well. 

- the acoustics in tower 3 were horrible with respect to night time entertainment. We heard everything very loudly in our room till around maybe atleast 10pm. They need to find a way to change that. So people can enjoy the quiet.

findings.title: Nora C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We spent one week at this hotel recently.  I give it a SOLID three stars.  I read hundreds of hotel reviews before selecting this one.  The bottom line is that it is nearly impossible to get everything you want in a hotel.  I have to say that Paradisus for the most part met my expectations.  I will also gladly recommend the hotel to family and friends.  We purchased the general all inclusive package.

THE GOOD

-The staff are extremely friendly and always of service.  From our check in to food and room service, all staff were professional and courteous.

-The hotel is not only big, but it is long, which means you have access to a long stretch of beach.

-Buffet food is always fresh, full of flavor and area is kept clean and food is replenished in a timely manner.

-The Vacation Club Melia staff are friendly, not at all pushy if you aren't interested in joining vacation club.

-The decor and and the overall ambiance of the hotel is stunning!  I enjoyed walking through the main pyramid and smelling the soothing aromas, hearing the calming zen like music, and appreciating the unique decorative pieces throughout the hotel.  I also enjoyed hearing the fountains and the ocean from my room everyday.

-If you want to relax in the comfort of your room, order room service!  We planned a day trip to Isla Mujeres and opted for room service for breakfast.  Within 30 minutes of ordering we received our order.  The presentation was nice and the food was delicious!

THE ROOM FOR IMPROVEMENT

-The policy for reserving beach chairs either needs to be enforced or thrown out altogether.  If you go out at 630 am to reserve chairs, nearly all are taken!The policy is such that if you are not at your lounge chair for 30 minutes staff can remove your personal items so that other hotel guests can use the chairs.  Make up your mind Paradisus management!   

-The kids club feels like an afterthought.  On paper, there is a nice, balanced schedule of activities, but we did not choose to leave our kids there for several reasons: 1) kids 5-12 are lumped together in the same not so big room with about 6 activity/toy stations and a jumper.  I walked in twice.  There were 2-3 staff there with as many as 40 children!  
2) There is an iffy system of identifying children who are part of the kids club for outdoor activities--there was an outdoor treasure hunt activity one afternoon.  When I asked staff how children from the kids club would be tracked as they walked through the hotel grounds I was told that the kids were identified by paint on their face.  How about a matching bracelet for kids and parents?
3) A majority of activities are indoors, and the kids zone room is dark with no windows.  We are in Cancun!  Have activities outside!  There seems to be a large underutilized space where the playground is.  Put a big palapa over this area and create a fun outdoor space with a water tables, water slides, etc so kids aren't enclosed in the existing claustrophobic space.

-As big as the hotel's oceanfront is, you can't enjoy swimming in the ocean as the ocean is rough. The  red warning flags were up the entire week we were at the resort.  Based on tripadvisor reviews the red flags have been up since May.  Not fault of hotel..its Mother Nature..but something for you to consider if you enjoy swimming in the ocean or you have small kids.

TIPS
1. Lounge chairs- have someone in your group reserve chairs in the early am--as early as midnight for the next day.  Place Paradisus towels, cheap flip flops, beach bags on your chairs.  

2. Make reservations at Fuego and Mole!  These restaurants, in particular, have amazing food.  Be curious!  Try food you'd typically never order and you'll be surprised at how delicious every item on these menus are.  (Make reservation the day before)

3. Go to the Market Grill restaurant for lunch.  The restaurant has an ocean view, no reservations are required, and the food is fresh, healthy and made to order.  The kids loved the pasta and pizza.  The adults enjoyed the salads, the shrimp skewers and the sides.  

4. Be persistent!  We purchased the junior oceanfront suite.  The room we were given was in the 3rd pyramid and had a view of the roof of the Market Grill restaurant.  After seeing this we asked the hotel staff for a complete ocean view room, as we had purchased.  The hotel management offered us other rooms but these had issues as well- one room had outdated light fixtures and decor, the other had a leaky air conditioner.  Needless to say, we ended up staying in the room with the partial ocean view for one night.  The next day we were given another room in the 3rd pyramid which had a complete ocean view and updated furniture, fixtures.  For the inconvenience the hotel management made dinner reservations to 2 restaurants for us.

5. Go to breakfast early!   Anytime after 10 am you'll have to wait in line to get seated, wait in line for the omelet station, and the juice bar...and lines get long

findings.title: Scott G. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Keep in mind it's so bad that I am writing this during my actual vacation. Here now in room 3712, room is actually nice and beach location great hence the two stars. 

However everything is below average across the board. Desperately trying to check out and move to the Paradisus Playa Del Carmen. 

Will write a comprehensive review upon return.

findings.title: Danny J. (4/5)
findings.snippet: This isn't the resort to go to if you're looking for s spring break kind of a vibe. If you get the royal service they treat you like royalty (seriously). We were offered drinks every other minute from when we were around the pool to when we were having breakfast in Naos. It was a nice place to just get away and relax but also drink till you can't anymore. All the restaurants were pretty solid.

findings.title: Jessica L. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Generally had a great stay except for the first and last day and losing my jacket. I really wanted to have this review be great but felt I had to call out a few things.

Had to move rooms the first night due to my room flooding (it was raining cats and dogs and I don't think the hotel was made for rain.) 

The last day, though the hotel is all-inclusive, I was charged for lunch...which I was communicated to me while I was halfway through eating. I think this was poorly handled and communicated to me as a guest.

Another thing was that as I was switching rooms I left my jacket in the old room and didn't realize it until I was packing (you don't really need jackets in Cancun.) I asked the front desk and no one had heard of my jacket or reported it...so I'm guessing it "disappeared." Again, hate to give a poor review but felt I needed to be honest.

findings.title: Local L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
All I got to say is WOW this place is a must stay resort I say this because one the food is great. We have been to other resorts all inclusive and the food is terrible but here at the Paradisus hotel
All of the restaurants are really good 
We first ate at Blue Agave awesome service wonderful then the next morning we tried out the buffet lots to choose from 
Egg omelettes to fresh fruit cereal etc
All the employees at the resort very well trained except for 2 incidents we had that just had us appalled we went down to the pool area and we did NOT get asked once if we needed a drink, we actually had to get up to walk to the bar every time.
And again we went up to the relaxing station near the bar area had 2 girls 
Waitresses just look at us with out greeting is 10/15/2015 6:40 pm
Didn't ask us if we needed anything 
30 min pass by  theirs a group of 10 that showed up next to us and the 2 waitresses were their to serve them
So my wife had called one of the virus over to ask if we needed to get up to ask for a drink and the girl replied no I could help you that's when my wife told her in a nice way in Spanish well you attended to that group and we have been sitting here for a while sh said oh sorry we didn't see you REALLY other than that this resort is beautiful little dim 
Rooms clean comfortable when we needed more toiletries we called the front desk & they answer good evening
 Mr. (Your last name) how could we serve you then they call you back to make sure if it's been delivered and if we needed more of their service at that time
Blue agave must go eat 
entertainment  every night at the hotel

findings.title: Mandi T. (4/5)
findings.snippet: My fiancé and I had a great get away to Cancun right after getting engaged. We choose this hotel based upon the price and reviews. This was our first time ever doing an all inclusive hotel we decided on Royal Services the adults only area of the hotel.                             Pros- gorgeous hotel room with a view of the beach! Bali bed we laid in by the pool was amazing. We loved the staff they are nice and accommodating. Free shuttle do and from the airport was great too. The fitness center was nice and had fresh towels and waters. We really liked the Asian restaurant Bana.                                                                   Cons- there is an air conditioning problem in the hotel it wasn't cool enough in the lobby or our hotel room. The food was average I think that's expected on an all inclusive. They could do more offer some variety and spices.                                                         It was really hot when we went on our vacation in September I may recommend a cooler time of year. There was also a lot of seaweed on the beach but, we hear that is not typical. I would recommend this hotel if you want an all inclusive (not sure that is our thing).

findings.title: Samantha C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The hotel was perfect!! My boyfriend and I got upgraded to Royal Service and was the best thing that happened. We had private pool, which was adult only, cabana's, a butler, a private restaurant that served amazing breakfast lunch and dinner. The  hotel had maybe about 8 restaurants. And I have zero complainants about any of them. Bana and Vento were my two favorites! I'm super picky with food, and I had nothing bad to say about any of the food. I hate buffet food and even the buffet restaurant they had there was amazing! Food was always fresh! The workers there were the nicest people ever! I stayed 7 nights 8 days, and still we were not ready to come home. 

There is one lounge, and the DJ was great every night. Nice crowd there every night. And there are a few other bars. Coco beach was really nice too, you could get hookahs there if you wanted to. Avenue was an awesome bar also! The same guys worked there that entire week we stayed, so it was nice to see the same face everyday, and they remembered you. 

There are 3 pools, not including the private royal service pool. They had a kiddie pool, a pool with a DJ and swim up bar, and then another pool. They pool with the DJ always had a nice crowd! Music was always great. If you stay in royal service, the only thing I recommend is that when you first get to the pool area on your first day, to book for the entire week to have a cabana. They get booked fast! Oh, and waking up very early to make dinner reservations! The hotel isn't too big so it's not annoying or tiring walking anywhere.  I would recommend this hotel to anyone! I can't wait to come back to Cancun to stay at this hotel again!

findings.title: Karine K. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Great hotel nice food and pools for kids. The pool side chairs are always full. Gets loud at night if your rooms are by the club area, we could not swim in the ocean at all but the pools took its place instead.

findings.title: Nait P. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Overall, we had a decent experience.  They need to get rid of Arturo at the towel hut in the Royal Service section (Pyramid 5).  His attitude is not in line with everyone else we encountered, and but for him, we would have had a much better experience and would be more likely to return/refer this place to friends.

findings.title: Ellie Q. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I want to give negative stars if I could! I was searching for a brunch place on yelp and Naos popped up as first on the list. So we drove there and found out this is an all inclusive hotel. One of the help desk people suggested to attend a 90 minute hotel information tour that includes a free breakfast. So that's what we did. We have a 1 year old toddler who was demanding for food at the moment. 

Breakfast was closing at Naos, so we quickly grabbed some food next door. I had very little food, because I was feeding and watching my toddler. The sales guy wanted to move quickly to the tour, so we rushed through breakfast. At that moment we realized this was a very bad choice! However nobody told us this tour was 3 hours long and it was not a good time for breakfast or lunch! All we wanted was a quick tour and enough food. Food tasted bad and dated by the way. It made my little one sick and he had a diarrhea from it!! 

The sales person was pushing us to buy their membership, another surprise! We thought this was a tour of the hotel, maybe next time we can come here for a vacation. Guess what? We would never ever choose your hotel or hotel chains in the future!!!! Worst hospitality ever!! I don't feel welcomed, why should I spend money and time with these people for the entire morning?!!!! Your tiny suites are not as half good as the one we chose, you don't even have ocean front, free standing vilas!! Lol...five stars? Are you kidding? All inclusive? I don't think I want to eat out dated food and make my family sick!

We asked several times that we want to leave, but they always have something to say! Baby needs nap, baby is sick, I have poops on my dress...they didn't even ask if we are ok. They kept us there for 3 hours, asking for money!!! 
At the end, they sales person asked if we were offered some day passes to use for doing this. I said no. We asked the manager, he was very reluctant to give us anything. We walked away with only a thought of avoid this hotel and any of its chains in the future!!!!!! Never return!!!! Run!!!!!

findings.title: Leana E. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Disclaimer: I have not stayed at this hotel, this is a review upon my visit last night.

First off, we walked to the hotel from our hotel which was just next door. It is a bit of a walk considering how many stairs we had to trek up since the hotel is up on a hill, but not bad. I wasn't panting like a puppy since the weather was better @ about 10:30pm. 

The reason why we visited this hotel was to eat at the Blue Agave. 

When we entered, zomgggg. The hotel looked phenomenal. It was so cool & exotic!!!!!! They have a coy fish pond & waterfall in the middle of the hotel, along with a wooden bridge to walk over. It was so serene & beautiful. I love the vibe the hotel gives. 

Another plus: They have so many restaurants to choose from!!!!!!!!

Wishing we would have stayed here instead of the Marriott lol. Since it was like a jungle in there, we got a little lost. The employee we asked was so kind & actually walked us down to Blue Agave! From what we encountered, service is A+++++

Blue Agave was amazing & not overpriced like many other restaurants we've experienced! Definitely a must eat.

findings.title: Steve R. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Had a wonderful time here. Very lovely climate and attentive staff. Was treated very nicely. Only spent a week here, but I can imagine it gets old not too long after that. Very touristy climate and everything was very expensive. 
Still had a very great time, all inclusive and amenities were top of the line.

findings.title: Ana D. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
As a return Paradisus/Club Melia member, I was pretty underwhelmed by the experience at this resort.  Although the hotel was  clean, it looks a bit nicer in pictures.  Additionally, while the staff was nice, the service was pretty average, and not what we have been used to in the past.  

Ultimately, many of the average ratings and reviews found on the internet for this resort are fairly up to par. We roomed in the main building - building three - which was noisy.  Our room wound up being infested with small flying insects that were beyond annoying.  Further, there were countless times that we dialed service numbers to make reservations, only to have them ring without answer or be put on hold for over ten minutes, and call back to find that all restaurants were booked.  By the third night we completely gave up and looked up places to go/dine on our own.  That was also a task, as the Wi-Fi here was extremely shotty and worked mainly in the lobby or outside by the pool and beach areas.  When we actually were able to get in contact with people for service, we were constantly repeating ourselves, not due to language barriers, but due to lack of attention. 

At the end of the day, it was nice to get away, but this particular resort experience wasn't worth it. Having been to Melia resorts as both regular guests and royal service guests, we know what the experience could be - they've gone from amazing to outstanding.  Those who say paying for royal service at this resort changes everything must not have been to some of the other Melia properties.

findings.title: Samantha R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: So I would have to say I was really expecting much more from this location. The best thing about this place is the lobby. It is quite beautiful BUT then you start to endure the lack of air conditioning! In the evenings it is very warm in the lobby and in the restaurants connected to the lobby. This needs to be fixed. We traveled with a few other families and one room the air conditioning leaked and the other room the AC didn't work. This to me in unacceptable! Also, you need reservations to restaurants that are 25% full. The food is mediocre at best. It isn't horrible but not really too good either. Actually we just walked out of of Blue Agave because the service was soooo horrible. We vacation in Mexico twice a year and know that service is slower than the states but this service was just plain BAD. Also, the entertainment is seriously lacking. Our kids had their friends to hang out with but asked why this location didn't have activities or entertainment. Also, you can't get a latte on the property. The kicker is they have a machine but it is in a bar that doesn't open until 4. When I requested a latte they said the machine was out of order. Our room was clean but we had a patio with no patio furniture. I read this in the reviews but still find it odd to have so much space and no furniture to make it useful. Save your money and book some place else.

findings.title: Kendra B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My sister and I took our mom here for her 60th birthday. I was pleasantly surprised! The hotel was nice as were the people. The food was good and the service was excellent. Check in was a breeze and everything is explained. We had an all inclusive package which was nice. It included all except two restaurants. We were only there for the weekend so we opted not to hassle with reservations to the restaurants. You had to do them a day in advance which I read about online - it seemed to be more hassle than it was worth. We opted for the buffet at Naos each day which was always well stocked with options. Overall, the trip was great and we had a good time!

I notified them before arrival that we would be celebrating a birthday. They decorated our room and mom's bed with balloons and left her a cake. Really sweet. On our final night there, it was pretty comical but the waiter was drunk out of his mind! Again - hysterical! We went to the night club they have at the resort the night before mom's birthday. This was a lot of fun. The DJ was decent and played songs requested. 

I have to compliment the beach staff. Roger was absolutely amazing!! Such a sweet guy. He was so kind and was not looking for tips - which made me want to tip even more. Genuinely kind and accommodating. He kept ice cold water on hand and was always there if you needed anything. He served ice cold fruit popsicles around 1pm one afternoon - they were incredibly delightful! 

Overall great trip! The only reason I docked a star is because I had to call for them to service our room our first full day. While they would like guests to reuse sheets and towels if at all possible, I think it's absurd to come re-stock my mini bar and not make the beds and empty my trash. Around 6pm, I had to call to see if anyone planned to come clean. They came right away, but at 5 star hotels, this is not a request I've ever had to make. 

All else was good. If ever in Cancun check them out!

findings.title: Kim S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Royal Service ALL the way! Came to Cancun to celebrate mine and my friend Kamilla's birthday with my boyfriend and other friend, Heidi. From the get go we were treated like royalty. Check in was a breeze and right when you walk in you are greeted with champagne. One out of the two rooms we booked were ready so we hung out there before heading to the pool. We were hungry and ordered room service right after our butler Ivan explained everything to us. The room was nice with a king bed and a view of the lagoon which was nice. Our butler Ivan was really nice and attentive when we needed him, but we didn't see him much. The staff in the Royal service building were THE nicest people I have ever met! Nothing we asked for was out of reach. My friend Heidi and I drank Hennessy & Remy Martin which they didn't have out for guest, but they brought out for us since we asked, we felt pretty damn special after finishing 3 bottles in a days span (DONT' judge us lol) ! The breakfast buffet they put out in the morning is pretty good and ready at 7AM which I loved because I tend to wake up really early while on vacation. They also have a self serve alcohol bar with great brands of liquor, if you don't see a particular bottle you like you can ask and they more than likely have it and will bring it out for you. We spent our entire day on Friday at the royal service pool and beach area. Chairs on the beach were always available. With royal service you get two guaranteed bali beds by the pool during your stay which are pretty big, lucky for us we booked separate rooms so we got four, but couldn't use two since it rained Saturday and Sunday while we were there =( We were able to get one on our last day which was nice since many weren't already reserved. Service at the pool was prompt and amazing! Daniel and Rogelio were awesome and made sure we were always taken care of, lets not be cheap people TIPPING your server should come naturally and it gets you the best service, believe me we didn't have to want for anything and they remember you and make sure you are always satisfied. No complaints when it comes to service. The only down fall to this beautiful and absolutely amazing hotel is their food. We went to Naos, Bana, Vento, Blue Agave and Market Grill, the only one that I actually liked was Market Grill for lunch where we had pasta, steak and chicken it was all seasoned and grilled soo well ! Other than that everything was pretty bland so I stuck to fruits and veggies and room service which is open 24/7. I also didn't like their whole reservation system, if you show up and want to eat at a restaurant they will flat out tell you no even if you see about ten tables open for seating. We got lucky at Bana because my friend and I were very persistent and refused to leave until we got a table all for almost nothing because their sushi was just okay and tasted like the pre-made stuff at Giant, but their dumplings and chicken teriyaki roll were good. All in all this place was awesome and I am glad I researched all the resorts in the area before deciding on staying here and my friends were super happy and thankful about my choice, I highly recommend this resort and would not hesitate to stay here again! I actually want to stay at other Melia resorts after coming to this one. I WILL BE BACK, PARADISUS! Thank you for the amazing hospitality!


p.s. Don't listen to the reviews where they tell you RS is not needed, IT IS! Clearly, they haven't experienced the perks you receive with RS. You get extra perks that I know for a fact that regular guests do not receive. What's better than being treated like royalty and having everything you need and want in the building you are staying in? NOTHING!

(Would have rated at 5 stars, but took one off for the food.)

findings.title: Chris S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Terrible! Terrible! Terrible! Terrible! I cant even begin to explain how bad this company/resort  F&%@# ed  us! I never, ever write reviews for anything.  But for this experience I will make an exception. 
Had confirmation and booked room here for over a month. Had been called by Marin, who would be our concierge when arriving, and arranged pickup from airport. Two days before our arrival we were called and informed there was no availability at the resort and we would have to change hotels to their Melia Cancun property. I hate Cancun. Always have. Its for Spring Breakers. Its an entire different experience than Playa del Carmen.  Completely ruined out entire vacation as we had planned and paid for lots of local Playa Del Carmen activities such as Tulum tour, snorkeling, etc and it was mostly all non refundable. We had friends and family who were traveling to Playa del Carmen based on us being their whom we didn't see at all for our vacation. 

WORST EVER!. Them changing us to an entire different city cost us over $1000 extra. 
To make it worse, they said we would at least get an upgraded room such as Ocean View at Melia Cancun because of the "inconvenience". When we arrived and asked for it they said we could only have an ocean view for more money. I said, "are you kidding me". Nope, we got a view of "lagoon" and road out front. Our ride from the airport was a no show so we immediately spent $60 on a ride and all went downhill from there. I would avoid any Melia property like the plague.

findings.title: Steph C. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Really enjoyed our stay there.

We booked our trip through CheapCarribbean.com  6 night 7 days.all inclusive. about $1300pp (airfare direct flight with aeromexico included too)

when we first arrived the resort has a very herbal spa like smell... that is because they have these misters right when you walk in..  this really put you in a relaxing state.  we were then greeted by Paola who explained all the features of the hotel.  we were given a map/brochure.  our rooms were ready maybe about 15 minutes after we got there.  



Pros:
-Food is pretty good, 
t-he pools do not have an overwhelming chlorine smell!:
-Dancing everynight at 8:30 really talented
-rooms are clean, well stocked sometimes they came around again to see if you needed anything additional usually around 5/6 pm
-short walk to the beach
-wifi works pretty well
-ocean view front room we had was great!
-staff super friendly
-buffet at Naos has really great selection of foods
-Staff is always smiling/friendly, no cat calling (none that i heard)


Cons:
-Dont wear or avoid wearing white bathing suits in the pool especially the bar pool.. the amount of chlorine they have to put in there and piss from all the drunkies will turn it yellowish/light green
-the lights in the room do have a "main" shut off so if thats off nothing will turn on. 
-they do not announce when activities will be happening on the resort.
-they do not play music near the pool.
-they do offer cabanas but you have to rent it for the day about%50.. but if you get vouchers you can save $10.

OVERALL
i would return.

findings.title: John A. (3/5)
findings.snippet: This place could be so much better.  The food options are plentiful. If you're a foodie, you will want to pay for the food that isn't part of the 'all-inclusive' package. My primary reason for the low score is the quality of the room. The bathroom in our room had paint chips breaking away from the ceiling.  The plumbing fixtures in the bathroom all leaked.  The original room we had was supposed to be an ocean view room. Instead it was a view of all of the people coming and going from the first pyramid to the beach/pool area.

findings.title: Kru K. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I am absolutely in love with this resort!!!
To start with, it has awesome vegetarian options.

We took the all inclusive package as we just wanted to hang out at the resort and relax..

The resort has many restaurants but most are open only for dinner and you need to reserve.

Naos, market grill and sunset grill are open all day.
Noas has buffet all 3 meals... The dessert spread is awesome... They are so kind to actually make custom stuff for me as I am a vegetarian... Many many points for them... I had them make me veg empanadas... The juice station during breakfast is awesome :)

The resort is very very clean... Coco bar is awesome ... The swim up bar is too good :) You can order drinks anywhere in the whole resort... They even fill up the mini fridge in your room..... The service is simply fantastic..... I loved my stay here !!!

findings.title: Shanna J. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Fabulous experience, best travel of the year. It started with very cautious security guard, he kindly asked our room number and last name which made me feel very safe. After I entered, I was taken to a place to check-in. It was a little slow, but the server frequently brought us water which made the process not so long. We walked through the pyramid and found the decoration very fascinating, it's like walking in a luxurious jungle. 
The royal service area is extraordinary. The room is spacious and the service was very good. I especially like the royal lounge, where you can get snacks and drinks at anytime you want. Butler service is very sweet too, they will take you to walk around the hotel and they will also help you with check out, basically u don't need to do anything but walk out.
The food in buffet and some restaurant is super good, but some are very disappointing. Fugo, Bana and La palapa is very good but never ever go to mole!
The beach is beautiful and Bali bed is so comfy. Nothing to complain.

findings.title: Ellen S. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed a week back in July 2014 with 21 family members.  We had 5 rooms in the main tower, all on same hallway.  View was beautiful.  Everyone was so nice, waiters, bartenders, maids alike.  We really enjoyed our stay and really don't have any complaints.  Vento was the best add-on restaurant, and the best bartender was Luis Cortez at the swim up bar in the smaller pool.  I would definitely come here again.  Why not 5 stars?  They didn't have salmon at the breakfast buffet, but sometimes they would 'find' some if you asked.  But they should have it available for guests, not just those who ask.  Still I had a wonderful, relaxing time!

findings.title: Dan R. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
"Oh think twice, it's another day for you and me in paradise 
Oh think twice, 'cause it's just another day for you, 
You and me in paradise, think about it"

Another Day in Paradise -Phil Collins

Plusses

1- ALL INCLUSIVE RESORT -all food and drink!
2-The room is spacious, the beds are comfy, the wifi is terrific.
3-The bath towels are gigantic and as plush as a comforter
4-The showerhead is as large as a Thanksgiving turkey platter
5-The entire facility is aromatic - as if there are 15,000 hidden incense sticks
6-The restaurant choices are staggering
7- 99% of the hotel staff we interacted with was polite, courteous, and helpful
8-The Royal Service level is the way to go, at least it was for us. Adults only accomodations, no children allowed. Private beach, private pool, incredible lounge area with included food and drink all day, private check in. You even get a private butler to arrange all of your restaurant and excursion needs.
9. Our butler (Juan) was awesome. Basically he was our private concierge.
10. The fresh fruit is absolutely incredible. Puts to shame what we get at home.
11. They have tons of fun classes. We did a class on ceviche, mixology, guacamole, tequila tasting, and sushi sampling.
12. The Avenue Bar has "shows" every night for your entertainment pleasure.
13. The beach is beautiful, warm turquoise water and white sand.
14. The huge Royal Service pool is wonderful, but for variety you can choose two more pools  - there are three total.

Minuses

1.The hotel room water is not purified and the guest book tells you they "do not recommend its use"
2. There is a thick strip of unattractive seaweed between the end of the beach and the water line.
3. Amazingly, the pool-side beverage service was quite inferior to the beach-side beverage service.  A guy served the folks next to us, and walked right by us 2X as if we were invisible.
4. The towel and sun screen guys at the pool weren;t very friendly.
5. Probably because of its size and hundreds of employees, not every employee is familiar with the hotel activities. We went to a scheduled Mixology class, and the Maitre D' looked at us as if we were hallucinating or delusional. He asked the bartender if he knew what we were talking about, and he knew exactly what we meant and he took care of us.
6. Its very difficult to tell exactly who is a hotel employee and who is a time share/vacation club shill. They dress alike and are located in the same places.
7. The interaction between our room's ceramic tile floor and our desk chair created the most godawful squeak when you move the chair. Unless you carry earplugs, you'd better hoist the chair clear up off the floor to move it. Slide it at your auditory peril.
8. The procedure to sign up for the classes really needs to be overhauled. You get a printed slip for your dinner reservations, but no such printed confirmation exists for these classes. When we were at the tequila tasting, more people showed up than expected, but there was no real procedure in place to deal with that. We had our valet sign us up for today's sushi making class, but a dozen folks were there for a class that reportedly had 6 openings. There was a young guy from the hotel present at both classes and he seemed to take a sadistic glee in shutting the door on some folks who honestly felt they belonged there. We were asked "who signed up for the class, c'mon, be honest?". I thought that was demeaning and insulting. Printed slips to confirm reservations shouldn't be that hard to orchestrate.

findings.title: Brian B. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I gotta be honest here...after reading the reviews prior to coming, I had HIGH hopes for this place.  Last year I went to Live Aqua for a work function and was so blown away by how awesome that place was that I re-booked later in the year to go on personal time with the wife. So I was sure hoping this place would outdo them.  Sadly, we weren't even 24 hours in and my wife and I both felt that Live Aqua was way better.  I actually came for work to this place (I DJ for a living) and was working a corporate party.  The decor is pretty spectacular.  The place is HUGE!

The client graciously put us up in the "royal service" building (a $500 upgrade from what I hear). Again, I was excited after reading the reviews on that particular service. Outside of the fact that it is adult only in the RS, it sure seemed like much ado about nothing.  The butler service is essentially your own concierge. But unlike most concierges, this particular "butler" did nothing for us.  His name was Tony and although he was plenty friendly, he informed us that almost all of the restaurant reservations were taken for that day as well as the cabanas.  I understood that would be the case (we got in at 2PM).  So I said no biggie, how about getting us a cabana for the next day and the day after? He said the next day would be tough but the day after shouldn't be a problem.  Same thing with the restaurants.  So he ended up getting us a restaurant reservation at 9:30PM at La Perla for that evening.  Even though we're young, that was way too late for us.  So we took our chances and went around 7:30PM to see if we could get a walk-in seating.  There were TON of spaces and we got seated immediately.  I'll get to the food in a moment but this butler service was a joke.  He checked in one other time on us.  The reservation for the cabana (which we were hoping for on the 3rd day) never came through. Very disappointed in that.

The other thing about royal service is that you are in the furthest building away from anything you want to go to.  It took us a day or two to figure out how to get around (signage is virtually non-existent) and the floors don't all make sense.  We were in building 5 and floor 1 is really floor 2, whereas everywhere else floor 1 is floor 1.  Yes, it's great to be away from everything to a certain extent (quiet) but we wanted a little bit of a sense that something was going on.  The building did have it's own snack, bar  and breakfast area and although it was continental style, it was the best breakfast we had during the stay (again, kinda sad to say that).

The room was fine.  We had a decent view and nothing out of the ordinary impressive there EXCEPT that you could order special pillows based on density.  I actually thought that was pretty cool.  The fridge comes stocked (not too cold though) and anything you want out of that is free.

Now to the food. That was the weakest part of Live Aqua.   But even Live Aqua was better than this place overall.  The breakfast buffet was pretty weak and that's usually a meal you can bank on at an all-inclusive.  Things were cold, bacon was under cooked, and the options were below average.  We tried it twice thinking maybe they had an off day.  Nope, both days were about the same.  The last morning we opted for the royal service breakfast and minus the omelettes, they had just about everything else.  Way easier and decent food. 

We went to two restaurants during our stay (we were there only 3 days) so I realize I may have not tested them all and may have missed a great one.  Night 1 we went to La Perla (their steak and pasta place).  It was just OK.  Not amazing, not terrible.  The options were a little limiting but you definitely can get either steak or pasta.  The next night I had to work a private party and didn't eat dinner.  The 3rd night we went early to the Blue Agave, the taco bar. I hear the lines can be crazy for that place. I can see why!  That place is awesome.  Think of it like a taco truck.  The mini tacos are good (pork was our favorite) and the chicken quesadillas are small  enough that you're not overwhelmed and the flavor is amazing. We got in and were seated pretty quickly.

The pools were OK but no jacuzzi.  I wish the cabanas had foot massages like Live Aqua.  It wouldn't have mattered though because we couldn't get a cabana anyway (bitter, party of 1). The pools were heated which I appreciated but no swim to bar in the royal service side.  In fact only 1 of the 4 pools has a swim to bar. The pool service was pretty slow as far as drinks and things go. Definitely could use improvement there.  

Coming from the other reviews, I can't even imagine if I hadn't gone royal service what the experience would've been like.  I'm glad a client was paying for our room as I won't be back as a paying guest.  Too many other options. I'm headed to Cancun again for work in June at another resort.  Check back to see where that one ranked.

findings.title: Elly R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Hotel is located on a beautiful beach (that somewhat cluttered with a row of seaweed).

Everything is well organized, from check-in to check-out.  Someone meets you at the door, grabs your bags, walks you to the concierge for check-in.  They wait for you to finish your check-in (at which point if you didn't get the VIP service, the concierge will try and convince you to upgrade), and then flip though the hotel's brochures with you, showing you were to eat, where to swim, and most importantly (**sarcasm**) where to go for a time-share meeting.  The meeting will be mentioned multiple times throughout your stay, especially until you get a little bit of a tan to look like you've been there for a while and you have either already attended one or refused enough times to make a habit out of it.

The organization of the hotel will remind you of a prison.  When you drive in (car, shuttle bus, tour, etc), they will ask for the names/room numbers of everyone and document the number of people entering.  When you leave, they'll document who's leaving and who's going where.  You cannot help it if you're being driven, all drivers are very used to the well oiled practice and provide the information without any qualms.  If you try to leave the premises on foot without giving them your destination, they will stop you at the door and interrogate you until you either give up and tell them where you're going or they get tired of trying to run after you to stop you (they are not allowed to touch you, so just keep walking away).  Shudder to think you say you are leaving for a time-share lecture to a different hotel, I think they will tackle you to the ground, chain you and only release you when it's time to check-out.

The Expedia travel agents are very friendly, well organized, and run a mean transportation scheme.  Getting from point A to point B couldn't be easier.  If a driver's running late (rare), they'll call them to make sure they're on the way.  The excursions are pricey, but if you book two, they'll give you a discount.  They are not pushy at all, they'll make good recommendations based on what you ask them, and may provide some alternatives.

The food is good.  The buffet's menu does not change, but there is a large variety of different foods to choose from, so that you don't have to eat the same thing every day even though it is available.  The service is exceptional.  Waiters are friendly, chatty and really care.

The restaurants for dinner are good and provide different kinds of food.  Vento restaurant serves Spanish tapas, portions are very small, but very yummy, and you can order as many as you want.  Bana has sushi, not great, but good enough.  Market Grill turns into a Brazilian steak-house for dinner - meat is good, salads/appetizers are okay.  La Perla serves okay burgers for lunch and turns into a pool-side restaurant with an American menu for dinner.  And Naos is your to-go to place - that's the buffet that is open almost all hours and does't need a reservation. 

There is no jacuzzi, but the infinity pools are clean and warm.  The straw huts provide great protection from the sun and if you splurge and get a Cabana bed, you get fast personalized service all day and get to relax on a nice mattress.  People reserve lounge chairs very early in the morning by placing hotel's towels on them.  The good thing here is that no one steals your towel (which is common in most other hotels).  The pool bar provides nice refreshing drinks (which are slightly watered-down version, but it may be great if you drink non-stop, like people seem to do at all-inclusive resorts).  The entertainment by the pool is very limited.  There is pool side dancing/aerobics for half an hour and a 10 minute game of throwing a football.  The rest of the time just get your drinks refilled.

The gift shop isn't very large but it is overpriced - a can of sunscreen is $30 US.  If you forget something at home, the stay will be much pricier than originally expected.  They do not accept US dollars, but okay with credit cards.

The nightly entertainment is very sub-par.  Not only do they not have a formal stage and seats to accommodate the number of people that want to attend (shows take place in a bar/lounge on a dance floor in front of a few couches and tables, with more than half of the guests unable to see anything because their tables are on the wrong side of the DJ station), but the quality of the shows is very amateur.

The hotel provides free wifi, however, the signal is so weak that the only place where you are really able to use your device is by the check-in counter and certain "lucky" spots by the pool.  The signal is so week that even simply checking email becomes a hassle.

In general, the stay was good.  People are friendly and accommodating, the food is plentiful and different, the beach is clean and warm.  I would consider coming back here if they improve entertainment and relax about forcing guests to go to the time-share lecture

findings.title: Kayla S. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Absolutely love it here, the rooms are beautiful, the views are spectacular, the hotel is stunning, and I've gotta say the cabana boys are the nicest and incredibly helpful! Close to all attractions, and a great place to go with a special someone. The restaurants are delicious, and you can dress up every night. The pool always has a dj, and fun games going on. 

We have a time share here, so this wasn't my first time, but it was my birthday and they sent balloons, a card, and a cake to my room. I can't wait to go back!

findings.title: Kelly N. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
So we were here during the time of Thanksgiving, for 6 nights. Unfortunately, we hit some windy weather so the waters weren't calm at all. So we barely went outside the hotel, very rough waters and very windy. Inside, it's very nice. I enjoyed most of the entertainment. However, for the food, it was really not good. Maybe we had a few good dishes, but definitely fell way below the bar for a 4/5 star hotel. The sushi place, don't even go there, it was really really bad sushi we couldn't even eat it. The drinks were all poorly made as well, which really sucked. Sucks that there's no dance/club (there's a small one) but not much going on in that scene -- but I didn't expect it to be. The service was not that great either unfortunately. If I had to go again, i would not recommend paradisus. The hotel is very nice, but service and food was not good. Most of the food from the buffet was stale, it was just weird that they didn't have even just okay food at the resort.  We definitively weren't the only ones thinking this, we met a bunch of other folks who felt the same. Another horrible thing is that they didn't heat up the pool, so there was literally no one in it. The pool was heated however in royal service, and that's just unacceptable. There were a bunch of kids and they didn't get to enjoy water time (the waves out there were way too strong). Service was slow and sometimes there just wouldn't even be food or plates and utensils.. and selection of food was way too small, just didn't have all the perks you think would be basic for an all inclusive price of this resort. It kind of killed our trip staying here. :/

The only good thing is because our resort experience was so poor, we ventured out a lot and did a lot of excursions. It would have been nice to have the choice to just relax at your resort though.. which is a big part of your decision to vacay. :( We'll try another time at a different resort...

findings.title: Tanya S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is a fantastic resort! It is very hard to pick a hotel based on pics because so many are deceiving but the pics of this place are spot on. The hotel itself is beautiful, very upscale but still welcoming. There are restaurants, bars, a night club, shops and fitness center. You could come here and never leave the resort. There is only a buffet for lunch and dinner but the food was very good and a very good variety. We ate out at night so we didn't try the other restaurants but there are 5 open at night. The service was incredible, everyone was friendly and very helpful. We did tip throughout the day, 50 pesos here and there, although it's not required. The room was large, comfortable, and super clean. The beach is beautiful, very large and has a dj all day. This resort is perfect, especially for the price, you will not be disappointed!

findings.title: Chad J. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This place is amazing... review to continue.  Best advice, if you are having a little sexo in your room don't be too loud your neighbor will call call front desk and  complaint about the mating call. Then front desk will call and ask "is everything okay" then you yes.. then say " you are part of the royal service, you have special discounts come downstairs right now and let your neighbor sleep" then I said I was having sex and the she said it's okay are your going to any excursions?  And I said I was was "exploring new grounds" and she said okay I'll see you In a bit. Moral story is tell your chick to keep it down or bite the pillow. Did I mentioned complimentary aromatherapy pillows?  Get it get if!!

findings.title: Young-In L. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Might try out other resorts before coming back. Still, it was a great first all-inclusive resort experience in Cancun! 

Pros: 
- Service (everyone was so friendly)
- Private Cabanas (in Royal Service - which you need to get your butler to reserve for you in advance)
- Wifi (not bad at all, could watch Netflix seamlessly in our rooms, which btw, Netflix Mexico has waaaay newer shows and movies available than Netflix USA)
- Full body massage (downstairs at the spa - not available in all inclusive package)
- Ambience (really modern, chic, and different depending on each restaurant's theme)

Cons: 
- Food (even though it was all-inclusive, we barely ate)
- Alcoholic beverages (so weak)
- Elevator broke down for 2 out of the 3 days we were there (sis-in-law was pregnant so this was a problem -- however they let us use the service elevator)
- Royal Service area was quite far away from most of the restaurants, had to walk around a lot (bit rougher on my pregnant sis-in-law)

Overall, good experience, they just need to improve on their cuisine and alcoholic drinks, it wasn't worth the price of paying all-inclusive.

findings.title: Lily Z. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The boy's company rented out the entire hotel for a few days. Afterwards, we stayed at the Aloft. Comparing the two, I have to say that customer service was excellent at the Paradisus. Very friendly with drinks, cleanup or housekeeping. Loved the rain head shower. Plus, they are able to exchange money at the front desk!

I wasn't a fan of the food, however that may have been a logistical issue with the event planners and not the hotel itself. There was always a lot of food, but the quality and the variety wasn't very good. I lived off a diet of hot wings because everything else was bland or boring. I loved that we had our own private beach and an ocean-view room. I like the tropical theme in the heart of the hotel, but it made the hotel feel humid. When we were finally able to pick our own restaurant for Monday night's dinner, Tempo was amazing. Flawless customer service and a great tasting menu. Plus it was a nice haven compared to the outside electronic/techno music and restaurants. 

We will probably be back next year, so I'm looking forward to it! If you need to buy snacks or cigarettes, you're better off going across the street since it will be a lot cheaper.

findings.title: Sheila W. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful property but alot of walking. Must enter the beach from building 3 or Royal Service areas only. Consists of 5 buildings. If mobility impaired request bldg 3 in advance of arrival. Food is great too! Both European plan and All Inclusive available. Does use natural fiber wrist bands.

findings.title: Ron W. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed here for 6 nights recently and I was VERY pleased.  I will say this multiple times during this review, but make sure you book Royal Service!!  When you book you have option of Ocean view and Lagoon View and then below you will see Royal Service Ocean view and Royal Service Lagoon View.  It is up to you if you want to pay a little extra for Ocean view versus the Lagoon view...but do NOT skimp on the Royal Service.  This is a MUST!  A disclaimer here:  Royal Service is adults only, so if you are traveling with children, this option is not for you unfortunately.  This is an all-inclusive resort.

There are several restaurants on the property which I will review individually this week.  There are several souvenir shops, a convenience store, and a few clothing and jewelery shops here as well.  They have a wickedly expensive Spa, but not surprising as most resorts tend to charge arms and legs for that.  They also have 2 "front desks" which is very confusing.  There is one behind glass doors (which is the one you need to go to!) and one directly in the lobby that seems more appropriate but is staffed by vendors such as timeshare people and tour guides.  They dress the same in order to trick you to talk to them unfortunately.  Not the resort's fault, but you'd think the resort would try to shield their guests from this.  Oh well, not a huge deal.

OK, now for the two things people mostly care about, (besides the food which is reviewed separately) The beach, and the rooms.

(I will be reviewing Royal Service features only)
The Beach:  Beautiful.  You walk through the pool area which is adults only and private to royal service guests.  They have roughly 15 or 16 Bali beds which you can reserve when you arrive for your stay.  We had one each day, and they are beyond worth it.  The beach was white, and the water was an amazing blue color that was see through.  The waves were tame, yet big enough that you can body surf them every so often.  The water (even in December) was bath temperature and amazing.  Servers came by as often as they could (which was slow, but understandably so) to ask you if you want more pina coladas or my new favorite drink there called a BBC (which is basically Banana, Bailey, and Chambord blended together and topped with chocolate sauce)

The Rooms: We had a lagoon view because the view really didn't matter much to us.  Each room is a large suite with either 1 King or 2 Queens.  They can put the 2 Queens together with a special mattress to make it a super King and that is what we had....it was comical how large the bed was.  You have a couch with a coffee table, as well as a desk for a computer or late night card games.  Room service came back twice a day to make the room and turn down service with chocolates on the pillows and everything.  The minibar was complementary and was refilled every day.


Other high points was the Royal Service Foyer which had a Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner buffet always available with light snacks (don't think actual buffet, but more of appetizers)
The foyer also had a bar with top shelf alcohol in a self-serve type of setup.  You want 4 ounces of Tequila in your drink? go for it, no bartender here. :)

All in all, I would come back/recommend this place any day!

findings.title: Tiffany G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I've been to Cancún four times & this has been the best resort I've stayed at. I stayed in the Royal Service Suites & experienced nothing but flawless service. Although this is an all-inclusive resort, don't forget to toss people tips--it's mainly what they live off of. If you're looking to relax, smile, have fun, & just enjoy life, this is the place to go.

For a full, in-depth review of Paradisus Resort (Cancún), read my blog entry at http://humpsandpumps.com/post/104251734498/travel-review-paradisus-resort-in-cancun

findings.title: Cheryl G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My daughters (20 & 22 yrs) just returned from this lovely resort. I've been to Mexico six times, four times in Cancun and twice in Riviera Maya. We opted for the Royal Service at Paradisus Cancun and were so happy we did. Having the extra ammenities and superb service added to the perfection of this trip. We were well taken care of in the private concierge for the Royal Service Suites by Leticia and her supervisor Natalie. Our private butler, Hector was wonderful and was always available to answer questions and arrange things for us. We befriended a wonderful Server at our private pool named Francisco Terrazas. We liked Francisco so much that we asked for him exclusively each day. The last day he was assigned to the beach so we had Geraldo as a server, he also was very good. If I was returning I would absolutely request Francisco. His service MADE our vacation so wonderful. His humor, good attitude and his attention to detail was over the top. I urge anyone who does the Royal Service to request Francisco's section. We were sad to say goodbye to him. We had so much fun thanks to him!
As far as the restuarants, I thought they were all very good, service was excellent. The one exception was Vento, this was our least favorite. The server could not understand english well and totally messed up our orders. The food was mediocre at best. Since we went to all the other restaurants by this time we were so disappointed. We LOVED Bana, it was so delicious and the food was fresh and inviting. Our servers were wonderful. La Palapa, the Royal Service only restaurant by the pool was awesome for lunch and the cook there had no problem accommodating special requests! Lunch served each day to our bali bed was so good! The menu was perfect for eating pool/beachside. 
The drinks/liquor was all top shelf which I appreciated. The drinks that you received were perfectly made and actually had liquor in them unlike some other resorts I have been to.
My daughter is a blogger for an online magazine and also has her own website where she fully reviewed all the staff and property in detail. You can find her review on Paradisus Cancun by going to www.humpsandpumps.com, she was not paid by the resort to review their property.  We stayed there in November 2014.

findings.title: Martin N. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Not even one star...
Don't waist your vacation here, HORRIBLE FOOD, HORRIBLE SERVICE, they tell you "you have a concierge " BUT ALL THEY DO IS TRYING TO SELL THEIR STUFF TO YOU, they are no help....their mission is to get you to become a member, so you will pay extra to get the standard of service you already deserve! 
If you ever come here, avoid room 3129, it's above the resturant and it smells like food all DAY AND NIGHT...
The most decent food you can get is the breakfast from the buffet and all 6 days was the freaking same... The "restaurants" that are included with your service are warm up stations. All the food is pre made and its served at room temp! So on the last two days I had to be creative about my food and mix and match or go to McDonald's across the street or the 7eleven ....
At the end all I can say is "do more research and find somewhere else"

findings.title: Reda B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The service is atrocious; hospitality business ran by thugs... unless you want to be abused and insulted, be my guest and visit this hotel.
My pregnant wife and I stopped by this hotel after learning that some close friends were staying here (we were staying at the Riu Palace Peninsula and had an overall decent experience (Facilities among the best we have seen although lacking maintenance and ... service can be spotty based on tips). 
Back to the 1 star... we were 'escorted' out of the hotel by a staff member who decided to abuse us because we did not tip him for showing us to the reception area and asked us to get a room if we wanted to stay; point is we were just stopping to say hello to friends (who happened to be sleeping when we stopped by) and were already booked at a different hotel.. while walking through the hotel we realized it was a rather older spa feel like hotel, the only area of interest is the pool; the beach section is normal at best and the feel of the hotel was a bit creepy to my wife and I. 
Bottomline, if Mexico wants to say in the hospitality business, they will have to bring their game up by investing in training their personnel and taking corrective action against bad employees who may provide a bad image to their reputation.
We are travel addicts and have been to 12 European countries, 3 Asian countries, 2 Latin American countries, 18 States and a couple of African countries but can ascert that Mexico and more specifically, Cancun was by far the worst getaway I had personally experienced.
My wife will be writing a full blown article in regards to Cancun's positioning in the hospitality business shortly to be published in travel journals and research papers to follow.

findings.title: Robert B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We visited Paradisus recently for a little getaway. We stayed here before when it was the Gran Melia. We were greeted warmly by the staff and lead into their check in area which was comfortable and relaxing and away from the main lobby. We were then taken to our room by a nice, friendly young woman who took us to our room. Our room was ocean front and the view of the ocean was beautiful.
The food was wonderful and they offered many menu selections for breakfast, lunch and dinner. The waiters were all pleasant and excellent. We tipped them despite the 18% tip included in the package. This is not the place to go if you are on a diet - I guarantee you will gain weight with all of the great food and drinks. The outddoor staff were great too. Give them a daily tip for bringing you drinks as you bask in the sun and they will not forget you. They all work very hard too for their pay. 
Sergio the manager was top notch. My wife forgot her phone in our room and he sent it to us via UPS. He also listened to us one morning when a drunk guest from a large conference was trying to get into our room at 3:00 am.

Pros: Great food, Sergio the manager, the staff. The view and the pool. Sergio sending us our phone! 

Cons: the very large gathering of conference attendees who appeard to arrive already intoxicated. Many of them were kicked out of the hotel for their behavior. Being aroused from sleep at 3:00 am by a drunk stranger trying to enter your room (although security handled the situation well). Also, most importantly to me was the chef making pasta dishes the night we arrived who had a bad attitude like he didn't care to be at work or to have a job.

findings.title: Meybol C. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
This hotel is gorgeous! My bf who has traveled a lot and he has been to many hotels said "this is the best hotel I have ever been in. U did a good job selecting this one" Score!!!!! 
This hotel consists of 5 pyramids. Inside each pyramid, the center is decorated like a cenote! Green branches found down the center, small ponds with large fish inside and chairs and dim lighting.
The entire hotel smells like lavender which my bf loved.
The only thing is that during hurricane season, there are large groups from 900-2,000 arriving due to conferences like for pharmaceuticals and stuff. U might get pushed to another hotel if u arrive on a day when a large groups arrives, so I would call ahead to make sure ur rooms will be ready. I did not have this problem but the waiter did tell me that someone's wedding got moved to another melia hotel due to accommodating the large groups coming in.

This hotel is amazing. I highly recommend getting the "Royal service" which includes ur own butler. He gives u a cell phone and u can call him whenever u need anything. He will even go to the pharmacy to get u prescription meds if needed!!! It was awesome!
The hotel has about 8 restaurants and if u have a butler, he makes all of ur reservations and reserves ur Bali beds!! 
When I was out on the beach, people would pass by and see out nice hotel and say "wow, that is a really nice hotel"
U won't regret it!

findings.title: Alice B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: we are so disappointed in melia! we are getting married in two days at the paradissus cancun.  it's a shame that melia has chose to move our wedding guests instead of some convention people because they overbooked the resort. highly do not recommend this resort or other melia properties if this is how they treat there guests!

findings.title: Tara M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This is an all inclusive resort, which told us 18% tip was already included in the price. But, if you don't tip on top of that, no one will treat you nicely. We did tip but even then service was spotty at best. We went into the buffet at 9:30pm and it was not closed yet. We just wanted some dessert but when we asked for ice cream, which they get in the back, the waiter gave us a hated look and then flipped us off when walking away. Another waiter refused to serve us at 11:30 am and made us wait 30 minutes for a menu. We thought it was odd and then after the late breakfast we understood... It was our day of checkout and if you eat after noon, they charge you for it. We got a bill for $60. Went to the concierge and explained what happened. He was apologetic and did get our cash back. It was super shady!!! 
    We come here and it's beautiful, but some things are old...the pools, the paint, etc,... Food was ok, not great. Staff was not friendly or personable. Never a smile or hello. Room and view were nice and modern. 
I would not come here again just because of the staff. I will tip if service is good on top of the 18% paid up front, but in this case it was only warranted a few times during our stay.

findings.title: Cindy G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Sent us off to Paradisus Playa del Carmen when they did NOT have the ocean view room we paid for(Deluxe Ocean View Junior Suite - All Inclusive) with the promise of having an Ocean View Room there. Two hours later, were sitting in the lobby of paradisus Playa with no room and only thing available is garden view room. If we have to pay for an upgrade, why don't hotels pay when they downgrade ??? 

They wasted a day of our vacation that we spent in a lobby, traveling, then in a 2nd lobby waiting for pure disappointment. Really upset and don't want to come back to Paradisus if they can't do something as simple as give me what I paid for. It's not my fault they overbooked!

findings.title: Chuck C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Paradisus is an all-inclusive mega resort located on that beautiful stretch of beach in Mexico called Cancun, better known as heaven. When I say mega resort, don't get the wrong idea; it may be really (REALLY) big, but it is amazingly intimate once you get inside - Assuming you opt for the Royal Service, but we'll get to that in a bit. 

This was my first time at an all-inclusive, and to be honest I was a bit nervous about the whole idea. For me a fun vacation is picking a spot on a map (usually somewhere in Europe), hopping on a plane, and walking as many miles as my body can before my feet give out or I'm too buzzed to go on (looking at you Amsterdam). It's not that I don't like the beach, I totally do! But growing up down the Jersey Shore; I've done as much beach-bumming that I care too, now there's only so much lounging around I can take. This place had so much to offer, I knew that I could never possibly get bored. 

There's one big preface I have to mention before I really get into too many details of this place:YOU HAVE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ROYAL SERVICE. Seriously. I can understand why some people who visit this place have some mixed feelings about it, but I guarantee that anyone who's stayed in the Royal Service section will give it nothing but 5 stars. Here's why:

To begin the Royal Service has its own check in lobby. In this lobby you will find team of staff members who great you with a hot towel for your face, and, if you're so inclined, a bottle of champagne. Did I fail to mention that the booze in this place flows like water? OK well now that we have that straight, yes, you start with a bottle of champagne right off the bat. The staff will then happily whisk you away to your room located in Tower 5, the private (no one under 18 allowed) residence block. If you have planned ahead, you will have already asked for an ocean view room (a bit more, but 110% worth the price), on a high floor. Yes this place is shaped like a pyramid so you lose a bit of square footage the higher you go, but the views of the beach are so much more dramatic from the 7th floor as opposed to the 2nd or 3rd. If you have not opted for an ocean view, it doesn't really matter what floor you're on the view will be of the golf course and the main road - not bad but nothing like the ocean side.  The rooms are pretty standard, one bed (or two if you're just friends), basic cable that you won't be watching and a nice balcony to drink on and watch the waves break on the beach. The bathroom isn't bad; the showers have enough power to wash the sand and salt off, and there is a bidet which I found very European, and very funny as I have the same sense of humor as a child. There is a mini fridge in each room, STOCKED with FREE beer, snacks, and most importantly water. Water? That's the most important thing? Yes, you see everywhere you go in this resort people will be tripping over themselves to get you a drink, so when you wake up in the morning sunbaked and hung-over, the cold water in the fridge is a lifesaver. 

OK so you've found your room now what? Time to hit the beach! Remember earlier when I said that I wasn't a huge fan of lounging around on a beach etc etc? Well this beach has something that Jersey doesn't (unless your super rich), drink and food runners. This beach is SO much bigger than the neighboring hotels; the sheer size of it makes them look cheap by comparison. OH YEAH and you got the Royal Service right? So you have a private beach that the other people at the hotel can't come to (private pool and private outdoor bar as well), look at you go fancy man.  The rest of the day involves lying under a thatched roof, drinking beer / frozen (peach is the best) daiquiris, and listening to the waves hit the sand. If you do want to swim, the water is really clear and warm, but the rip tides can be very (VERY) strong, so be careful (especially after that third drink).

When you inevitably get hungry, the same guy who brings you drinks will bring you food. Here is what you get: the guacamole is to be had every day - it's that good. The burger isn't bad, but burgers as a rule are not great outside the states. If you like seafood person the shrimp tapas are pretty good too. I won't get too into the food of the resort in this review, but to sum it up in a few words, it's basically cruise ship food. I get why, they have 5000 guests. There's no way you're going to feed them all cheaply - this place was by no means overly expensive and so I'm not complaining. People eat a lot on vacation, all-inclusive resorts have overhead, its basic economics - the booze is free stop being so annoyed that the croissants are not fluffy enough. 

This resort is absolutely worth coming to, but again do yourself a favor at opt for the Royal Service (did I mention that yet). You won't be disappointed, as you'll find the biggest and best hotel in Cancun with an amazing staff that will take care of anything you could possibly want or need.

findings.title: Taylor C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My boyfriend and I went on our first vacation together and stayed at the Paradisus Cancun for 5 nights - all inclusive. The resort exceeded our expectations! We are a 26-year old couple and we couldn't ask for a better stay. 

Upon arrival, we were greeted with refreshing cold towels and a beautiful lobby/interior that reminded me of a rainforest. Check in was pretty simple - the staff was very friendly, however we had a slight issue with our reservation (due to Expedia, not the hotel) - this was later resolved. Our room was not ready, but the concierge offered to hold our bags and provide us with a changing room. We were totally fine with that and went straight to the beach! 

Upon getting to our room, everything was perfect. Large living space and balcony. We were in tower 3 however did not have any noise level issues. 

The beach - beautiful. We thought it would be hard to get a palapa every morning, but we never had an issue (we got one early in the morning, then also around lunch time, and were always able to get one). These were perfect to give us the mix of sun and shade. Waiters are very attentive and come regularly to get drink orders. Be sure to tip!

The food - absolutely amazing. We were so impressed and the all-inclusive deal was amazing. We enjoyed dinner at Vento, Bana (be sure to get sake bombs), Mole, and Fuego. At each of the restaurants, we literally ordered almost everything on the menu. We would order at least 2 apps each, 2 entrees and 2 desserts, and of course drinks! The wait staff was so friendly and kind, that we felt like royalty. We wanted to try Tempo, but it is not part of the all-inclusive deal (which was unknown to us). We ordered room service breakfast one morning - ordered everything off the menu again, and it was on-time and delicious. 

The biggest thing with the restaurants, which was kind of annoying, is that you NEED to make reservations. You can make them the day before for that night and the next. If you don't make a reservation, you will have to wait for a while, or will be out of luck. We did get lucky at times, though, but better to be safe than sorry!

The staff everywhere was the highest quality of professionalism and so nice! Customer service was great and fast too - we had a small issue with our room and they had us moved to another room in 5 minutes. 

During the day, we would go to Naos for the buffet - they have a great selection, including fresh made-to-order juices every morning. For lunch, we would also order from the Market Grill menu - loved their hearts of palm salad!

Every night, we would go to Cocoas on the beach to watch the sunset and have some drinks. Juan was amazing here! He would conjure up amazing and unique shots and drinks for us every night, to get us off to the right start. He was so sweet. Amazing view. 

They have entertainment at the Avenue Bar every night, we went a few times... it was okay. Entertaining! But lower-grade entertainment ;)

For activities, Jay Jay at the pool stand was super helpful. So friendly and enthusiastic, too! We talked for a long time about what we should do and we finally settled on Deep Sea Fishing & Snorkeling.  Both excursions were amazing. 

Deep Sea Fishing, we caught Sail Fish, a Marlin, Tuna and Trigger Fish! The best part about it, the team on the boat filleted them right in front of us and gave us the Tuna and Trigger. We brought them back to the hotel and met with Arcide (chef) at the Market Grill - he hooked us up and was amazing. He made our fish so fresh and in an hour's time, we had the most fresh, gourmet meal ever. Seriously, a trail of multiple chefs came to our table to present our fresh Trigger ceviche, seared tuna, grilled tuna and tuna tostada! They even saved the other half of our fish for the next night. That night, we sat at Bana and they brought us our cooked fish to that restaurant. This was the BEST part of our trip. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND - Thanks, Arcide!

For the snorkeling, it was great too! We saw barracudas, puffer fish, and a bunch of Sea Turtles that followed us around and swam right underneath us!
